1207 S. JOSEPHI HYMNOGRAPHI 1208 salve, 191 propitiatorium peccatorum; salve, quæ Deum incarnatum peperisti. O receptaculum lucis, quæ ex te pura digne Deo effulsit, illumina, o immaculatissima, oculos animæ meæ, atque ignorantiæ tenebras elimina, peccatique nebulas dejice, atque extermina. Ex Canone in festo S. Philippi apostoli, unius ex septem Diaconis, die 11. Qui ex iis quæ non sunt universa creavit, habuit te, o Dei Mater inviolata, tanquam incarnationis suæ causam; propterea fideles pro debito te beatam dicunt. Candelabrum mysticum facta es, o Puella, vere circumferens illam lampadem, quæ ob summam suam bonitatem eos illuminavit, qui ignorantiæ nocte ante detinebantur. Filios Dei esse fecit Filius tuus eos qui erant filii hominum, incarnatus ex castis sanguinibus tuis, et ex te natus, o immaculatissima: propterea te glorificamus. Nos, qui te vere Deiparam confitemur, a tentationibus, rebusque difficillimis eripimur intercessionibus tuis apud Deum ac Dominum omnium, o Virgo, divina gratia cumulatissima. Præter naturæ leges peperit te Mater tua sancta Conditorem naturæ, et supra naturam vere mansit virgo inviolata, o Christe omni bonitate superior. Virginem genitricem nominamus te, Maria, Sponsa Dei, nos qui per te singulis diebus ac noctibus, a noxia hostium violentia, ab omnigenis tentationibus, et ab animæ inquinamentis liberamur. Commotam hostis improbitate animam meam, firmam stabilemque redde, o Virgo casta, quæ illum sine 192 commotione suscepisti, qui divino aspectu commovet universa. Voces emittit ad te in gratiarum actionem, omne quod spirat, clamans cum lætitia, ac dicens: Salve, throne igniformis Altissimi; salve, Dei regio spatiosissima, salve, o casta, pulcherrima apostolorum corona. Ex Canone in festo SS. Probi, Tarachi, et Andronici, die 12. Verbum Patri sanctoque Spiritui coæternum D virginalem uterum sponte inhabitavit, et caro sine mutatione factum est; ac voluntarie passum, divinos martyrum exercitus ad certandum cum fide præparavit. Tanquam pulchram, tanquam speciosam, tanquam electam cum te Verbum elegisset, o inviolata, immaculatum ac Dei capacem uterum tuum sponte inhabitavit. Sola fers in utero Deum incarnatum, qui rebus omnibus esse dedit, quem divini martyres in stadio confitentes immobiliter decertanere, o Virgo Deipara, angelorum admiratio et dæmonum vulnus, omni laude dignissima. Superior supernis potestatibus facta es, o Virgo,


[1209] {#pg.105.1209}
κυήσασα τοῦ Πατρός, Παρθένε, τὸν συνάναρχον καὶ συναΐδιον, οὗ ταῖς φρυκτωρίαις οἱ ἀθληταὶ καταυγασθέντες ἀθεΐας τὴν νύκτα παρέδραμον. Συνέλαβες ἐν γαστρὶ τὸν προαιώνιον, ἄχραντε, καὶ τέτοκας ἐν σαρκὶ τὸν φύσει ἀπρόσιτον, καὶ γάλα ἐπότισας τὸν τροφέα πάντων, θεομῆτορ ἀπειρόγαμε. Κενοῦται ἐν μήτρᾳ σου Πατρώων κόλπων μὴ ἀφιστάμενος ὁ πληρέστατος Λόγος, καὶ σὰρξ ὁρᾶται, καὶ βρέφος τίκτεται, ᾧ μελῳδοῦμεν, Παρθένε, γηθόμενοι· Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς ὁ τῶν πατέρων. Σὺν ἀσωμάτων τάξεσι, σὺν μαρτύρων στρατεύμασι, σὺν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις καὶ προφήταις, ἅπαντες τὴν πάντων-δεσπόζουσαν τῶν ποιημάτων Δέσποιναν, ὡς τῶν Χερουβὶμ ἁγιωτέραν, καὶ μόνην θεοῦ ἁγνὴν Μητέρα εὐσεβῶς ἀνυμνοῦμεν, Χριστὸν ὑπερυψοῦντες εἰς πάντας τοὺς αἰῶνας. Φεῖσαί μου, Σῶτερ, ὁ τεχθείς, καὶ φυλάξας τὴν τεκοῦσαν σὲ ἄφθορον μετὰ τὴν κύησιν, ὅταν καθίσῃς κρῖναι τὰ ἔργα μου, τὰς ἀνομίας παρορῶν, καὶ τὰς ἁμαρτίας μου, ὡς ἀναμάρτητος, ἐλέημων ὁ Θεὸς καὶ φιλάνθρωπος. Ex Canone in SS. Carpum, et Popylum, die 13 (86*). O porta lucis, quæ ex incorruptis visceribus tuis effulsit, vibra in me illuminativos pœnitentiæ radios, et dissipa peccatorum meorum tenebras, o divina gratia plenissima. Cognovimus, Domine, quod cum Deus esses principio carens, principium habere sustinuisti, et ex Virgine absque mutatione procedere, quam etiam post partum incorruptam puramque conservasti. Thalamum Dei incontaminatum, montem a lapicidæ manibus immunem, arcam sanctam ac mensam, et carbonis immaterialis thuribulum omnes fideles te prædicamus, o casta Virgo, tota immaculata. Portum salutarem te, o Virgo, habentes nos qui assidue in gravissimorum malorum pelago jactamur, ad te confugimus, et in te sperantes, mala hostium consilia non formidamus. Concepisti absque virilis consortii experientia, Ἐκ τοῦ Κανόνος εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους μάρτυρας Ναζάριον, Γερβάσον, Προτάσιον καὶ Κέλσον, ἡμέρα ιδ´. Τὴν μόνην χωρήσασαν τὸν πρὸ αἰώνων Κύριον ἐν μήτρᾳ πανάμωμον κόρην ὑμνήσωμεν, ὅτι γέγονεν οὐρανῶν πλατυτέρα, θεὸν σωματώσασα δι᾿ ἀγαθότητα. Νόμου προετύπου σε ἡ σκηνὴ γενήσεσθαι μέλλουσαν, ἁγνή, θεοῦ ἅγιον σκήνωμα, ἐν ᾧ ὁ ἱλασμὸς ἡμῶν ἁγιασμὸν δωρούμενος πᾶσιν ἡμῖν ἐπελεύσεται. Μὴ κενώσας τοὺς Πατρώους ὁ ὑπέρθεος, ἄχραντε


[1210] {#pg.105.1210}
Verbum Patris enixa, eidem Patri coæternum, similiterque principio carens : cujus splendoribus athletæ irradiati, infidelitatis noctem percurrerunt. Concepisti in utero, o immaculata, eum qui est ante sæcula; peperisti in carne eum qui naturæ est inaccessibilis, lacte potasti eum qui nutrit universa, o Dei Mater nescia viri. Evacuatum est in utero tuo, o Virgo, non recdens a Paterno sinu, Verbum plenissimum, et caro apparuit, atque infans natum est : cui suaviter caninus lætabundi : Benedictus Deus patrum nostrorum. 193 Cum agminibus incorporeorum, cum martyrum exercitibus, eum apostolis ac prophetis, omnes religiose pieque collaudemus Dominatricem omnium, reginam rerum creatarum, tanquam Cherubim sanctiorem, et solam Dei matrem castissimam, Christum superexaltantes in omnia sæcula. Parce mihi, Salvator, qui natus es, et conservasti incorruptam post partum genitricem tuam, cum sederis ad judicanda opera mea; dissimulans iniquitates et peccata mea, tanquam impeccabilis, et Deus misericors, atque hominum amator. Deum incomprehensibilem, peperisti supra naturæ modum, plasmatorem naturæ. Magnum mysterium! inintelligibile 194 miraculum, o Virgo sola sine ulla macula (87). Ex luto passionum, ex barathro peccatorum educ, et rege me servum tuum semper confitentem te Deiparam. Tu enim semper eorum qui cadunt es erectio. Primæ matris nostræ Evæ maledictionem manifeste, o Virgo, solvisti. Sacer prophetarum divinorum chorus prædicat te, o purissima, futuram Matrem Dei, cui omnes clamamus : Benedicite, omnia, etc Fers in ulnis, o castissima, tanquam thronus Cherubicus, ferentem omnia, qui propter nos carne nostra circumdatus est, et cum esset simplex, duplex apparuit; quem tu semper precare pro nobis, laudantibus te. Ex Canone in festo SS. Nazari, Gervasi, Protasi, et Celsi mart., die 14. Laudemus immaculatissimam puellam, quæ sola in utero Dominum, qui est ante sæcula, comprehendit : facta est enim latior cœlis, Deum corpore vestiens propter ipsius bonitatem. Legale tabernaculum præfigurabat te futuram esse sanctum Dei tabernaculum, o casta, in quo superveniret propitiatio nostra, quæ nobis omnibus sanctificationem largiretur. Non relinquens vacuum Paternum sinum ille

Alexandrum VII extraordinario oratore, in suo Propugnaculo theologico pag. 286 et 287, ex divina maternitate praerogativam conceptionis sine peccato, in hunc modum deduco: « Licet dubitandum non sit de Virginis humilitate, magis velle Filium honorari, quam seipsam, et quod ipsa libentissime cederet huic honori, si non posset stare cum Filii praerogativa, et non cederet in majorem honorem Filii eam praeservare, tamen neque decenter comparatur Maria Agrippinae, neque Christus Neroni, qui vult magis honorari matrem, quam seipsum. Et quidem nonne crudelis fuit Nero occidendo matrem, quamvis ipsa dixerit: ‹Occidat ut imperet› cum imperase ipsa vivente? Ergo cum Christus imperium puritatis obtinere possit, imo multo magis imperium Redemptoris possideat praeservando Matrem, debuit illam praeservare, ne posset ab aliquo Arpalego Neroni comparari, nec multo magis de honore Matris quam de suo curaverit, ut inquit Ambrosius in illud Luc. ‹Et bene utrunque posuit Scriptura, ut et desponsata esset et virgo. Virgo, ut expers virilis consortii videretur: desponsata, ne temeratae virginitatis adureretur infamia, cui gravis alvus corruptelae videretur insigne proferre. Maluit autem Dominus aliquos de suo ortu, quam de Matris pudore, dubitare. Sciebat enim teneram esse virginis et lubricam famam pudoris, nec putavit ortus sui fidem, Matris injuriis astruendam. › Sic Ambrosius. Quomodo ergo putaret Christus imperii sui principatum, et redemptionis titulum, Matris labe et morte, esse astruendum?

Linguæ facundæ, ac disertæ non valent eloqui conceptionem tuam, quæ omnem superat loquelam; Deum enim in carne peperisti, o sanctissima, factum similem nobis propter bonitatem suam.
Ille qui purus est, cum te omni re creata puriorem invenisset, o castissima, inhabitavit in te, vo-
sistunt in indivisibili, quæ semel amissæ reparari non possunt, ex quibus est virginitas corporalis, quæ semel deperdita resarciri non potest, sive adhibito proprio consensu fuerit violata, sive violenter oppressa. Pari etiam ratione puritas, et virginalis candor spiritualis castimoniæ semel amissus recuperari non valet ultra. Sed hæc puritas, posttissimum mortalis, quod, secundum Scripturam sacram, est animæ spiritualis fornicatio, et Chrysostomus animæ derginationem appellat. Igitur anima semel per peccatum, quo separatur a Deo, corrupta, sive illud a propria voluntate descendat, sive ex generationis communis ac descensus ab Adamo, animæ impressum (nam quomodo id contingat nihil refert, ut paulo ante notavi de virginitate corporali), deinceps impollutæ titulo lætari nequibit. Itaque si B. Virgo in instanti suæ conceptionis fuit violata, et polluta spiritualiter per peccatum originale, nullo jure sibi vindicabit titulum impollutæ et incorruptæ.

τὴν ἐν Ἀδὰμ οἰκήσασαν, παρανομίαν ὡς φιλάνθρωπος. Ὑπάρχων ὁ Θεὸς τὸ πρὶν ἀόρατος ὡράθη, Παρθένε, δι᾿ εὐσπλαγχνίαν ἐκ γαστρός σου σωματούμενος. Διὰ τοῦτό σε πίστει μακαρίζομεν. Φορέσας με ἐκ τῶν σῶν θείων αἱμάτων ὁ Χριστός, ἄχραντε, καταστολὴν χάριτος πάλαι γυμνωθέντα ἐνέδυσεν. Νέον βρέφος ἀπεκύησας τὸν προόντα γεγηρακότα κόσμον νεουργοῦντα, Παρθένε, θείαις ἐπιγνώσεσι. Διό σε δοξάζομεν. Νόμοι ἐν σοὶ παραδόξως, Παρθένε, καινοτομοῦνται· τίκτεις γὰρ ἀσπόρως Θεὸν ὄντα, καὶ διαμένεις παρθενεύουσα πάλιν, ξένον θαῦμα· ὅθεν Μητέρα σε τοῦ Ἐμμανουὴλ εὐσεβῶς καταγγέλλομεν. Τὴν πώρωσιν, ἁγνή, τῆς ψυχῆς μου διάλυσον, καὶ δίδου μοι εὐαισθήτως τοῦ Υἱοῦ σου προσέχειν τοῖς θείοις ἐπιτάγμασιν. Διὰ σοῦ, παναγία θεόνυμφε, οἱ νενεκρωμένοι ζωῆς ἠξιώθημεν, καὶ τῇ φθορᾷ δουλεύοντες ἀφθαρσίαν σαφῶς ἐπλουτήσαμεν. Νέκρωσον τῆς σαρκός μου, Παρθένε, τὸ φρόνημα, ἢ τὴν ζωὴν τετοκυῖα, τὴν θανάτῳ θάνατον καθελοῦσαν, καὶ τοὺς παῖδας παραδόξῳ ἐγέρσει δοξάσασαν. Ἐτέχθη ἐκ σοῦ ὃν ἐγέννησε Πατὴρ πρὸ τῶν αἰώνων διτταῖς οὐσίαις καὶ θελήσεσιν, οἷα Θεὸς καὶ ἄνθρωπος, Κόρη, γνωριζόμενος πᾶσι, τοῖς ἐν πίστει κραυγάζουσιν, Εὐλογητὸς εἶ, ὁ Θεός, ὁ τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν. lens, tanquam hominum amator, eliminare iniquitatem, quæ habitaverat in Adan. Ille qui prius erat Deus invisibilis, factus est visibilis, corpore ex utero tuo accepto, o Virgo, propter misericordiam suam; propterea te cum fide beatam appellamus. 200 Christus, qui me ex divinis sanguinibus tuis acceptum tanquam vestem tulit, o inviolata, me eumdem, qui olim nudatus fueram, gratiæ stola vestivit. Contritionem et miseriam antiquam terrigenarum medela adhibita curasti, o tota immaculata, Dei sponsa, illum enixa, qui propter ineffabilem misericordiam suam infirmitates nostras portavit. Novum infantem peperisti, o Virgo, qui mundum ante senio confectum, divinis cognitionibus renovavit; ideo te glorificamus. Leges in te mirabiliter innovantur, o Virgo: etenim sine semine paris Denm Salvatorem, et virgo, qualis antea eras, perseveras. O peregrinum miraculum! Hac de causa te Matrem Emmanuelis religiose ac pie pronuntiamus. Dissolve, o casta, durissimum callum animæ meæ; et concede mihi, ut facili promptoque sensu divinis Filii tui mandatis attendam. Per te, o sanctissima Dei Sponsa, nos qui mortui eramus, vita digni facti sumus; et cum essenius corruptionis servi, incorruptionis divitias manifeste adepti sumus. Mortifica carnis meæ prudentiam, o Virgo, quæ C vitam peperisti, quæ morti mortem abstulit, et pueros admiranda excitatione glorificavit. Natus est ex te, o Puella, ille quem Pater genuit ante sæcula, qui in duabus substantiis ac voluntatibus agnoscitur (Deus scilicet et homo) ab omnibus, qui cum fide clamant: Benedictus es Deus patrum nostrorum. Apparuisti, o Dei genitrix, angelis superior; apparuisti vere athletarum robur; apparuisti, o castissima, salus eorum qui te verissimam Verbi genitricem recognoscunt. Ecce lectulus Salomonis, quem nunc potentes circumdat, Scripturæ scilicet, divinitus inspiratæ, prædictiones; in quo Christus Deus per divinam D incarnationem requievit, nimirum benedicta et gratia plena. Ægrotantem animam meam medica manu cura, o Virgo, 201 et inhærentes mibi affectionum sordes absterge, atque ad tribunal omnipotentis Dei siste me totum, salvum factum, ut cantem: Omnia opera, laudate Dominum. Lucernam illuminativam prævidit te olim propheta, o Virgo castissima, divinam lampadem in se ipsa vere ferentem; solum scilicet Deum supersubstantialem, qui propter viscera misericordiæ suæ ex te homo factus est. Gestas in ulnis eum, qui palma sua divina continet universa; quem suppliciter exora, o Virgo,

Ἱερὸς πάλαι προφήτης ὄρος σε θεῖον ἐκάλεσεν  ἀρετῆς, Παρθένε πάναγνε, δι᾿ ὅλου κατάσκιον, ἐξ οὗ σωτήριος Λόγος πεφανέρωται εἰς ἀνάπλασιν καὶ φωτισμὸν τῶν ψυχῶν ἡμῶν.
Ἀληθῶς Θεοῦ Υἱὸν ἐκύησας, ἁγνή, ὁμοούσιον τῷ Πατρὶ καὶ τῷ θείῳ Πνεύματι, Θεογεννήτρια, ὃν ἀπαύστως αἴτησαι, οἰκτειρῆσαι τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν.
Στόματι καὶ γλώσσῃ σε Μητέρα παναληθῶς, Παρθένε, τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν ὁμολογοῦμεν αὐτόν, ἁγνή, ἐκτενῶς ἱκέτευε, τοῦ σωθῆναι τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν.
Λελυτρωμένοι τῷ σῷ, Θεογεννῆτορ, τόκῳ τῆς αἰωνίου κατακρίσεως, τῷ, Χαῖρέ σοι, κράζομεν ἀεί, εὐλογημένη καὶ κεχαριτωμένη.
Νεκρωθέντας ἡμᾶς ἀνεζώωσας τὴν ζωὴν τῶν  ἀνάντων κυήσασα, Θεοκυῆτορ Δέσποινα, τῶν μαρτύρων δόξα, καὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὸ διάσωσμα καὶ περιτείχισμα.
Φωτὸς οἰκητήριον, ἁγνή, ὑπάρχουσα τῆς ψυχῆς μου κόρας φώτισον ἀμαυρωθείσας ἀμελείᾳ, καὶ σκότος ῥᾳθυμίας βαθύτατον ἀεὶ περικειμένας, πανάμωμε, ὅπως ἐν πίστει μακαρίζω σε.
Ἐκ τοῦ Κανόνος εἰς τὴν μνήμην τοῦ σεισμοῦ, ἡμέρᾳ κσ΄.
Ἱκετικῶς σοι βοῶμεν, Μῆτερ Θεοῦ, τὰ συνήθη σπλάγχνα σου ἐπὶ πόλιν καὶ λαὸν συμπαθῶς δεικνύουσα, σεισμοῦ βαρυτάτου καὶ φθορᾶς ἡμᾶς ἀπάλλαξον.  Ἡ μόνη οὖσα ἀγαθή· τὸν πανάγαθον Λόγον ἐκτενῶς ἐκδυσώπει τῆς ἀνάγκης τοῦ σεισμοῦ ῥυσθῆναι πάσης ὀργῆς, Θεοτόκε ἄχραντε, δεόμεθα.
Ναόν σε, Δέσποινα, Θεοῦ γινώσκοντες ἐν ἁγίῳ ναῷ σου χεῖρας οἰκτρὰς αἴρομεν εἰς δέησιν· ἴδε τὴν κάκωσιν ἡμῶν, καὶ παράσχου τὴν βοήθειαν.
Νῦν βοηθείας ἦλθε καιρός, νῦν καταλλαγῆς χρεία, ἁγνή, πρὸς τὸν Υἱόν σου καὶ Κύριον, ὅπως οἰκτειρήσῃ προσκεκρουκότας ἡμᾶς, καὶ τῆς ἐπικειμένης ὀργῆς λυτρώσηται.
Ἁγία Θεόνυμφε, ἀπορούμενον νυνὶ τὸν σὸν λαὸν οἰκτείρησον, καὶ μητρικαῖς πρεσβείαις τὴν καθ᾿


[1222] {#pg.105.1222}
ut me, qui unice damnatus sum, propter ineffabilem pietatem suam ulnis excipiat, et salvum faciat.
Ex Canone in festo S. Marciani et Martyrii martyrum, die 25.
Filium Dei æternum concipiens, o casta, corporasti hominem factum propter ineffabilem misericordiam suam. Unde illum adorantes, te devote glorificamus, quæ causa fuisti deificationis omnium.
Circumdata varietatibus in fimbriis aureis, tanquam Regina ac Domina, a dextris Dei ac Domini nunc astas, intercedens pro servis tuis.
Olim sacer propheta te divinum montem appellavit, o Virgo castissima, virtutibus undequaque umbrosum; ex quo salutare Verbum manifestatum est in restaurationem, et illuminationem animarum nostrarum.
Vere, o casta Dei genitrix, Filium Dei genuisti, Patri ac Spiritui divino consubstantialem; quem incessanter precare, ut misereatur animarum nostrarum.
Ore et lingua te verissimam Dei nostri Matrem confitemur, o Virgo: eumdem impense deprecare, o casta, pro salute animarum nostrarum.
Ab æterna damnatione per partum tuum liberati, o Dei genitrix, ad te semper clamamus: Ave, benedicta, et gratia plena.
Nos mortuos ad vitam revocasti, vitam omnium enixa, o Dei genitrix Domina, martyrum gloria, et hominum salus ac munimentum.
Lucis habitaculum cum sis, o casta, animæ meæ pupillas illumina, incuria obscuratas, et tenebras profundissimas negligentiæ, quibus semper involutus sum, ut te cum fide beatificem, o purissima.
Ex Canone in memoria cujusdam terræ motus, die 26.
Suppliciter ad te clamamus, Dei Mater, ut consuetæ misericordiæ tuæ viscera super hanc civitatem populumque demonstrans, a gravissimo terræ motu et interitu nos liberes.
Tu quæ sola bona es, optimum Verbum enixe deprecare, ut a necessitatibus, terræmotibus, atque ab universa ira liberemur, te oramus, o Deipara inviolata.
Te Dei templum agnoscentes, Domina, in templo sancto tuo manus miserandas extollimus supplicantes: vide afflictionem nostram, et præbe nobis auxilium.
Nunc venit tempus opportunum auxilii, o casta; nunc opus est reconciliatione cum Filio tuo ac Domino, ut nostri, qui terrore perculsi sumus, misereatur, et ab ira imminente liberet nos.
Sancta sponsa Dei, miserere nunc populi tui in angustia positi; et maternis intercessionibus in-


[1223] {#pg.105.1223}
ἡμῶν Θεοῦ ἀγανάκτησιν μεταποίησον τάχος, δυσπωοῦμέν σε. Νεῦσον, ἄχραντε, σωθῆναι τοὺς οἰκέτας σου ἀπολεσθῆναι μέλλοντας· ἐν ὀργῇ Θεοῦ, καὶ θυμῷ μεγάλῳ καὶ φρικτῷ τῆς νῦν ἐπελθούσης ἀπειλῆς διὰ τὸ πλῆθος τῶν πολλῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν. Συμπαθὴς Θεοτόκε, τὸν ἀσυμπάθητον ἡ τεκοῦσα Σωτῆρα, ἴδε τὴν κάκωσιν καὶ τὸν στεναγμὸν λαοῦ σου, καὶ τάχυνον τοῦ παρακαλέσαι ἡμᾶς· οἰκτειρηθῆναι. Φθορὰν τῷ τίκτειν μὴ ὑπομείνασα, πάσης φθορᾶς, Παρθένε, ἐξελοῦ ἡμᾶς ἅπαντας, καὶ σεισμοῦ βαρυτάτου καὶ θλίψεως, παύουσα τοῦ Δεσπότου τὴν ἀγανάκτησιν ταῖς σαῖς μητρικαῖς καταλλαγαῖς, Θεοχαριτωτε. σæculi cruciatibus mihi paratis libera me, o illibatissima. Habentes te, o Virgo inviolata, præsidium ac murum, et portum, a noxiis tentationibus variisque tribulationibus, precibus tuis eripiamur, dum te pro merito laudamus. Pro iis qui te Virginem Matrem agnoscunt, legatione 204 fungere, o benedicta, ut a tentationibus ingruentibus, a serpentis jaculis, atque a sempiternis suppliciis, o Virgo, liberentur. Bonorum amica Virgo, quæ Deum Verbum undequaque bonum peperisti, animam meam peccatorum gravissimo pondere male affectam, precibus tuis bonam effice, ut ea exsequi possit quæ conducunt ad vitam; et ea fugere quæ ad malitiæ mortem deferunt; et ego te cum fide beatam dicam. Ἐκ τοῦ Κανόνος εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν μεγαλομάρτυρα Ἀναστασίαν τὴν Ῥωμαίαν, καὶ τὸν ὅσιον Πατέρα ἡμῶν Ἀβράμιον, ἡμέρᾳ κθ´. Σὲ τὴν οὐρανομήκη κλίμακα, ἐν ᾗ Θεὸς ἐπεστήρικτο τοὺς βροτοὺς οὐρανίους ἐργαζόμενος, Κόρη, γεραίρομεν. Σαρκὸς ἐξ αἱμάτων σου ἱερῶν Θεοῦ Πατρὸς Λόγος ἐσαρκώθη ὑπερφυῶς, Παρθένε Μαρία, ὃν δυσώπει τὰ τῆς σαρκός μου νεκρῶσαι φρονήματα. Ὕλην ἁμαρτίας μου σῶν πρεσβειῶν πυρὶ σύμφλεξον, Μῆτερ Θεοῦ, δρόσον μοι τὴν θείαν τῆς ἀφέσεως φέρουσα. Ἐπὶ σοί, παναγία, ὁ τοῦ παντὸς αἴτιος δι' ὑπερβολὴν εὐσπλαγχνίας θέλων ἐσκήνωσε, καὶ καθηγίασε τὴν τῶν ἀνθρώπων οὐσίαν, παραβάσει πρότερον ἐξολισθήσασαν. Μετὰ τόκον διέμεινας ἄφθορος, Παρθένε, ὡς πρὸ γεννήσεως· νέον βρέφος γὰρ ἐκύησας τὸν πρὸ αἰώνων γνωριζόμενον. Ῥαθυμίᾳ κρατούμενον καὶ τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ με βυθε-
dignationem Dei contra nos cito, te rogamus, a averte. Annue, o inviolata, saluti famulorum tuorum, qui exitio propinqui sunt ob iram Dei, gravemque atque horribilem furorem minarum nunc ingruentium, propter multitudinem multorum peccatorum nostrorum. 203 O Domina compassione prædita, quæ Salvatorem summe compassivum peperisti; vide afflictionem et gemitum populi tui, et accelera ab intercedendum, ut misereatur nostri. Tu quæ corruptionem in partu non sustinuisti, crue nos omnes, o Virgo, ab omni corruptione, gravissimoque terræ motu, ac tribulatione, placans indignationem Domini maternis reconciliationibus tuis, o Deo charissima. Ex Canone in S. Demetrium, die 26 (92*). Assiduas ad Deum preces effunde, o Puella, ut misereatur mei, qui plurimis hujus vitæ fraudibus detineor, et peccati cæca nocte involutus sum. Domina Deo gratissima, tu, quæ Solem peperisti, tenebrosa animæ meæ nubila undequaque dissipa ac dispelle. Mater Virgo, quæ Deum corporasti, a corporeis passionibus libera me, et medere omnibus contritionibus animæ meæ. Speciosa facta es, o Virgo, quippe quæ speciosissimum Verbum genuisti; quod assiduis precibus exora, ut peccantis populi misereatur, et mundum, qui sperat in te, o Deipara, ab omni dæmoniaca fraude salvum faciat. Supplicationem miserabilis animæ meæ ne despicias, Virgo Deipara : sed benigna interventione tua me omnium Deo domesticum redde, et a futuri Ex Canone duplici in festo S. Anastasiae Romanae Martyris, et S. P. N. Abrahamii, die 29. Te scalam illam, quæ ad cœlum pertingebat, et in qua Deus innitebatur, homines reddens cœlestes, o Puella, veneramur. Dei Patris Verbum ex sacris sanguinibus carnis tuæ supra naturæ rationem incarnatum est, o Virgo Maria : quod deprecare, ut carnis meæ sensus interimat. Peccatorum meorum sylvam intercessionum tuarum igne combure, o Dei Mater, divinum mihi remissionis rorem afferendo. In te, o sanctissima, universi auctor ob excessum misericordiæ suæ voluntarie habitavit, hominumque substantiam sanctificavit, quæ prius ob transgressionem ruinam subierat. Post partum, Virgo, inviolata permansisti, quemadmodum fueras ante partum; novum quippe infantem genuisti, qui ante sæcula fuisse cognoscitur. Me socordia oppressum, et in peccato demersum,


[1225] {#pg.105.1225}
ζόμενον τῇ πρεσβείᾳ σου με λύτρωσαι, Θεοτόκε, Μῆτερ ἀειπάρθενε. Ὑμνοῦμέν σε, πανύμνητε Δέσποινα Θεοτόκε, Θεὸν ὑπερύμνητον σαρκὶ ἀσπόρως κυήσασαν. Μητροπάρθενε κόρη, θείῳ φωτιζόμενοι Πνεύματι, πάναγνε, ἱεροὶ προφῆται ἱεραῖς ἐν φωναῖς σε προήγγειλαν, ἐξ ἧς Θεὸς Λόγος ὑπὲρ αἰτίαν τε καὶ λόγον ἐσαρκώθη δι᾿ οἶκτον ἀμέτρητον. Φιλάνθρωπον κυήσασα Θεόν, φιλάγαθε Δέσποινα, αὐτὸν καθικέτευε τῆς γεέννης τοῦ πυρὸς λυτρωθῆναί με. Βαρούμενον νυσταγμῷ ῥαθυμίας διανάστησον τῇ σῇ μεσιτείᾳ, Μῆτερ Θεοῦ, καὶ μὴ δῴης ὑπνῶσαι τῆς ἁμαρτίας, Παρθένε, εἰς θάνατον· προστάτην  γὰρ καὶ ὁδηγὸν τῆς ἐμῆς σε ζωῆς ἐπιγράφομαι. Ὅλον τὸν ἄνθρωπον φορέσας ὁ ὑπέρθεος δίχα τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἐκ γαστρός σου, ἁγνή, προῆλθε σαρκοφόρος, ὃν ἐκδυσώπει πίστει σε τοὺς τιμῶντας διασῶσαι. Μόνη τὸν ἕνα τῆς Τριάδος ἀπεγέννησας ἐν διτταῖς οὐσίαις ὑποστάσει μιᾷ ὁρώμενον, Παρθένε, ᾧ μελῳδοῦμεν, πάναγνε, ἀσιγήτως εἰς αἰῶνας. Σὲ τὴν ἁγνὴν καὶ ἄμωμον ἡ παρθένος (Ἀναστασία) ποθήσασα, ἄμωμον καὶ σῶμα καὶ ψυχὴν ἐτήρησεν, παθῶν ὑπεκκαύματα ὑπομονῇ τεφρώσασα, πεῖράν τε πολλῶν ὑπενεγκοῦσα βασάνων, καὶ νῦν ἐπουρανίοις ἐν θαλάμοις χορεύει, σὺν σοὶ εὐφραινομένη εἰς πάντας τοὺς αἰῶνας. Ῥείθρου ζῶντος ὤφθης πανάγιον σκήνωμα, ἐξ οὗ πιόντες οἱ θανατωθέντες τὴν ζωὴν κληρούμεθα, ἀναβοῶντες· Εὐλογεῖτε, πάντα τὰ ἔργα, τὸν Κύριον. Φορέσαντά σε σάρκα ἐκ γυναικὸς ὡς ἐπέγνω ἡ μάρτυς σου, Κύριε, παρθενικαῖς κατηγλαϊσμένη μαρμαρυγαῖς, καὶ μαρτυρίου αἵματι περινθισμένη, σοὶ τῷ Χριστῷ ὀπίσω τῆς Μητέρος σου ἐνδόξως προσηνέχθη, ὡς βασιλεύοντι τῆς κτίσεως. Φιλάγαθε Παρθένε, τὴν κεκακωμένην τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ψυχήν μου ἀγάθυνον καὶ ἀγαθῶν αἰωνίων μέτοχον ποίησον. Ἐκ τοῦ Κανόνος εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους μάρτυρας Ζηνόβιον καὶ Ζηνοβίαν τὴν ἀδελφὴν αὐτοῦ, ἡμέρᾳ λ΄. Χαίροις, ὁ πανάγιος ναός, ὁ ποκος ὁ θεόδροσος, ἐσφραγισμένη πηγὴ τοῦ ἀθανάτου ῥείθρου, τὴν ποίμνην σου, Δέσποινα, φύλαττε ἐκ παντοίων πολεμίων ἀπολιορκήτως. Τριάδος τὸν ἕνα ἀπεκύησας τὸ ἀνθρώπινον φορέσαντα, παναγία Μητροπάρθενε, ὃν αἴτησαι σωθῆναι τούς σε ἀνυμνοῦντας. Τῷ ξένῳ σου τόκῳ τοὺς ἐκ Θεοῦ ξενιτεύσαντας ἐν αὐτῷ οἰκειώσας, πανύμνητε, ὅθεν σε μεγαλοφρόνως πίστει δοξάζομεν, καὶ κραυγάζομεν· Χαῖρε, πάντων γηγενῶν τὸ διάσωσμα.
PATROL. GR. CV.

intercessione tua redime, o Deipara, Mater Virgo perpetua. Laudamus te, o omni laude dignissima Domina Deipara 205, quæ Deum superiorem omni laude in carne sine semine genuisti. Mater Virgo puella castissima, prophetæ sacri, divini Spiritus lumine illustrati, sacris vocibus te prænuntiaverunt, ex qua Deus Verbum, supra causam ac verbum incarnatus est propter immensam misericordiam suam. O Domina bonorum amatrix, quæ amatorem hominum Deum peperisti, eumdem deprecare, ut liberet me a gehenna ignis. Me dormitatione negligentiæ gravatum, exsuscita mediatione tua, Mater Dei, neque sinas me in mor- tem peccati obdormire : te enim patronam ac ducem vitæ meæ vendico, o Virgo. Superdivinus ille qui totum hominem tanquam vestem portavit, citra peccatum, ex utero tuo incarnatus prodivit, o casta; quem deprecare pro salute eorum, qui te fideliter honorant. Sola unum Trinitatis peperisti in duabus substantiis, unaque hypostasi conspicuum, o Virgo castissima : cui suaviter concinimus sine intermissione, in sæcula. Te castam et immaculatam, virgo (Anastasia) amore prosequens, corpus et animam sine macula conservavit; passionum incendia patientia despiciens, multorumque tormentorum experimentum perferens : et nunc in cœlestibus thalamis tripudiat tecum gaudens in omnia sæcula. Fluenti viventis sanctissimum tabernaculum facta es; ex quo bibentes nos qui mortui eramus, vitam hæreditamus, clamantes : Benedicite, omnia opera, Dominum. Statim atque martyr tua (Anastasia) cognovit te, Domine, carnem ex muliere acceptam gestasse, virginalibus radiis illustrata, et martyris sanguine tanquam floribus exornata, tibi Christo tanquam creaturarum regi, post Matrem tuam gloriose adducta est. O Virgo bonorum amatrix, animam meam peccatorum 206 malis vitiatam, bonam redde, ac bonorum æternorum participem effice. Ex Canone in festo SS. Zenobii et Zenobiæ sororis ejus mart., die 30. Salve, o templum sanctissimum; o vellus divino rore perfusum, o fons signatus immortalis fluenti : custodi, Domina, gregem tuum, ita ut a nullis hostibus expugnetur. Unum Trinitatis peperisti, o sanctissima Mater Virgo, humana natura indutum; quem deprecare pro salute laudantium te. Partu tuo peregrino eos, qui a Deo peregrini facti erant, eidem domesticos reddidisti, o omni laude dignissima. Unde te magna voce cum fide glorificamus, clamantes : Salve, o omnium terrigenarum salus.

Ἀμαρτίας βαρεῖα πάντοτε περίκειμαι φορτία, ἄχραντε, καὶ βοῶ σοι, τούτων μεσιτείᾳ με ἐλάφρυνον σὺ γὰρ εἶ προστάτις ἁμαρτωλῶν δεδοξασμένη, λυτρωτὴν καὶ Σωτῆρα κυήσασα.
Ὡραῖωσον τὴν ψυχήν μου, Παρθένε, ἀμορφίᾳ τῶν παθῶν κρατουμένην, καὶ λογισμοῖς ἀληθοῦς μετανοίας τὴν ταπεινήν μου καρδίαν ὀχύρωσον, καὶ σῶσόν με τὸν ἐπὶ σοὶ ἀδιστάκτως, ἁγνή, καταφεύγοντα.
Τόπος, Παρθένε, ἀνεδείχθης ἁγιάσματος, ἐξ οὗ Θεὸς ἐφάνη, ἁγιάζων ἡμᾶς τοὺς πίστει μελῳδοῦντας· Εὐλογημένος, πάναγνε ὁ καρπὸς τῆς σῆς κοιλίας.
Τὸν ἀγεώργητον βότρυν συλλαβοῦσα, ἀναπηγάζοντα οἶνον, Παρθενομῆτορ, ἀφέσεως, τῶν παθῶν με τῆς μέθης ἀπάλλαξον, δέομαι.
Φώτισον, πύλη τοῦ φωτός, τῆς καρδίας μου τὰ ὄμματα, δέομαι, μακρὰν ἐλαύνουσα τῆς ἁμαρτίας σκότος βαθύτατον ἐκ τῆς ἀθλίας μου ψυχῆς, ἵνα μεγαλύνω σε, ἵνα πόθῳ σε ὑμνῶ τὴν πανύμνητον.
Ἐκ τοῦ Κανόνος εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους ἀποστόλους Στάχυν, Ἀμπλίαν, Οὐρβανόν, Ἀριστόβολον, Νάρκισσον, καὶ τὸν ἅγιον μάρτυρα Ἐπίμαχον, ἡμέρᾳ λα΄.
Τὸ περιφανὲς ὄρος Θεοῦ, τὴν κιβωτὸν τὴν ἁγίαν, καὶ τράπεζαν, στάμνον τε πάγχρυσον, τὸ καθαρὸν τοῦ Κυρίου παλάτιον, τὴν εὐλογημένην ἐν γυναιξὶ μακαρίσωμεν.
Ἄσομαί σοι, Κύριε ὁ Θεός μου, ὅτι ἀσπόρως ἐκ γαστρὸς Παρθένου ἐτέχθης, δι’ ἧς καὶ σῴζεις ἅπαντας, ὡς μόνος πολυέλεος.
Παστὰς Χριστοῦ φωτοφόρος, καὶ θρόνος ὑψηλότατος, θεογεννῆτορ, ὤφθης, πανάμωμε· ἐν σοὶ γὰρ μόνος ἀναπαυσάμενος τοὺς ἡμῶν ἀφείλατο κόπους, καὶ τὴν μέλλουσαν τοῖς ἀξίοις ηὐτρέπισεν ἄνεσιν
Χαίροις, Μῆτερ ἀπειρόγαμε, ἡ Θεὸν Λόγον ἐν γαστρί σου χωρήσασα, καὶ τεκοῦσα σεσαρκωμένον, ὡς Θεὸν ὁμοῦ καὶ ἄνθρωπον.
Ὁράθης ἀγγέλων ὑπέρεχουσα, Δέσποινα· τὸν γὰρ ἐκείνοις φοβερὸν ἀνερμηνεύτως ἐν γαστρὶ χωρῆσαι ἠξίωσαι, καὶ ἐν χερσὶ βαστάσαι καθάπερ νήπιον τὸν ἡμερῶν τε καὶ χρόνων ἐπέκεινα.
Χαῖρε, Θεοτόκε ἀνύμφευτε, χερουβικῶν ταγμάτων ὑπερέχουσα, καὶ Θεὸν ἐν ἀγκάλαις ἐποχούμενον μετὰ σαρκὸς βαστάσασα.
Συνέλαβες ὑπὲρ λόγον τὸν Λόγον, καὶ ἔτεκες, πανύμνητε, ὃν Πατὴρ ἐκ γαστρὸς ἀπεγέννησε πρὸ αἰώνων, ἄχραντε· ὅθεν ὡς τούτου σε Μητέρα χρεωστικῶς μακαρίζομεν.
Τίς ἐξειπεῖν δυνήσεται τοῦ τόκου σου, ἁγνή, τὸν

Clamo ad te, o Virgo, emunda ab omni sorde A animam meam, et salvum fac me, o casta, quæ Salvatorein Deum verum in terra corporasti. Rubus te ante præfigurabat, o omni laude dignissima, et castissima, dum ardebat et non comburebatur : etenim tu similiter non es combusta, quamvis Deus ex te incarnatas fuerit. Providentiam tuam admirabilem hymnis collaudamus. Jam stella exorta est ex tribu Juda, quam cum agnovissent reges, ex Oriente advenerunt accelerantes iter, 241 ut viderent Christum natum in Bethleem secundum carnem. Quomodo, o Verbum, suscipiet te spelunca angustissima ac vilissima, natum in carne? Quomodo fasciis involveris, tu qui nubibus circumdas populum? Quomodo tanquam infans in brutorum stabulo reclinareris? O Edem olim mihi clausa, aperire in posterum, videns Christum infantem incarnatum, et in civitate Bethleem, quemadmodum illi placitum fuit, ex puella Virgine natum. In spelunca Bethleem puella manifeste parit Deum factorem universi, et tanquam hominem fasciis involutum, reclinat nunc in præsepio. Aurem præbeamus sermonibus sacris; Dominus nascitur puer propter nos, cujus principatus factus D est super humerum ejus, et vocatur Angelus magni consilii Patris, princeps pacis Christus. Sicut juravit Dominus, ecce complevit jusjurandum, dans nobis ex semine David Virginem matrem suam, ex qua natus est infans secundum carnem in civitate Bethleem, supra omnem conceptum verborum. Virgo, alabastrum spiritale, fert Christum unguentum inexhaustum, quod in spelunca Bethleem egreditur ut in spiritu manifeste evacuet, ut suavitate odoris sui repleat animas nostras. Οὗτος μόνος ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, ὁ ἐκ σοῦ, Παρθένε, σάρκα ὑπὲρ λόγον ἀληθῶς φορέσας, τεχθῆναι ἐν σπηλαίῳ ἐπείγεται, ὅπως, οἶκον γενόμενον λῃστῶν, δείξῃ ναὸν τοῦ θείου Πνεύματος. Ἀπειρόγαμε Κόρη, τὸν τῇ χειρὶ φέροντα ἅπασαν τὴν κτίσιν, ἐν μήτρᾳ φέρεις σαρκούμενον, ὃν καὶ τικτόμενον ἀνακλινεῖς ἐν φάτνῃ βρέφος καθορῶμενον τὸν προαιώνιον. Ῥήσεις ἤδη πεπλήρωνται τῶν προφητευόντων ἐν θείῳ Πνεύματι· ἡ Παρθένος γὰρ ἐπείγεται ἐν σπηλαίῳ τίκτειν τὸν παντέλειον. Σαρκοφόρος προέρχεται ἐκ σῆς φωτεφόρου νηδύος, ἄχραντε, Βασιλεὺς ὁ ἐπουράνιος, ὡς ἐν θρόνῳ φάτνῃ προσκλινόμενος. Νῦν ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ ἴδια, ἐν ξένῳ τοκετῷ Λόγος τοῦ Πατρὸς σωματούμενος ἐκ τῆς Παρθένου, καὶ ὡς νήπιον ὁρᾶται ἐν σπηλαίῳ δι᾿ ἄκραν εὐσπλαγχνίαν.

spelunca; qui ex ipsa secundum ineffabilem hypostasin, carnem, tanquam vestem supra naturæ modum, accepit, ut deificaret genus humanum. Ut homines liberaret, Deus ille piissimus ex Virgine casta 242 nascitur in Bethlehem, et tanquam infans recipit fascias. Cum Deipara virginitatem suam post partum sigillatam videret, stupore correpta, clamabat: O Fili, quomodo nunc fasciis te involvam, qui tanquam fasciis, arenis mare circumdas? O novum miraculum! Virgo inviolata festinat parere in spelunca Bethleemitica Deum hominem factum. Qui nutu voluntatis suæ mare, tanquam fascia, nebula circumdat, cum sit Creator, nascitur ex Virgine puella, et fascias tanquam infans recipit, ut redimat mundum. Salve, o Virgo Mater, receptaculum illius, quem nihil capere potest. Hunc tu, o inviolata, in spelunca paritura es incarnatum propter nos, ut restauret opus manuum suarum. Dominus, qui ponit nubem ascensum suum, per nubem Virginis venit ad nos nasciturus ex illa, ut obscurissimas peccati nubes animarum nostrarum dissipet, dum eidem clamamus: Benedicite, omnia opera Domini, Dominum, etc. Ferens ferentem omnia, ad Bethlehem venis, o Virgo, ibi eumdem paritura, et tanquam infantem reclinatura, ut hominum revocationem mirabiliter operetur. Ex canone duplici in festo S. Anastasiæ martyris, die 22. Mendicat ille qui dives est, propter suam misericordiam e Virgine natus: reges Magi discessum præparant ab Oriente, ut illum intueantur incarnatum, et fideliter adorent. Apparuit Deus qui erat invisibilis, supra humanum morem natus ex te, o Virgo Mater, propter multam misericordiam 243 suam, pauper factus qui erat dives, ut immortalitate humanum genus ditaret. Hic solus Deus noster, qui ex te, o Virgo, vera carne ineffabiliter indutus, in spelunca nasci festinat, ut me, speluncam latronum effectum, templum divini Spiritus efficiat. O puella viri nescia, fers incarnatum in utero tuo illum qui universam fert creaturam; quem etiam ex te natum in præsepio reclinas; et cernitur ut infans, ille qui est ante sæcula. Jam completa sunt verba eorum, qui in Spiritu sancto prophetaverunt: Virgo enim accelerat parere in spelunca perfectissimum Deum. Ex utero tuo lucifero procedit incarnatus Rex cœlestis, o inviolata, et in præsepio tanquam in throno reclinatur. Nunc in propria venit novo partu editum Verbum Patris incarnatum ex Virgine; et tanquam infans cernitur in spelunca propter summam misericordiam suam.

Cum te sacris symbolis figuratam agnovisset Joseph justus, o Virgo Deo charissima, per virgæ sortem venerandum conjugium tuum accepit, in memoriam reducens sanctam virgam Aaronis, quæ olim germinaverat.
Legis umbras vidisti abundantia luminis gratiæ perfusas; et e Virgine, nube lucida, orientem in carne intellectualem solem aspexisti : et tanquam astrum illuminasti, o sapiens Joseph, omnes qui clamant assidue : Benedicat omnis creatura Dominum.
Custodisti, o Deifere Joseph, Virginem, quæ virginitatem incorruptam conservavit; ex qua Deus Verbum incarnatus est, conservans illam virginem post partum ineffabilem. Tu, o Joseph, una cum illa memor esto nostri.

ruined, he took away the wall of enmity standing between us, established peace, and bestowed life and divine redemption.

Hail, lone Mother of Him who begged for our flesh; hail, raising up of the fallen world, O most immaculate; hail, dissolution of sorrow; hail, salvation of the faithful; hail, most high throne of God.

O more-than-admirable Maiden, you bore Him for us who is before all ages and who was made like us through His extreme compassion, that He might save those who sing: Blessed are You, the God of our fathers.
Following your divine words, the generations of men call you blessed, O ever-blessed one, sweetly singing together: Bless the Lord, all you works. O Virgin, lover of good things, make good my soul, which has been corrupted by the malice of sin; for you gave birth to the good God and Lord.

O miracle of miracles! How is it that our God, who is above all creation, is created and formed from the Mother of God; and by His own will, He renews and fashions us again out of water and spirit, a most wonderful creation, He the only Benefactor? The Cherubim and every heavenly nature shudder, O most immaculate one, out of reverence for your incomprehensible and venerable Offspring, who became like us through His ineffable mercy and was baptized in the flesh; whose divine appearance we now all celebrate with rejoicing.
*From the Canon on the holy seventy apostles, day 4.*
Let us honor the divine palace of the King, in which He dwelt as He willed; let us praise the unwedded and only Theotokos, through whom we have been deified. The most blessed choir of prophets of old...
Note: To the Bishop of Cythera, Antonius Pinellus of Venice published in 1529, in quarto. in the Spirit, invokes thee divinely, O most pure one, as the gate and the shaded mountain.

I praise thee, the only one worthy of all praise; I glorify thee, O ever-glorified by God; and I call thee blessed, whom generations of generations call blessed, O Virgin most blessed by God.
Thou hast become an expiation, O most pure one, for those who are always sinning, having given birth in an order above nature to Christ who takes away the sin of the world, to whom we cry out: Blessed art Thou, O Lord and God of our fathers.

Strengthen, O most immaculate Lady, my weakness, [thou] who gavest birth to the power of the Most High, who grantest being to all, and who magnified the memory of Domnica.

Thou hast brought forth the Holy Lord of all, O Giver of the Lord, whom Domnica, desiring from her soul, dominates the death-dealing passions, O Virgin, praising thee.
For my sake, like unto me, that infant became, He who is most perfect, that He might renew me, grown old from passions, through thee, most holy bride of God.

Cause the waves of my fleshly passions to rest, I pray Thee, O Maiden, and as it were to fall asleep, through Thy ever-vigilant intercession; and do not allow me to fall into the deepest sleep of sin.
Thee, who didst bear in Thy womb the Manna of life, that ancient jar which contained the manna most truly and clearly prefigured. Blessed art Thou among women, O most pure Lady.
Through Thee the ancient Paradise is opened once again, and man, formerly condemned, is brought into it, and is truly deified, O chaste one, full of God’s grace, the lump of mortals who cry out: All ye works, praise the Lord.
The Cherubim shudder, seeing that Word who is inexpressibly present among them and who rests there, held as an infant in the arms of Thy mother, O most holy Lady, who surpassest in the height of Thy dignity all created things.
From the other Canon for the same saints.
Check the floods of my sins, Thou who didst dry up the corruption of death by Thy birth; and grant me compunction, O most pure Mother of God.
That turning sword, which used to bar the entrance to Paradise, blushes and is filled with shame, seeing the lance which pierced Thy Son, O Virgin Mother—He who was born of Thee.
Awaken me from sloth, for I am asleep and covered in sins; call me to repentance, O most chaste one, as Mother of the Word.
As fair, as beautiful, as radiant with the brightness of purity, Thou didst embody the Word who is beautiful in form and didst give Him birth, O Virgin Mother: He who by divine operation gives existence to all from the riches of His goodness.

and calm the grievous storm of my passions, I beseech thee.
Loosing the curse of Eve, thou didst dwell in a womb free from all stain, pouring forth a fountain of blessing to those who cry aloud: Blessed, O most pure one, is the fruit of thy womb.
He who is in all things perfect and by nature inaccessible, was made accessible to me, being clothed in flesh from thee, O unwedded one; whom do thou fervently beseech to scatter the burden of my iniquities, and to save me as I sing: Priests, bless; O ye people, superexalt Christ unto all ages.
Spare me, O Savior, who wast born and didst keep her who bore thee undefiled after the birth, when thou shalt sit to judge my works, overlooking my iniquities and my sins, as one sinless, as a merciful God and lover of mankind.
From the Canon to Saint John the Hut-Dweller, day 18.
By the grievous assaults of my passions, O Virgin, being tossed by a tempest, and shaken by the onslaughts of sin, I flee with longing to thy sleepless protection, O all-praised one. Have mercy on me, and save me, O Ever-Virgin.
As a myrrh-breathing rose, O undefiled one, did the Pure One find thee in the valleys, and He dwelt in the midst of thee, filling the human race with most sweet fragrance.
Direct the impulses of my soul, O all-immaculate one, toward the divine commandments of Him who shone forth from thy womb, delivering me by thy intercessions from the tempest of the scandals of this life.
Thou didst bear Emmanuel, the Lord of all, without the seed of a man, remaining a virgin even after the birth, O Virgin-Mother; whom do thou unceasingly entreat to deliver from the invasions of enemies those who flee under thy protection.
The Word, who is co-equal in operation and upon the throne with His Begetter, thou didst embody from thy womb, O chaste one, because of His ineffable compassion, having assumed our whole nature.
We praise thy birth-giving, O blessed one, through which we were redeemed from ancient condemnation; and we call thee blessed, O divinely-blessed one, whom alone He loved who is blessed and super-glorious.
perennial river thou pourest forth for us who flee to thee, O chaste one; of whose abundant grace tasting, we praise thy birth-giving, O most inviolate one, and superexalt it unto all eternity.
Thy womb became the dwelling-place of Light, through whom those who sat in darkness have seen the light; whence we continually praise thee with unceasing voices, O Mother of God, and with longing we venerate the hope of our souls.
From the Canon to the Adoration of the Precious Chains of the Holy and All-Praised Apostle Peter, day 16.
All the swords of the deceitful enemy have failed, O undefiled Virgin.
Since that time when that Word, who dwelt within your undefiled womb, was wounded by the lance, I beseech you now to wound my heart with his most sweet love.
Death halted when it reached you, its unbridled impetus [(50)] checked; for you alone gave birth to the fountain of immortality, O Mother of God, Virgin Mother.
As the King of all, inhabiting your holy womb as a spacious palace, he appeared incarnate, O most pure Lady. Burdened as I am, O undefiled one, by the weight of many sins, lift me up now, strengthening me to bear the most light yoke of Christ. Our first father was clothed in the leather tunics of mortality; but the Creator is clothed in him, having become incarnate from your blood beyond all understanding, O all-blameless one.
He who descended upon the earth as rain, O Virgin, watered the whole earth with divine knowledge, and showed you to be more honorable than all the angels, O pure one. The prophet of old prefigured you as an intellectual candelabra, O Mother of God, bearing the divine lamp which enlightened those who were formerly overshadowed by the many darknesses of evil. You became a dwelling-place of light: therefore enlighten me, O maiden, darkened by all the unbelief of the enemy, so that in faith I may magnify you, O most holy Mother-Virgin.
From the Canon to the Holy Martyrs Speusippus, Eleusippus, and Meleusippus, on the 16th day [(50')]
You appeared as an unplowed earth, O most august Mother of God, most chaste; you brought forth for us the provider of all, the Lord Jesus, of whom we partake and are recalled to life. Seeing God incarnate from you, O chaste Virgin Mother of God, we properly confess you, who were clearly the cause of the reformation of all things. That superessential One, who was without flesh, became incarnate from your venerable blood, O most chaste one; and having become flesh without any change, he conversed with men. The laws of nature are truly made new in you, O most pure Virgin: for you remain a Virgin after the birth, just as you were before the birth, having given birth to Christ the Lawgiver. Heal the passions of my miserable soul, O most chaste Mother of God; render my mind, which is tossed like a storm by the invasions of the enemy, tranquil and peaceful, O maiden. Jesus, the planter of all, truly found you to be a rose in the midst of thorns in the valleys of this world, O chaste Virgin, and born from your womb, he poured over us the most sweet fragrance of divine knowledge. We have acknowledged you as the spiritual candelabra, O Virgin Mary, for you received the inaccessible light, and you illuminated the souls of all the faithful and eliminated the darkness of sin. With voices full of thanksgiving we cry out to you: Hail, most pure dwelling-place of immaterial light; hail, cause of the deification of all; hail, dissolution of the curse; hail, recall of the exiled children of earth.
From the Canon to the Holy Martyr Neophytus, on the 21st day
Having given birth to the Creator by nature, you have deified the whole substance of those born of the earth; therefore we rightly confess you to be the Theotokos, O Virgin, Bride of God. The race of mortals ever offers a hymn of thanksgiving to you, Mother of God, having obtained immortality through you.
You have brought forth the One who, being super-divine, voluntarily became poor through the riches of His goodness, in order to show compassion for our poverty. The divine mystery, hidden before all ages, O maiden most immaculate, has been made known through you to the ends of the earth: Your Son and the Word of God, who became flesh and deified man, O Virgin. You have shown yourself to be the most radiant throne of the heavenly King, O Virgin, in whom He rested in the flesh of His own will, and took away our great weariness, and established man upon the paternal throne, as He was pleased to do. You appeared higher than the angels, having given birth to the Angel of Great Counsel, O pure Theotokos, to whom we all sing: "Blessed are You, O Lord God, unto the ages." You have given birth to a New Child, the One born of the Father ineffably before all creation, O all-pure One; therefore, entreat Him now to renew me, grown old in sins, and to save me as I cry out: "Children, bless; priests, praise; O people, supremely exalt Christ unto the ages." You, O Bride of God, who like tongs have carried the heavenly coal, burn up the brush-like passions of my heart, and deliver me, I pray, from the fire of Gehenna, that I may glorify you, the hope of the faithful, O most worthy of all praise.
From the Canon to the holy martyr Agathangelus, on the 23rd day.
You have given birth, O Virgin, to the Lord who became incarnate out of ineffable compassion, He whom Agathangelus desired, and so departed from the flesh after a wondrous contest, with whom we hymn you. O marvelous mystery! How has the Virgin been shown to be more spacious than the heavens, conceiving in her womb, without being straitened, Him whom no limit can contain or define? We always bless you, O blessed Mother of God, through whom we have been made worthy of glory, and have received back the ancient Paradise which we had lost. Show yourself, O Virgin unwedded, to be the deliverer of us all from temptations, dangers, and tribulations, as we hymn you with affection. Free me, O pure One, from the death-dealing sleep of negligence, and strengthen me, O Lady, to keep watch in divine hymns and good works, that I may be able to praise you with affection. You have become the word of an inexplicable mystery, O Virgin; for you contained without being straitened God, who is in all things incomprehensible, and you gave birth to Him, and nourished Him at your breasts, when He willed to show mercy to us who confess you to be the Theotokos. Your people, O Virgin, who glorify you, have you as a powerful intercession, and consolation, and a hope that is not confounded, an unassailable wall, and divine protection; and having attained salvation, it cries out with most sweet voices: "Bless, all you works of the Lord, the Lord forever."
You illuminate the world, O most pure one, shedding forth light, which before the ages shone from the Father beyond understanding. Therefore I cry out to you: Drive away the darkness of turbulent thoughts from my heart, that I may praise you, O chaste one.
In an unspeakable manner you contained the Word, who became like us for the sake of his supreme goodness; and you truly gave birth to that same one in two wills and one person: therefore we proclaim you, O Virgin, the immaculate and inviolate Mother of God, so that they may attain eternal glory and light, O most immaculate Virgin, who are the help of the faithful.
58 The human race offers to you a hymn of thanksgiving, for it has received immortality as its lot through you.
Lady, immune to the marriage bed, you who gave birth to the Word incarnate, illuminate my soul, and free me from Gehenna and punishment.
Do not cease to deliver me from captivity, and from the deadly tempest that presses upon me from all sides, and from the most grievous passions that drive me to death, O holiest maiden, refuge of sinners, and prompt help of men.
The Lord, having entered your womb like a most beautiful bridegroom, proceeded from it supernaturally, and adorned men with immortality, and saved those who recognize you as the true and chaste Mother of God.
The light, having arisen from your womb, illuminated the circle of the earth, O Virgin, and utterly eliminated everywhere the mist of demons and the darkness of ignorance, O Jesus, giver of light.
Make me stable, O Virgin, by your intercessions upon the rock 59 of truth; and never allow me to be tripped up by the snares of the deceiver, O most dear to God, that I may faithfully call you blessed.
As though we were enriched by a propitiatory, as though by a fervent patronage before God, we your servants have you, O inviolate one, immune from every stain: free us from eternal torments while we sing your praises.
The Lord was incarnate without change from your chaste blood, O Virgin, all-pure, and recall all of us, entangled in the snares of errors, to divine life, while we praise you, O most worthy of all praise.
Distill upon me, O most chaste Lady, the showers of divine compunction, that I may mourn and cleanse myself entirely from the filth of my immense sins.
Wounded and cast down by the sword of sin, I am dead. You who gave birth to Christ, who by his own death took away death, restore me to life and salvation by your life-giving patronage.
The most sacred tongues of the prophets, foretelling, called you the fertile mountain, O most immaculate and chaste maiden; the gate unspeakably bringing forth the Sun of justice, who illuminates our hearts with divine splendors, while we cry out: The Lord, etc.
Free me from the most fearful necessity, O chaste Virgin, when the time shall come in which your Son and Lord will come, to examine all things by true judgment, and to render to each according to their merit rewards or punishments, while all the orders of the heavenly host stand round with trembling.
60 MONTH OF FEBRUARY.

From the Canon to the holy Parthenius, Bishop of Lampsacus, 7th day
O you who have brought forth the good God, O spotless one, make good my humble heart, which is corrupted by many passions, and strengthen me to perform the will of our Redeemer, who wills that all men should be saved. The Lord conversed with men by having taken flesh from you in an inexplicable manner; therefore, O all-holy one, entreat Him to have mercy on me, who am worn down by the attacks of the serpent and am being cast down. (51) It is a distinguished praise of the Theotokos that she was always kept untainted by any sin with regard to the state of grace, and was positioned far from the curse and subjection to the devil, outside the common defilement of nature. Therefore, by this praise, of which she is most worthy, she ought to be celebrated by all who desire to praise her. Furthermore, that this praise of the Theotokos is everywhere excellent, it ought to be beyond all doubt. It is most a matter of wonder that the Abulensis, although he thinks excellently of the conception of Mary, affirms that she was immune from sin, and pronounces that to be safer and clearly more eligible, at length arrived at saying: "The praise and glory of the Theotokos is not changed or diminished in this, if it is said that she incurred original sin, as those think who do not penetrate the nature of original sin": C since it is no small glory to be always like to God, and to have been exempt by the benefit of God from the state of unlikeness to God, which is original sin, and likewise from the stain of sin, which by its nature corrupts and infects, nay even kills the soul: just as, on the contrary, his praise is not diminished, who is supposed to be sullied by that stain. See Velasquez, *De Maria immaculate concepta*, lib. 11, dissertat. 5, annot. 1, where he shows that the most holy Virgin cannot be praised according to her dignity, unless to the common praises of the Theotokos that is added, which is surely that she was immaculately conceived. Moreover, Ambrosius Catharinus in his disputation *Pro immaculata conceptione*, lib. 1, acting against some who said that it did not pertain to the praise of Mary that she was preserved from the stain of original sin, says among other things: "What they add, furthermore, that it pertains little to the praise of the Lady that we ascribe to her the privilege of preservation from original sin, is absolutely unthinkable. Do they, I ask, think the foulness of sin, the wrath and enmity of God, and slavery to the devil to be a small evil, even if one were held by these great evils for a short moment? But those who see the matter with spiritual eyes do not think so. Wherefore they judge it to be a great thing that she was saved from this so miserable condition by a singular gift, just as that woman herself, exulting in spirit, professed (Luke 1): *For He who is mighty has done great things for me.* But if we were to profess this gift, even in itself, to be small, yet surely it would become great, both by the excellence of the Giver, and also by the singularity of it, to whom alone it was given; for, as someone said excellently, even small gifts, when bestowed by great princes, are reckoned great and favorable. Finally, if that man, the diligent examiner and prudent appraiser of spiritual things, Augustine, could not without horror think about the flesh of Mary, once dead, being subject to corruption for any point of time (as he himself testifies), how much less should this certainly be thought concerning that most sacred soul, that it could truly be said to have been corrupted by sin, subject to the power of the devil, and finally, for any moment, even an enemy to God? But why do I delay further? When even in this place they fight diametrically against the opinion of the Blessed Thomas? For what they make of such little account, Thomas himself on the contrary makes so much of, that he therefore denies it is fitting for Mary, because it seemed too exalted, in that by it she seemed to be made equal to Christ. We, however, as we will declare in our own places, confess that it is indeed great, yet not so great that it ascends to the Majesty of Christ. Wherefore it is completely frivolous what they added, that it suffices that she be celebrated as the Mother of God, and that alone in place of all praise; for by this very reasoning they would conclude that she not be praised as Virgin, that she not be honored as sanctified, and that her glorious Assumption, and other titles of prerogatives in which she abounds, should be passed over in silence. Thus Catharinus in the cited place.
and the hosts of the incorporeal ones glorify with trembling. Supplicate Him, therefore, always to show mercy to those who glorify you.

O most holy one, throne of God, higher than the cherubim, cloud of light, illuminate the eyes of my soul, O all-pure one, and cleanse my heart from the mist of passions.

From the Canon for the Holy Apostle Archippus, on the 19th.
The divine-speaking prophets, seeing [it] from afar with prophetic eyes, O all-pure one, the dread [mystery] of your divine birth-giving which is beyond the mind.
They have manifested, O most chaste and inviolate one, that mystery in various ways and figures. You were shown to be clearly a temple of God, O all-pure one, and a pure tabernacle, and a dwelling place worthy of God. As a shady mountain, Habakkuk foresaw you long ago, O all-perfect one, carrying the Word, who overshadows all men from the heat of transgressions and the burning of sins, O Virgin. D ...that the Deipara is called [such], it must be asserted that every stain of sin, whether actual or original, had been entirely removed from her.
(54) To effect the body of Christ in the Eucharist, an immaculate host is required, and it is offered to God thus: "We offer to Thee, O Lord, an immaculate host": which is understood to persist everywhere clean and as unleavened bread without any leaven. Therefore, in the mystery of the Incarnation, the Son of God had to take flesh from an immaculate and most pure Mother subject to no old leaven, as learned authors observe that in ancient times, on the hosts in which the body of Christ was to be consecrated, images of the Mother of God were carved, so that the immunity of the Deipara from the stain of sin might be explained by the immaculate host of the Eucharist. See Velasquez, *De Maria Concepta*, book II, dissert. 2, annotat. 1, n. 5.

You became the bridal chamber of the Word of God, and his fire-formed throne, in which the same Word, because of his supreme goodness, rested incarnate; therefore beseech him, O chaste one, to have mercy and show his compassion toward me.
My wretched soul, weakened by the many aggressions and blows of Belial, make whole and sound through your strengthening prayers, O Virgin Mother of God, that I may glorify you unto all ages.
You renewed the corrupted nature of the first parent, giving birth beyond the order of nature to the Creator of the universal nature, while remaining a virgin; whom you once lamented, O most holy Virgin Mother, when you saw him hanging upon the cross.
MONTH OF MARCH
From the canon for the holy martyr Hesychius, 2nd day
You remained truly a virgin after birth, just as you were before birth; for you gave birth to the Creator, whom, O most immaculate one, beseech for the salvation of those who praise you.
Death persisted until you, O most holy one; for you gave birth to the fountain of immortality, Christ our only most good God.
Having blossomed forth the incorruptible cluster, O maiden, you appeared as one who pours out the sweetness of immortality for all, O immaculate one and mother who knew no wedlock.
You alone on earth have given birth to Him who is in heaven, the divine Word, whom all creation praises as Creator and Lord.
The Lord, having dwelt in your holy womb, O Theotokos, makes those who now call you blessed with true faith become the delightful dwellings of the Trinity.
Us who were all dead through sin, having given birth to Life, you have revived; therefore we cry out to you, O maiden and God-bearer, ever-glorious.
The most holy prophet calls you an unpassable gate, O inviolate one, through which none may pass, and the Creator alone passed, as He alone knows, leaving it closed just as it was before birth.
Light has risen for us from you, O most immaculate one, the only Lord of all, and He has brightened the hearts of all with divine knowledge and lessened the darkness of ignorance; whence we all call you blessed.
From the Canon for the Holy Martyr Theodotus, on the 6th day
Human nature at one time became slave to seduction through deceit. But when you, O inviolate one, gave birth to Christ, having obtained freedom, it venerates Him with great voices.
Heal my mind, O most chaste one, which languishes, struck by the blows of the most wicked Dragon, and serves captive to sins.
Most luminous Palace of the Lord, most holy Lady, make us dwellings of the Holy Spirit, while in your holy house we offer praise to the Lord.
You conceived God who was made man, O Lady; therefore generations of generations incessantly call you blessed.
Together with the heavenly choirs, we all cry out to you; Hail, Mother of God; animated heaven, most glorious palace, and fiery throne, in which Christ rested according to the flesh.
Christ our God, who dwelt in your womb, O immaculate one, having cleansed human nature from every defilement, O inviolate one, having given birth to the super-celestial Son made man, you have renewed us, who were worn out by antiquity: and now we cry out, O chaste one: Praise the Lord, all you works.
Light, which shone forth ineffably from the Father before the morning star, you have brought forth to us, O Virgin, and dissipating the darkness of ignorance, you have illuminated and gladdened those who sat in the shadow of sin.
From the Canon for the Holy Martyrs Theodore, Constantine, etc., on the 6th day
O most holy Virgin, divine ornament of the athletes, you who gave birth to Christ, beautiful in beauty, beseech Him to adorn my soul.
The company of the forty-two holy martyrs, struggling, proclaimed you overtly as the truest Mother of God most high, who emboldened the same by your intercessions in the struggle.
The divine martyrs, knowing you to be a chaste mother, O maiden, and celebrating the glory in you, inherited immortal gifts in the highest.
Direct the motions of my mind, I pray, O inviolate one, toward God, who is the way of life, and who has made smooth the paths of the triumphant martyrs leading to the heavenly things.
The Deipara, a maiden, beyond the laws of nature and above the order of the same nature, brought forth Thee, O Christ, who truly crowned the martyrs who struggled lawfully for the faith.
You are a scroll most new, O inviolate one, who held the Word written within you, who in the book of the living inscribed His own divine athletes, who most exactly fulfilled the things that were written.
The divine archangel, appearing to you as the harbinger of divine nuptials, O chaste and inviolate one, cried out: Hail, O fiery throne of God, the support of the triumphant martyrs who confessed that God was manifested in the flesh.
O receptacle of light, most dear to God, with your illuminating rays enlighten my heart, driving away the clouds of sloth and eliminating the darkness of sin; you who brought forth God, who is free from every stain of sin.
72. From the canon to the holy martyrs Basil, Ephraim, etc., on day 7.
The penalty of the first parents was removed, O chaste and inviolate one, by your ineffable birth-giving; and to them the former entry to Paradise was opened, wherefore they celebrate you with a loud voice.
O Virgin, totally chaste and inviolate, you brought forth that most powerful Lord, who liberated men from the power of the enemy.
You brought the dead men to life, O Virgin, having given birth beyond all grasp of thought to Christ our God, who for His mercy’s sake became man.
Blessed is that people that acknowledges you, O most immaculate one, as the Mother of the Lord of all, and with affection calls you blessed.
The shadows of the Law, and the ænigmas of the prophets, prefigured you, O most pure Virgin, who were to conceive and bring forth through the ineffable Word Him who would bring salvation to the world.
The Word of God, who with His hand formed Eve, desiring to reform the universe, received from your womb, O maiden, the human form, beginning to be, though with the Father and the Holy Spirit He is coeternal and coequal.
The supersubstantial God, born of you, O inviolate one, appeared as man, with two natures, operations, and wills; appearing manifestly to those to whom He willingly became similar. Wherefore we cry to Him: All you works, praise the Lord.
The maiden most dear to God, carrying in her arms Christ, who with His hand carries all things, struck with awe, cried out, saying: How do I see You as both my Son and my Creator, O incomprehensible one?
73. From the canon to St. Quadratus and the martyrs with him, on day 10.
From the filth of the passions, from the tempest of thoughts, from the darts of the wicked one, and from every hostile assault, save, O immaculate and totally pure Deipara, the souls of those who praise your ineffable birth-giving.
Not even the celestial mind is able to explain, O
to interpret, O Maiden, is possible; for you conceived in your womb, O chaste one, the Word of the primordial Mind, who established all things by His word. The most holy Theotokos, in whom the consubstantial Word of the Father was pleased to dwell as in a fragrant house, felt no burning of the womb, nor did she experience the pains of childbirth; for she has brought forth Emmanuel, God and man.
He who fashioned Eve from the rib, O immaculate one, was himself fashioned from your womb, O chaste one, wishing to save Adam because of His compassion, as a lover of mankind.
You have made heavenly the nature of men, which had become earthly, O all-blameless one, and you have deified it, corrupted as it was; for this reason, we all glorify you with unceasing voices.
Blessed is the fruit of your blessed womb, whom the hierarchies of heaven and the assemblies of mortals bless, He who redeemed us from the ancient curse; blessed are you.
Redeemed from the curse of the first mother through you, the chaste Mother of God, O blessed Lady, we bless you with faith and psalmody, O all-holy Virgin, Bride of God.
Having appeared as the bearer of the Maker of all things beyond all understanding, O most pure one, you were shown to be higher than the heavens and mistress of all, O Virgin Theotokos, all-praised one; therefore, we all magnify you.
From the Canon to our Holy Father Benedict, 14th day
We who have been enriched with incorruption through you, O most chaste Mother of God, cry out to you: Hail, full of grace, the adornment of all saints and just ones.
He who alone is good entered into your womb, O all-blameless one, where He assumed flesh and became perfect man; whom you entreat, O most pure one, for the salvation of our souls.
As rain upon the fleece, O immaculate one, the Word descended into your venerable womb, assuming flesh, and He clearly stilled the showers of polytheism, O all-blameless one, and dissipated the bitter storm, O most immaculate one.
He who dwells in the heavens dwelt in your all-blameless womb, that He might make us houses of the Trinity, we who proclaim you to be the Theotokos, O immaculate one.
From your holy womb has risen the unsetting Sun of righteousness, and He illuminated the faithful, O Virgin Theotokos, all-praised one.
Heal the passions of my soul, you who conceived the fountain of impassibility, O Virgin, and grant me showers of compunction, O holy Theotokos, that I may acquire future consolation in heaven.
Behold, He has been born of you, as Isaiah clearly proclaimed, O chaste one, the Son of the Most High, and your Son He is seen to be, O Virgin, making those who praise you sons of the heavenly Father.
O Virgin, bearer of Light, expel the clouds of my soul, and grant me, O Lady, to be purified and brought to reflect the saving beauty of Him who shone forth ineffably from your all-holy womb into the light of the nations, O all-hymned one.
75 From the canon for the holy martyrs Agapius and his companions, on the 15th day:
With the most radiant brightness of Him who rose from you, O Virgin, enlighten the pupils of my soul, that I may glorify you.
We recognized the Creator, who appeared in the likeness of flesh from your womb of light due to the bowels of His mercy, O Mother, ever-Virgin, for us who sing to you.
You received as perfume in your womb the Word, O spotless and chaste one, who purifies the world from the foulest stench of every sin; wherefore we faithfully call you blessed.
Let us believers bless the Theotokos with divine hymns, saying: Rejoice, O gate, through which the Lord alone passed.
O all-hymned one, having withered the plants of godlessness with your holy shoot, diminish the malice of the enemy that daily sprouts within me, O bride of God.
Loose me, bound by the chains of countless sins, O all-hymned one, granting me showers of tears as I sing to Him who rose from you: Blessed are You, the God of our fathers.
Heal the passions of my heart, O Mother of the Savior, you who gave birth to the fountain of dispassion, and guide me toward divine life, that I may glorify you, O Mother of the Savior, unto all ages.
Illumine me, O most immaculate one, darkened by negligence
B (55) No one ought to be ignorant (says Catharinus in his *Disputation on the Truth of the Immaculate Conception*, book III, testimonial 6) that in the Holy Scriptures, among the many adolescent girls and concubines of the king who are mentioned there, one is the primary Spouse of the King Christ Himself, chosen and pre-elected, which is understood beyond doubt to be Mary, just as the Church also sings. For, clearly, to declare her excellence, it is written: There are sixty queens and eighty concubines, and of the young maidens there is no number. One is my dove, my perfect one. But to no one, unless he be a man of excessively austere mind, can it seem decent that the supreme and primary king should have wanted to adopt for himself as Spouse such a one as this—namely, the first and primary one—of whom it could somehow be said, even for a moment, that she was under the power of a hostis and an adulterer: and thus subject to her own, and to His Father’s, the greatest and highest King, especially since He Himself could and knew how, if He but willed, to snatch her away and preserve her for Himself, lest she be surrendered into the enemy's hand. I beseech you, let us learn this at least from the prudence of the world; and let us not attribute less kindness and prudence to God. For if a spouse is sought for some son of a great king, who himself is beautiful beyond the sons of men, either the son himself seeks her, or (that the parable may be more fitting) if the power of choosing is given to the son himself—nay, rather, the power of creating and fashioning one according to his choice—will he, I ask, choose or fashion for himself one whom he allows to be seized and violated by an enemy, whom he could have nevertheless protected and managed to save beforehand? Indeed, a man must certainly be austere who would maintain this; for it is most indecent in a primary spouse. For these nuptials would limp most foully, since the spouse would not be suitable for the bridegroom, whom we already declare to be beautiful beyond the sons of men. But as for the fact that after this one primary spouse, who is entirely undefiled, he should have others secondarily—either handmaids or concubines—who are indeed redeemed and snatched from the hand of enemies, and therefore not entirely intact, there is nothing absurd in this; for no one would cast blame if that one first and principal spouse was kept for him such that she remained entirely undefiled, intact, and immaculate. What then? Will the children of the world be more prudent in their generation—I do not say than the children of light (for this often happens because of our own sloth), but than the Light itself? The Light itself, I say, the eternal Light and true Wisdom, whence everyone who is wise derives his wisdom? Far be it. For who can say this without blasphemy? Therefore, will the most beautiful and most wise and most omnipotent King not have adopted for Himself such a Spouse—nay, (to use the words of Jerome) even created and preserved her—such as He foresaw to be universally suitable for Him, namely, perpetually beautiful, unblemished, entirely incorrupt in mind and body, and with whom no discord could ever occur? That he who denies this must be maliciously affected is absolutely necessary. So far Catharinus in the cited place.
all-blameless one, enlighten me, so that I may hymn and glorify your greatness.
76 From the Canon to the holy Pope and Martyr, day 16
.
Existing holier than the angels, most holy one, you conceived the holy God, who incessantly bestows holiness upon all who glorify him and venerate his holy martyrs.
The prophet David, singing of you, Mother of God, most clearly prefigured you by the name of the "fertile mountain," from whom Christ came, who crushed the mountains of malice.
You appeared as a holy temple, O inviolate Virgin, which contained within itself God, who bestows holiness upon all, because of his ineffable mercy and utterly inexpressible piety.
The chorus of the prophets prefigured you, O most dear to God, as the future Mother of the Creator, whom you should beseech without any intermission, that he may have mercy on our souls.
O Christ, the abyss of mercy and compassions, born of the Mother, dry up the abyss of my evils, O most holy Lady, through your intercession, and grant me thoughts of compunction.
Blessed is your fruit, most heavily laden with every blessing, O most blessed Lady, whom you should implore to bless us, who have acknowledged you as the chaste Mother of God.
Cast down by your strength, O inviolate Virgin, the entire strength of the enemy, and strengthen us with virtue, that we may be able to perform the divine will of your Son, O formidable protection of those who call upon you!
O chaste and immaculate Virgin, who appeared as the receptacle of God, cleanse me, stained with many sins, I pray, O Mother of God, by your purificative intercession, and on the day of judgment deliver me from the sentence of condemnation.
77 From the Canon to the holy Alexius, man of God, day 17
.
The Son of God, coeternal with him, had you, O inviolate Virgin, as the cause by which he was made similar to us, since he had found you alone, above all creation, to be pure: whence all generations praise you and call you blessed.
He who is above in heaven, invisible to the angels, below on earth, having been born of you, O inviolate one, is seen by all as perfect man, about to recover the lost world.
O Virgin, who has suckled the giver of milk, satisfy my heart, now famishing and groaning, I pray, with all divine knowledge and compunction.
He who dwells in light inhabited your holy womb, O chaste one, that he might recover the world perishing in the darkness of ignorance; implore him to illuminate all who praise you.
When the Creator of all creatures had renewed the laws of nature, O inviolate Lady, he was born of you in an ineffable manner, and because of his immense mercy he deified me.
You became a minister of the great mystery, O all-blameless one; for you embodied God, who redeemed us from great evils, we who magnify you, O chaste, blessed, most dear to God.
As we had flowed down into corruption on account of the ancient transgression, the Lover of mankind, in an impassible manner, was incarnate from the Mother.
And he delivered all from the corruption of sin, O all-blameless one. To you we cry out, rejoicing, with the voices of Gabriel, saying: Hail, O untilled field; hail, O dissolution of the curse; hail, O fountain of living water; hail, O boast of the saints, Theotokos, ever-Virgin.
From the canon for the holy martyrs Chrysanthus and Daria, day 19.
He who by divine nature is inaccessible, appeared accessible to me, having taken flesh from you, O Virgin; whom Daria, longing for, struggled steadfastly, and was brought to him as a bride.
The Son, who was born of your womb, O inviolate Virgin, according to the flesh, betrothed to himself the chaste martyr bride, Daria.
He, incomprehensible to every intellect, who preserved you a Virgin after the birth, just as you were before the birth, was incarnate from you, O inviolate one, taking to himself the martyr Daria as his bride.
Who is able to explain your mystery, O most chaste one? For you have brought forth the God-Word, beyond thought and word, double in nature.
The Virgin bore you as a new child, the pre-eternal Word, whom maidens, longing for him, were brought after her as brides to you, the King of all.
He who in divine substance is uncircumscribed, in your bosom, O Virgin, became circumscribed like us according to the flesh. Blessed are you among women, O Lady, immune from every stain.
When God had found you, the immaculate one, like a rose in the midst of the thorns of this life, O most chaste one, he dwelt in your inviolate womb, and filled the world with mystical sweetness, which calls out: All you works, praise the Lord.
Mind and heart tremble while they contemplate your birth, O Maiden. For you conceived God the Word, whom no thought can comprehend, who through you delivers from every necessity those who honor you.
Ex Canone in S. Cyrillum episcopum Cataniæ, die 11 (58').*
My strength, my praise, and my salvation is Christ, O most chaste one; who was born of you as a man, [surrounding/in the face of] corruption, because of his great mercy, and became what he was not. A O the immense depth of the mystery: God is incarnate and born of an incorrupt maiden, and he dissolves corruption through the sufferings which he alone, the Good One and Lover of mankind, undergoes. How did you bring forth the Word? How, after childbirth, did you remain incorrupt, just as you were before, O most immaculate Virgin? How did you nourish the nourisher of all, the infant who appeared voluntarily, gentle and placid? O the novelty of your miracle, O most pure one! Save me, O most clean one, from most grievous dangers: raise me up from the dunghill of my passions; and from the captivity and vexation of the most evil demons deliver me, while I devoutly praise you. Be a helmswoman to me, O Virgin, in the most dangerous sea of this life, and direct me to the harbor of salvation, and save me. Revive my mind, which is destroyed by the disease of many passions, O most immaculate one; and give me strength, that I may be able to accomplish things pleasing to God, that I may magnify you, the fervent patronage and hope of Christians. You cured the contrition of earthly Adam, when you brought forth God the Savior, O most unblemished one. Entreat him for the healing of the wounds of my soul, which labors under an incurable disease. When the venerable maiden carried as a newly born infant the Word who is before the ages, she was struck with awe, and said: My Son, how do I carry you, who contain all things with a nod? How do I nourish with milk the nourisher, the Savior, and God?
*Ex canone in S. Basilium presbyterum et martyrem, die 22.*
The Only-Begotten, who is together with the Father, willed to inhabit your inviolate womb, O chaste one; and he became man that he might save men by his goodness. When Isaiah had known your conception from afar by the Spirit, O maiden, he clearly manifested it crying out: Behold, the Virgin shall conceive God in her womb. I praise you, Lady, who are worthy of all praise; I bless you, O Virgin, through whom all we men have been blessed, and have been truly liberated from the ancient curse. Let us honor the one more exalted than the Cherubim, more lofty than the heavens, superior to all creation, the rampart of the wise martyrs, the sole Theotokos. I praise you, O most praiseworthy one, whom the hosts of the heavenly orders praise; and I beseech you, O inviolate one, that you may heal the affections of my soul, and deliver me from eternal fire. Perceiving that your virginity remained incorrupt after the birth, O Virgin, you cried out to the Savior and God who was born of you beyond thought: Blessed are you, the God of our fathers. The human race has been deemed worthy of salvation through you, O most holy and God-beloved one; for you alone brought forth for us the Savior, whom we exalt above all for all ages. Dreadful is the manner of your delivery; for God, O Virgin, was the one born, having become incarnate; him you must entreat, that he may deliver from the dreadful punishment all who honor you with unwavering faith, O venerable and unwedded Mother.
*Ex canone in S. P. N. Niconem, die 23.*
The gate through which you, O Lord, have descended to us,
has mystically brought forth one born in a supernatural manner, the East, the Sun, and the Light, the God-man endowed with a dual nature. B The choir of martyrs imitated your slaughter, O Lord, when they recognized that you had sprung from an unwedded Virgin. C As one superior to every creature, the Creator loved you, O Virgin Mother, making you His Mother; you whom the throngs of athletes also beseech with every honor and veneration. You gave birth, O most immaculate one, to that Light without time, which is the splendor of the Father, having become subject to time through the riches of His goodness. B Recognizing you as the temple and living palace of God, the choir of triumphant martyrs beseeches you, O Lady, who alone among women took away the reproach. The Word of the Father dwelt in you without any corruption of your virginity, and drew to Himself the most celebrated choir of martyrs, who proclaim you the chaste Theotokos. Break the heavy burden of my evils, O most pure one, you who repaired the fall of Adam by your childbirth, O all-praised one, and illumine me, that I may be able to cry out with a pure mind: Bless the Lord, all you works! You appeared as the dwelling-place of Light, that is, of Him who was born of you for our sake; whom cease not to beseech that He may bathe in His light those who, O most chaste Virgin Mother, praise you and confess you to be the Theotokos.
From the canon for the Synaxis of the Archangel Gabriel, on the 26th.
