As soon as Gabriel saw you, chaste and lacking every stain, he cried out with a brilliant voice: Hail, Lady, who knows naught of the bridal chamber, the salvation of mortals, the glory and beauty of the angels. Recognizing the mystery hidden of old, O maiden, Gabriel once cried out to you: Hail, palace of God, in whom having dwelt, He who is merciful deifies all mortals. Having seen you wholly purified by the Holy Spirit, O most immaculate one, Gabriel cried out to you clearly: Hail, redemption from the curse, and the recall of our first parents. Being a temple of sanctification, O most undefiled one, through the voice of the Archangel Gabriel you conceived Him who rests among the saints, the most holy God, who sanctifies all and delivers them from evils. Obedient to the divine words of Gabriel, O chaste one, you brought forth in the flesh the eternal Word, who delivered the world from irrationality. Gabriel, the prince of the heavenly host, was sent to announce joy to you, O chaste Virgin Mother, through whom sorrow has truly ceased, and the curse has been made barren, and a blessing has blossomed for the faithful unto the ages. As the pleasant throne of the King, as
one excelling all creation, as she who alone brought forth the supersubstantial Essence, who through a most excellent union of an ineffable and strange generation deified mortals, let us hymn the blessed Virgin.
The radiance of the lightning of your birth shone forth and brightened the entire world, and destroyed the prince of darkness, O most pure Mother of God, the boast of angels and the salvation of all men, of those who continually glorify you with unceasing voices.
From the canon for our holy Father Hilarion the Younger, day 28.
Break the chains of my transgressions, O most pure one, interceding for me with your Son and God; and cast down the sin that tyrannizes me, O Ever-Virgin, that I may always honor you, O all-blameless one, as I am saved.
Heal the wounds of my soul, I entreat, and guide the movements of my mind toward the will of Him who was incarnate from you, O most pure Maiden.
The Lord made you Lady of all and Queen, O undefiled one, for from your womb He was incarnate, and He liberated His own creature from him who reigned over it.
You have become the strength and the firmament of the faithful and the holy, O intemerate one; for through you, to all, the fount of the most excellent goods has gushed forth, and to those dwelling on earth, the path to heaven has been opened.
The undefiled bridal chamber of God, the fire-formed throne of the Almighty, the Theotokos, let all generations of generations bless.
By symbols, the grace of the Spirit long ago prefigured you through prophetic charisms, calling you a rich and holy mountain, a saving gate, a most new volume, O chaste one, and an ark.
Cleanse me, O you most dear to God, from the filth of passions and the stain of sin, and open to me the doors of repentance, for I slip and continually encounter transgressions, O undefiled one, and provoke God to anger.
We bring to you the voice of Gabriel with rejoicing, saying: Hail, house of the Almighty, hail, glory of the holy and salvation of all the faithful, O Theotokos Ever-Virgin, through whom we have been deified.
From the canon for the holy Mark, bishop of Arethusa, day 29.
The shadowy mountain once illuminated the Prophet Habakkuk when he saw you, O Mother who knew no man, from whom God, having become embodied, appeared, covering with virtue, in truth, the heavenly things.
He who alone inhabits the heavens dwelt in your womb, O Virgin, by an excess of goodness, and was seen as flesh, born of you; but entreat Him, O most holy one, to deliver your servants from every adversity.
You who received without burning the fire of the Divinity, and
you who brought forth without seed the fountain of life, the Lord, O full of grace, Theotokos, preserve those who magnify you.
We who possess your protection, O immaculate one, and who are delivered from evils by your intercessions, and guarded in all things by the cross of your Son, all of us rightly and piously magnify you.
That mountain which the prophet Daniel beheld, from which the stone, Christ, was cut without hands, crushing the idols and casting down the pride of the demons, you are, O Virgin; therefore we glorify you.
Marveling at Him who was ineffably born of her, the all-pure one was struck with wonder, and magnified Him, and crying out said: "How do I hold you in my arms, my Son, you who hold all things?"
You have shown yourself to be the palace of God, O Lady, of Him who is King of all; whom you entreat to cleanse me, who have become a lodging-place for evil robbers, and to save me, O immaculate one.
My sloth, O Lady, and the heavy drowsiness that is in me, drive away by your sleepless and venerable petitions to God, O immaculate one, and have mercy on me who sing: "The praised God of our fathers and most glorious."
The nature of mortals, crushed by the ancient transgression, you have reformed above nature, and deified, O pure one, as it sings to your birth: "O all you works, bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages."
Spare your people, O Lord, and this inheritance of yours which you have acquired, being inclined by the prayers offered for us by her who bore you, the child of God, so that we may glorify you as Lord and all-merciful.
Ex canone in SS. martyres Jonam et Barachisium, die 29.
(Idem est cum superiori, et ideo omittimus.)
MENSIS APRILIS.
Ex canone in SS. martyres Theodulum et Agathopodem, die 4 (58**).
You conceived the Savior, Maker of all, and Lord, whom Agathopus together with the illustrious Theodulus preached as God and man, O Virgin Mother, most full of all blessedness. B Ex utero tuo, Deipara coruscans, exortus est, gloriosi mar- thyres salutare martyrii poculum lætantes biberunt. C O Mother of God, heal the very worst disease of my soul, you who produced the supreme Word, who makes all people good. Heal the passions of my soul, O most immaculate one, who brought forth the fountain of impassibility, and suppress the tyranny of those who constantly trouble and terrify my heart. When the Word, that Word which adorned the heavens with virtues, found you adorned with the splendor of virtues, O chaste one, He dwelt in you, O most pure one, and converted human nature into the heavenly. Without any change of His own nature, God truly assumed the whole man from you, O Lady, most full of divine grace; whose passion Theodulus and Agathopus representing, they cried out, constant and strong: "All you works, praise the Lord." By the brightness of your intimate piety, flood and illuminate me, who lie in the darkness of ignorance, O you who brought forth the unique Giver of light, and the Redeemer and Lord conceived in your womb, who has crowned the saints.
From the Canon to the holy martyrs Claudius, Diodorus, Victor, Victorinus, Papius, Nicephorus, and Serapion, on the 5th day.
In time, the Lord who is beyond time, having become incarnate from you, O Virgin, abolished the sins of men of many ages; implore Him earnestly that He may have mercy on our souls. You brought forth the Lord of all, O inviolate Virgin, to be celebrated with every praise, who delivered men from spiritual captivity. The prophet foresaw you intellectually, O venerable one, as a shaded mountain, from which the Lord truly shone forth in the likeness of flesh, that He might deliver the human race from corruption. You repaired the ruin of men, O Lady, having brought forth God the Word, who is able to restore to salvation those shattered and cast down. Strengthen the vigor of my soul, O most immaculate one, slackened by constant negligence and sin, that with faith and alacrity I may always sing your praises. We all praise you, O Virgin, as the most exalted throne of the Most High, and a golden lampstand, and an ark of sanctification, crying out: Blessed are you among women, O most inviolate one. Your wondrous birth-giving surpasses the grasp of the mind, O most graceful to God; for God, who is without beginning, accepted a beginning in time, in order to save those who cry out to Him with faith: Bless the Lord, all you works of the Lord. You who carried in your arms Christ, who took from you mortal flesh, implore Him, O most immaculate Virgin, that those who faithfully honor you and magnify you as Theotokos may attain immortality.
From the Canon to the holy and admirable Theodora, on the day (58***).
Heal the diseases and immoderate passions of my soul, O Virgin most dear to God, and save me, I pray, you who clothed the Savior and Lord with a body beyond the grasp of reason. We acknowledge you alone as the Mother of the Word, who shone forth from the Father before the ages without corruption, O unblemished spouse of God. Therefore we cry out to you: Hail, O blessed one. And we pray you to fill our souls with joy. Attracted by love of you, the illustrious Theodora is led after you, O Virgin, to the King incarnate from your womb, exulting with joy of soul. I am voluntarily enticed and snared by the fair appearance of evils, and I defile my soul; therefore divert me by your intercession, and save me, most pure one. O Lady, who brought forth the Lord, Light of Light, illuminate my soul laboring under the blindness of negligence and most grievous sins. Gathering and spinning thoughts like threads with joy, you wove a most beautiful garment for the Word from your own blood, O Virgin, which He shall wear forever. Slay our living sin, you who brought forth the truly living Life, O only pure and blessed Virgin, that we may praise you through all ages. With the light of your countenance illuminate me lying in the darkness of passions, O gate of spiritual light. Let not the night of death overtake and envelop me, O chaste Lady, by which the hope of my salvation might be utterly cut off.
From the Canon to the holy martyr Calliopius, on the 7th day.
He who created all things by His nod assumed a body from you ineffably, O Mother of God, He who crowned His martyr, the victor of the contest, with whom we ever faithfully call you blessed.
O most holy Virgin, glory of martyrs and ornament of the holy apostles, deliver from every distress by your intercessions those who joyfully celebrate you with praises.
As a fruit-bearing vine, O most immaculate one, you have produced a cluster from which divine must is pressed out for those who faithfully call you blessed.
Being delivered, O Virgin, from the fault of our progenitors through your mediation, together with the archangel Gabriel we cry to you, O all-immaculate one: Hail, the only salvation of all sinners; hail, the firmest strength of all martyrs.
Heal, O chaste one, the immense sins of my soul, and illuminate my mind, which is turned toward the constant darkness of all transgressions, so that I may dutifully call you blessed with praises.
The fruit of your venerable womb, O Mother of God, has brought us to life, who were dead and destroyed by fruit; therefore, praising you as is our duty, we cry out: Blessed is the God of our fathers.
You have given birth, O immaculate Virgin, having clothed in a body, and have carried in your arms, the Lord Jesus, who bears all things by His omnipotent nod; therefore, as Mother of God, we praise you, crying out in praise: Priests, bless; people, superexalt the Lord.
By the rays of your mystical light, O Mother of God, dispel the darkness of my mind, and calm the grievous storm of my thoughts, and lead me to tranquil harbors, O unique salvation of all, that I may with faith call you blessed.
From the canon for the holy apostles Herodion, Agabus, Rufus, Asyncritus, Phlegon, and Hermas, on the 8th.
O Mother of God endowed with compassion, glory of the apostles, ornament of the triumphant martyrs, and support of the faithful, confirm my mind, I pray, which is tossed about by the assaults of the seducer and obscured by the darkness of transgressions.
He who is inaccessible according to His divine substance has become accessible to me, O immaculate one; and through the assumption of flesh, He was wholly united to me, on account of His supreme mercy.
By a holy word you conceived the Word of the Father, O girl and Mother of God, who delivers men from every defect of rational discourse; hence we always magnificently glorify you with divine words.
You alone on earth had a strange offspring, who alone reconciled us to the Father, who alone is without beginning before every beginning; therefore we alone venerate you as the Mother of God.
The ark of the law prefigured you, who received the fullness of the divine law and gave birth in the flesh, and after the birth remained a perpetual virgin, just as you were before the birth, O Bride of God.
new Paradise, in which the tree of life is placed, you have become for us, O immaculate Virgin Mother of God; whose food...
restored to new life those who had fallen through food.
Having you as our protectress, O immaculate one, we your servants, and having you after God as an unashamed intercessor before your Son, save us from dangers and temptations, O venerable one, that we may always glorify you with faith and longing.
Like a flame-bearing pair of tongs, you received in your womb the spiritual coal, which burns up our passions, enlightens our souls, and dissolves the darkness of idolatry, O immaculate Virgin, worthy of many hymns.
From the Canon to the holy martyr Eupsychius, the one in Caesarea, day 9.
Born in the likeness of flesh from you, O Lady, the Master renewed our nature grown old, and made those who were mortal heavenly.
The choir of the athletes sings a hymn of thanksgiving to you, O venerable Lady, for under your leadership it achieved victory.
You who are higher than the heavenly powers, O Virgin, make my mind superior to fleshly passions.
Intercede for all those who have placed their hopes in you, O Mistress of all, that we may be delivered from future condemnation.
Raise me up, who have fallen completely, inasmuch as I opened the door to the passions, and by your most benign mediation lead me to the entrances of repentance, and save me, O you who gave birth to the Savior and Lord of all.
The prophet Daniel, inspired by the divine Spirit, called you a mountain, O Virgin, from which the stone, Christ, was cut without hands, and brought about the shattering of the idols of deceit.
O Virgin adorned with compassion, who gave birth to the Word filled with supreme compassion, have compassion on me who am void of compassion, who am desperate due to countless lapses, and who do not think of conversion, but rather spend my life in negligence.
Lighten me with the light of repentance, O Virgin, as I am darkened by the night of sin and covered over by the mist of negligence.
From the Canon to the holy martyrs Terentius, Pomponius, Maximus, etc., day 10.
I praise you, O Virgin, because you alone, worthy of all praise, made God incarnate from your precious blood, O all-holy one, and gave birth in a way beyond reason, dreadfully.
Save me, O you who gave birth to the all-good Lord, O chaste Mother, and calm the storm of my soul that is stirred up in many ways.
I, surrounded by temptations, call upon you, O all-immaculate Mistress, for help; hasten and save me, you who gave birth to the Word, the Savior.
He who delivers appeared, O immaculate one, your Son having become human, so that He might deliver all humans, O all-immaculate one.
Prefiguring you, the prophet Habakkuk foresaw you as a shadowy mountain...
covered with virtues, from which the Holy One, the God who is beyond speech, went forth from you, O Theotokos, having become incarnate, and he saved the world, which was being terribly troubled by the storm of grievous sin.
You, O Theotokos, who conceived Christ in your womb without defilement, have recalled to the ancient life those who once had flowed away, the progenitors of the human race, because of the transgression of an improper offense.
Bring to life my dead soul, raise up the fallen, heal my wounded soul, O most immaculate one, with the lance that pierced the divine side of the Savior who was incarnate from your womb, whom the children bless, the priests praise, and the peoples superexalt unto all ages.
Illumine, O gate of light, my soul, darkened and endangered by the grievous shadows of transgressions, and show me to be a participant of the divine day, that I may glorify you, O unfailing protection of the faithful.
*From the canon to the holy hieromartyr Antipas, bishop of Pergamum, day 11.*
With the flashes of your light, irradiate me, O most immaculate maiden, my heart that is detained in the night of passions and calamities; for you ineffably caused the Sun of justice to rise for all.
You have produced the Redeemer, O inviolate one, who liberated men from the captivity of the enemy; whence we religiously glorify you.
You were preserved after birth as you were before birth, O uncorrupted Virgin Mother; for you gave birth to the Creator of all, who willingly took on a human body from you.
That most divine Lord, who was in the form of God, dwelt in your womb, O most pure one, taking and bearing my form.
Holy is that Lord who dwelt in your womb, O Virgin maiden; and he rests in the saints, and glorifies those who, with true faith, O maiden, glorify him.
From your virginal blood the Word, co-eternal with the Father, has been made flesh, restoring our contrition; you are blessed among women, O most immaculate Lady.
As the Mother of the Creator of all, as the divine temple of the Almighty, as untilled earth that germinated the ear of grain without cultivation, save, O Virgin Mother, those who faithfully and always cry out: Bless, all you works, the Lord.
Light has risen for us, O maiden, from your light-bearing womb, the Creator of the sun, and of the stars, and of all creation, whom earnestly entreat to illumine those who hymn you.
*From the canon to the SS. and admirable Didymus and Photinus, day 12.*
The Creator, emptying himself entirely, as it pleased him, proceeded from your womb clothed in a human body.
O immaculate Lady, born of flesh, that he might cause the fountain of immortality to flow most abundantly for men.
We praise you, most holy Virgin, because you gave birth to Him who is assiduously glorified by all creatures.
You were made the throne of God, O most pure one, and a most brilliant palace, and a bed in which the Lord of all reclined, that he might awaken and relieve the first parent.
We magnify with perennial hymns the ready and prepared aid, the raising up of those who fall, the Mother of our God.
You shone forth from the paternal womb before the daystar, you who entered the most immaculate womb to assume a body.
From the Canon to St. Martin, Pope of Rome, day 13.
He who by his divine nature is invisible, was seen as an infant, having become a man from you, truly manifesting in one hypostasis two wills and operations; pray to him, O most immaculate one, that we all may be saved who lovingly revere you.
You gave birth to the Word, equal in honor and throne with the Father, bearing two operations and two wills, O all-holy Maiden.
You gave birth to the one of the Trinity known theanthropically in two substances, God and man simultaneously, bearing wills corresponding to your natures, O all-immaculate Virgin.
O Virgin who knew no man, who gave birth in the flesh to the uncircumscribable God, mortify the passions of my flesh; and quicken my soul which has been deadened by transgressions.
The laws of nature are dissolved in you; for you give birth ineffably to the Creator of all, O Mother of God worthy of all hymns, as God and mortal, possessing two wills and operations, O Mother-Virgin.
He who was born of you ineffably with two wills and two operations, O most immaculate one, preserves those who thus maintain the same mind, crying out: Blessed is the God of our fathers.
You have become holier than the hosts on high, and higher than the Cherubim, O Mother of God; therefore make me superior to the harmful passions. D 
Obedient to the voices of the Fathers, we faithfully confess the one of the Trinity born of you, O chaste one, in two substances and wills, and we magnify you, O Virgin.
From the Canon to the SS. Aristarchus, Pudens, and Trophimus, from the seventy disciples, day 14.
That he might unite those who were inferior now to those on high, God, because of the excess of his mercy, took flesh from you, O inviolate one, and remained what he was, even after the incarnation.
You nourish with milk the nourisher of the whole world, born without seed from your immaculate womb, who restored men crushed by the corruption of sin.
Since you are, O inviolate one, my strength and my protection, and an unassailable wall, and an intercessor before God, free me from the eternal flames of Gehenna. [(59*)]
Human nature, entirely sorrowful, you have renewed, O Virgin, by your new birth, with the laws of nature innovated by you beyond nature, O grace-filled Mother of the living God.
Free me from the flame of Gehenna, you who brought forth the unbearable light beyond the mind's conception, and kindle my soul with desire and affection for the knowledge of Him who came to cast fire upon the earth, O inviolate maiden, most full of divine grace.
From the Canon to St. Crescent the martyr, day 15.
The Lord is incarnate out of you by an excess of goodness, and for our sake, He who is by nature inaccessible appears as we are; him, O pure and all-blameless one, fervently entreat on our behalf. Let us honor with sacred hymns the only one among women who ineffably brought forth God, the Lady of all. She who supernaturally gave birth to the Creator of all creation, for the benefit of His own creature, the all-holy Lady, is worthily blessed. We praise you, through whom we were delivered from corruption, O all-praised Theotokos, and we cry to you: Hail, exultation of the martyrs. As the fire-formed throne of the Lord of all, we hymn you, O Maiden, and as a pleasant palace, and a lampstand, and a bridal chamber, and an all-holy, God-receiving table. C You have appeared holier than the Cherubim, O all-blameless one, having conceived the Word of the Father by the Word; Him we hymn and cry out: Blessed are you among women, O all-blameless Lady. O miracle! How have you brought forth God become man, O grace-favored one? How have you remained unburnt, having contained the fire that cannot be approached? Whence we glorify you with thankful voices and cry: All you works, etc. Light has dawned for us, O Maiden, from your light-bearing womb, the Creator of the sun and the moon, Christ the Lord; Him fervently entreat to illuminate our souls.
From the Canon to the holy women Agape, Irene, and Chionia, day 16.
You bring forth ineffably, O Lady, Him whom the Father begot without seed, and with your breasts you nourish Him who nourishes all things. Tear up the cruel bond of my transgressions, O Lady, you who by your seedless birth dissolved the chains of Hades. You brought forth the incarnate Lord of all creation, O Lady; Him entreat, O all-holy one, to deliver us from the enemy that tyrannizes us. Intercede for me, O Maiden, that a good end may come to me, that I may fear the everlasting punishments that await me, and be saved. Adam, casting off from himself the garments of death made of skin,
clothed has been with the robe of divine glory, glorifying thee with joy, as the Mother of God, immaculate in all things.
Mortify, O undefiled one, the sin that lives and kills my soul, and make me worthy to partake of the divine life, thou who didst bring forth joy and didst put to death the serpent.
The furnace of old, bearing the symbols of thy birth, O Virgin-Mother, did not burn the youths, just as the fire of the Godhead did not burn thy womb.
Lover of goodness, O Virgin, make good my soul which has been corrupted by sin, thou who didst bring forth the all-good Word.
From the Canon to the holy martyrs Symeon in Persia and those with him, day 17.
Thou bearest in thine arms, O Virgin, Him who bears all things, and thou nursest as an infant the Giver of milk; Him, therefore, entreat to have mercy on all thy people who faithfully hymn thee.
Thou hast delivered us from the curse of our ancestors with blessings, having given flesh to the Word who crowned all, O pure one always blessed, ornament of the victorious martyrs and forgiveness for those who sin.
From thee, the Sun of righteousness having risen beyond understanding, illumined the inhabited world, O Virgin full of divine grace, and dispelled the winter of error.
May I find thee, O Lady, freeing me in the hour of judgment from condemnation, I who faithfully glorify thy ineffable birth-giving.
From thee has risen, O all-holy one, the Creator, and with the rays of divine knowledge He has illumined those who were in the night of ignorance.
Heal, O all-immaculate one, the passions of my heart, calm the tumult that storms my mind, and save me as I cry: "Blessed art Thou, O God."
In order to signify thy venerable birth-giving, O all-pure one, the bush appeared unconsumed; for having received the divine fire into thy inwards, thou wert not consumed at all; therefore we hymn thee.
With most manifest flashes, O all-holy Mother of God, illumine my mind, [occupied by] the grievous darkness of ignorance;
that having attained divine illumination, I may proclaim thy great deeds, O Ever-Virgin.
From the Canon to Saint Acacius, Bishop of Melitene, day 17
Thou who in an arcane and ineffable manner gavest a body to God, and didst reconcile us, the rejected and cast away, to Him, O chaste one, worthy of all praise: heal, I beseech thee, the passions of my heart by the passion of thy Son, and save me who daily sing: For gloriously hast thou been glorified, etc.
O gate through whom no passage is open, open to me, O chaste one, the gates of repentance, and direct me in the straight paths.
Bring to life, O Lady, me who am dead; and him who has been led into error, quickly convert, thou who art the way, free from all error, and the guide of all.
He who in no way left the bosom of the Father, being superior to all substance, was seen to be contained in thy bosom as an infant, O Virgin, taking upon Himself my poverty, on account of the excess of the riches of His mercy.
Calm the shifts of my mind and the fluctuations of my heart, I pray, O Virgin, by thy mercy; and from the sin by which I am held bound, deliver me, who faithfully call thee blessed.
Te, as the cause of our salvation, all thy servants daily praise, O most dear to God, and with faith we call thee blessed, saying: O maiden, who art the fountain of incorruption, make me, corrupted by the inundations of many sins, worthy of thy healing, O Virgin.
Of that Light which illumined all things, thou hast truly appeared as a delightful propitiatory, O Virgin, all-luminous; therefore 101 illumine me, enveloped in the darkness of sins, that I might with faith magnify thee.
From the Canon to Saint Theodore the Martyr, day 19
He who, according to his nature, dwells in light inaccessible, when He had dwelt in thy womb, O most pure one, by His ineffable mercy made us inhabitants of Paradise, from which, on account of the envy of the serpent, we had been sent away and cast out.
He who according to his nature is free from time, born of thee in the likeness of flesh, was made under time, forgiving my temporal sins on account of His ineffable piety, O most immaculate one.
Without the pains of childbirth thou didst bring forth God, who was without a body, O maiden: who delivered Eve the first mother from the pains of childbirth, and redeemed from the pains of hell those who were living a life full of pains and miseries.
O most pure one, who alone art properly and truly the Mother of God, strengthen me, so that I may be able to master the passions of which I have become a slave, that, rejoicing with a free mind, I may call thee blessed, O salvation of the faithful.
Behold the holy mountain: behold the workshop of the aromatics of the spirit: behold the bridge which transports all to God, the maiden Mother of God; whom let us call blessed.
Be a propitiatory for me, O most unblemished one, to Him who was born of thee, obtaining for me the remission of grievous debts, and the divine entrance into the kingdom of God, and the fruition of delights, and fellowship with the light.
O depth of the ineffable mystery! He who once fashioned man with His hand is fashioned, assuming flesh, having entered the womb of the ever-Virgin, and He saves me, crying out with fear.
102 Illumine always the eyes of my soul, O Mother of God, lest the deepest darkness of sin should overtake me; and may the abyss of despair not swallow me: but do thou save me, and govern me, O defense of the faithful that is not confounded.
From the Canon to Saint Theodore, day 20
We, saved through thee, O maiden, name thee blessed in hymns as most immaculate among women and Mother of God, and we call out to thee as Gabriel did, Hail. Hail, O cause of the reformation of our first parents.
The people of the saints, recognizing thee as the most chaste maiden and Mother of God, O most holy one, have been irradiated by the light of thy splendor, and now in the heavens they pray to thee, glorifying with joy the Word risen from thee, O Mary bride of God.
Thy womb has been made the bridal chamber of immortality, O inviolate Virgin; from which, coming forth with splendor, the Bridegroom the Lord has drawn to Himself the peoples of the saints.
In the fearful hour of judgment save me and redeem me, O most holy one, and snatch me from Gehenna; that I may call thee blessed, and render thee honor with worthy praises, O most immaculate one.
Thou alone, O inviolate one, didst bring forth the subsistent Life, the Maker and Lord of all, whom the vast number of the holy Fathers, loving, passed on a pious and holy life.
As beautiful, as comely, the comely Word loved thee, O unblemished one, and inhabited thy womb, for the sake of our redemption, the faithful.
That bush points to thee, O most undefiled one, which, surrounded by fire, was in no part consumed; for indeed
MARIALE.] 
you bore the fire of divinity, which kept you, O Virgin, without being consumed, and after the birth shielded you as an incorrupt Virgin; do not cease to intercede for us.
103 Made beautiful by the ornaments of virtues, and encircled by the variety of golden fringes, O Virgin, [you bore] the Word, beautiful above all men.
From the Canon to St. Januarius and his companion martyrs, the 21st
Blessed is the people, O Mother of God, who glorifies you as the true Mother of God, and who always calls you blessed, O immaculate one, just as you foretold by sacred prophecy when you carried Christ within your womb.
Break the chains of my sins, O Spouse of God, you who shattered the bonds of hell by your birth-giving and filled all things with joy.
Let us magnify the only blessed one, through whom he who is superior to all goodness was incarnate from her, and truly and magnificently blessed all.
We praise you, O Mother of God, through whom the unsetting light dawned upon those who dwelt in darkness, that is, the Lord of all; and we glorify you with affection.
In order that he might show himself beneficial to men, God the Word received a body from your chaste blood, whom, O Mother of God, entreat earnestly for the salvation of our souls.
Mortify the impulses of my flesh, O inviolate one: do you who gave birth to life, quicken my soul, O chaste one, that has been killed by passions and many sins.
 He who ineffably dwelt in your womb made those who cultivate piety his dwelling place; to him we call out unceasingly: All you works, bless the Lord.
Illuminate my soul, which is blinded by the splendors of the light dwelling in you, O Maiden, and guide me by the hand, that I may walk the paths of salvation, and avoid the stumbling blocks of seduction and error, so that I may call you blessed with faith.
From the Canon to our Holy Father Theodore of Sykeon, the 22nd
That vine, which had no need of the laborer's work, blossomed from your womb, O most immaculate Virgin Mother; from which flowed the sweetness of indulgence and joy for all who, through the drunkenness of evils, had lost the sense of prudence.
The laws of nature are renewed in you, O Virgin; for you bear beyond reason the Lord, whom entreat earnestly for the salvation of our souls.
You have been shown to be blessed beyond all generations, O Virgin Mother, inviolate Lady, for you gave birth to Christ, who makes those who serve him blessed.
Irrigate with the drops of your mercy, O most undefiled one, my mind which is melting in the fire of sin; and light my extinguished lamp of the heart, O gate of light.
A tempest of passions disturbs me; the deep of despair stirs my heart: O Virgin, you who...
brought forth the Governor and Savior Christ, deliver me, I pray, and save me.
The beauty of Jacob, God chose you, O Virgin Mother of God; in you he dwelt, and after birth he preserved you a virgin, as you were before birth. The sacred voices of the prophets proclaim you, O Virgin, symbolically as the gate, the mountain, the tabernacle, and the holy cloud of light, from which the sun, Christ the giver of light, has risen upon those sitting in darkness and shadow. Revered is your birth-giving, O Deiparous Mother of God; therefore we call you blessed always, and faithfully we glorify you unto generations of generations, unto the ages. Amen.
From the Canon to our holy Mother Elizabeth the Wonderworker, on day 24.
Following with most ardent love you, O most pure one, who beyond the understanding of the mind brought forth the inseparable Word of God the Father, the celebrated Elizabeth became a receptacle of the Holy Spirit, shining with divine virtues.
Desiring in faith you alone, O most glorious Elizabeth, as the most pure temple of Virginity, O totally immaculate one, she rejoices, having been brought to your Son, following religiously in your footsteps.
You alone carry in your womb God incarnate, who grants existence to all; whom Elizabeth desired and loved from the heart, being spiritually betrothed to Him: O Virgin Mother of God, the miracle of angels and the wound of demons, totally admirable.
You have shown yourself superior to the supernal powers, O Virgin, having brought forth the Word that is co-eternal and co-equal with the Father; by whose radiance the God-bearing Elizabeth, being illuminated, dispersed the mists of the passions.
You conceived in your womb Him who is before the ages, O immaculate one; and you brought forth in the flesh Him who by nature is incorporeal; and with milk you nourished Him who feeds the universe, O Mother of God, unwedded and inviolate.
Behold my tribulation, O Virgin, which the multitude of my evils has brought upon me, and snatch me from the fire of Gehenna, as I cry out: Blessed, O most chaste one, is the fruit of your womb.
You brought forth clothed in a body, and carried in your arms, O inviolate Virgin, the Lord Jesus, who bears all things by His omnipotent nod; wherefore we praise you as the Mother of God, crying out with proclamations: Priests, bless; O people, superexalt the Lord.
Spare me, Savior, who having been born, preserved your Mother incorrupt after birth, when You shall sit to judge my works; overlooking my iniquities and my sins, as the most benign, compassionate, good, and lover of mankind.
From the Canon to the holy hieromartyr Basil, bishop of Amasea, on day 26.
The refuge of the faithful, O Ever-Virgin, the powerful help of those who flee to you, save us from every necessity and hostile harm.
You gave birth to the timeless King from yourself, Virgin-Mother, who received a beginning in time; entreat Him therefore, as a lover of mankind, to save your servants from all tribulation and from the conquest of enemies, O all-blameless one.
O all-praised one, ready help of men, calm the wild waves of temptations, saving your servants from the expectation of the enemy.
City of God, concerning which glorious things were spoken, deliver this your city and every region from dangers, from famine, and from the barbarians, O Theotokos Virgin, sole and unashamed protection of the faithful.
Most holy Virgin, Bride of God, who next to God are the protection of your servants, deliver us from barbarian conquest and from dangers.
The sole hope and help of the faithful, Mother of God, make haste, help your suppliants who are submerged in tribulations, and are in need, O Virgin, and exist in pain, and flee to you with confidence of soul.
Refuge of Christians, help of those who are held in distress, most holy Virgin, do not despise us who are always shaken by dangers and by the many incursions of the wicked barbarians.
Bearer of Light, Virgin, with the incorporeal angels, apostles, prophets, hierarchs, victors, and all the saints, entreat the only all-good God to deliver our souls from dangers.
From the Canon to the holy hieromartyr Simeon, kinsman of the Lord, on day 27.
As one who is higher than all creation, you held the Creator and God in your womb, O Virgin, and you gave birth for the redemption of mortals.
The whole law of encomiums is now defeated, O all-pure one, in singing your praises, O Bride of God, for you gave birth to the Word of God and have surpassed the angels.
Initiated in the mysteries of your childbearing, the prophet Habakkuk describes you, O maiden, as a shady mountain, from which our God came forth.
Intercede for us to Christ, who from your pure blood, O pure Theotokos, was clothed in material flesh and reformed mortals.
Heal the incurable passions of my soul, O Bride of God, you who gave birth to the Physician and Savior, who by His own passions cured the passions of men.
Pure Virgin-Mother, the wound of demons and the salvation of men, the beauty of angels, deliver my humble soul from the deception of the enemy.
That we may praise you with grateful voices, O pure one, who have filled our race with grace, protect and defend us, O Bride of God, from every harm.
Illumine me with divine light, O habitation of light, Virgin, dispelling the darkness of my passions and the truly deepest night by your intercessions, O Mother of God.
From the Canon to Saint Zosimas, Day 27
The Word, having become incarnate on earth without change, restored the dead to life; wherefore we, the faithful, proclaim you blessed with voices of thanksgiving, for through you, O most worthy of praises, we have been saved.
O incorrupt Virgin, O chaste one, you remained such after birth-giving, conceiving in an unthinkable manner Him who took away corruption; therefore do we all deservedly call you blessed, O Theotokos.
You have become a most lucid bridal chamber, a golden candelabrum in its entirety, a place of sanctification, the throne of the most high God, and a most spacious palace, O Virgin, overflowing with divine grace.
You were holier than the Cherubim, O most lauded one, when you inexplicably gave birth to God, who willed to save the human race, which had been corrupted and destroyed by the serpent’s guile.
You brought forth Life, O most chaste one, and you conceived and brought forth in an ineffable and unthinkable manner the Destroyer of death and Giver of life, O most chaste one.
Divine Law and the riddles of the prophets foretold you, O totally immaculate one, as one who was to bear Jesus Christ Emmanuel for the reconciliation, salvation, life, and redemption of all men.
Weighted by the slumber of negligence, a most profound sleep of sin has oppressed me; wherefore I cry to you, that by your ever-vigilant prayers you may awaken me to the light of repentance.
With a voice of thanksgiving we cry to you: Hail, pleasant and most holy tabernacle of God: 109 hail, salvation of the whole world: hail, O blessed one: hail, O removed from every stain, through whom we have been delivered from corruption and condemnation.
From the Canon to Saint Jason the Apostle, Day 28
To one who knew not a husband there appeared the Son, clothed in flesh because of His great mercy, He who cannot be comprehended by any reasoning of the mind, that He might manifestly reduce those who had miserably succumbed to the passions of the flesh to passionlessness through the passion of His own flesh, to whom we sing in the customary manner: For gloriously has He been glorified, etc.
Kill, O most pure one, through your life-giving intercession the sin that lives in me, you who gave birth to Life. O Lady, who knew not the bridal chamber, save me, having brought forth the Savior Word, and deliver me from perils and eternal condemnation.
You appeared holier than the Cherubim, when upon earth you clothed the Lord of all in a body, O inviolate Lady, most worthy of all praise.
As rain upon the fleece, the saving Word descended into your womb, and became man from you, that He might save me, O Maiden, through your mediation.
You who carried Christ in your arms, as a throne of fire, beseech Him, O most innocent one, as your Son and Lord, that He might bestow peace upon the world crying: Blessed is the God of our fathers.
The furnace, once symbolizing your birth-giving, O Virgin Mother, did not consume the youths, just as the fire of divinity did not consume your womb.
Having become the Mother of Emmanuel incarnate in your womb, you deified, O most inviolate one, human nature; therefore, O most holy Mother of God, we call you blessed.
From the Canon to Saint Memnon, Day 29
When God, because of His goodness, had assumed manhood from you, O immaculate Virgin, He proceeded with a dual operation and nature; Him, always entreat, that He might illumine those who praise you.
The Word of God dwelt in your unpolluted womb, O inviolate one, and took away all the sins of men.
Confirm my soul, which is plunged into the depth of carnal pleasures, I pray you, through your intercession, O Mother of God, who alone brought forth God, the Giver of all good things.
You brought forth God, and remained a virgin, O Bride of God; therefore all the tongues of men call you blessed with joy.
Mortify, O Virgin, the prudence of my flesh, which ...
Free me from the tempests of measureless sins, O Maiden, who alone are a most strong help for the miserable, and an altar of propitiation for sins, O blessed among women, most pure Lady.
Make my wretched soul, languishing and in danger from most grievous evils, worthy, O Lady, most dear to God, of your visitation, and restore to it entire soundness, while it cries out.
With the voice of the archangel we cry to you rejoicing, O Virgin: Hail, solution of the curse, glory of the holy confessors, exultation of the Fathers, preaching of the prophets, and salvation of men.
MONTH OF MAY
From the Canon to the holy martyrs Timothy and Maura, Day 3
The supersubstantial Word, having become substance from pure blood...
has deified us and delivered us from corruption, O pure One; therefore we faithfully glorify you forever.
Your Son, O Virgin, who is by nature impassible, took flesh from your pure blood and, by the passion of the cross, delivered me from the passions, O undefiled One.
Tabernacle of purity, domicile of the Lord of all, resounding echo of all the prophets, temple most acceptable to God, have mercy on those who praise you.
Stil the storm of my thoughts, the uprisings of the passions, and the surging swell of temptations, O Virgin full of divine grace, and save me as I praise your wonders.
All-good Lady, who in the flesh gave birth to the all-good God, make my soul, now corrupted by passions, good, so that with faith and longing I may magnify you.
O super-laudable Virgin, who gave birth to the super-laudable God, make those who praise you participants of the light, and by your intercessions deliver them from Gehenna, from the flame, and from every injury of the enemy.
You were made beautiful, O Virgin, when you gave birth to Christ the Lord, most beautiful in form, who illuminates the faithful with divine splendors, whom we superexalt.
Illumine me with your light, I pray, O Virgin most dear to God among all women, and redeem me from the eternal fire, so that I may magnify you, that I may glorify you, that as is due I may hymn your wonders.
From the Canon for the Holy Apostle Andronicus and Junia, Day 17
Rain down upon me, O Virgin, the redemption of all my transgressions and the amendment of my life, through your mediation and grace.
There is no one undefiled except for you, O Lady, and no B C [Note: Note 61 and the accompanying text constitute a scholarly excursus on the Council of Trent and the doctrine of the Immaculate Conception, which interrupts the liturgical text. As indicated in the instructions, the substantive content is:]
61) Concerning the title "Immaculate" added to the Virgin, it seems that it can be argued from the Council of Trent, which in Session V, at the end of the Decree concerning original sin, affixed the epithet "Immaculate" to the Blessed Virgin, so that we might perhaps understand this title to be proper to the mystery of the conception, and recognize that in the appellation of the "Immaculate Virgin" an "immaculate conception" is included. "This holy synod declares," it says, "that it is not its intention to include in this Decree, where the topic is original sin, the blessed and immaculate Virgin Mary, Mother of God." Concerning this declaration, the *Armamentarium Seraphicum* says (under the title "Immaculate Conception," page 150): "I do not necessarily include the Blessed Virgin Mary in the common law of sin, but I teach by example that she is piously called 'immaculate' by the faithful as being free from all stain." This intention of the Council is greatly illustrated by Session VI, Canon 23: "If anyone shall say that a man once justified can avoid all sins throughout his whole life, even venial ones, except by a special privilege of God, as the Church holds concerning the Blessed Virgin, let him be anathema." Here, the title "immaculate" is not heard, because purity from all actual sin is not sufficient for a person to be named "immaculate" in the full breadth of the term and by excellence; yet if she is not included under the law of original sin, she may most excellently be distinguished by such a title without any limitation. No one versed in the actions of the Council can suspect that the title "immaculate," expressed there and omitted here, was absent without mature counsel and some singular mystery, since it is known from the writings of the Fathers who attended the Council that the canons and decrees were crafted by the most experienced delegates in congregations and subjected to such a strict examination that, for the placement of a single word, or even one jot, they were often returned to the anvil of the delegates until they deserved to be approved by common judgment. This diligence, if ever elsewhere, must be admitted to have been applied most exquisitely in the article concerning the conception of the Virgin, with the controversy raging and the defenders of both opinions present. If, therefore, the title of "immaculate" is attributed to the Virgin for some great cause, while it was being declared in the general rule that she was not necessarily included in the contraction of original sin, and omitted when she was being established as a certain dogma of the Church that she was free from all venial sins, then either this cause must be assigned, or it must be granted that the cause brought forward by us is true, namely, that by the title of "immaculate" added to the Virgin, there is expressed (as I judge) her immaculate conception.
there is no one blameless besides thee, O all-pure; for thou alone hast been the dwelling-place of the God of all.
Thee always, O Virgin Deipara, do we all the faithful with one voice praise, as a most secure and most fit bulwark for the defense, and the redemption of our souls.
Thee, O most holy Maiden, the choir of the prophets prefigured in holy symbols as she who would be the Mother of God of the Lord.
The divine entrances of the Lord into thee, O innupta, who requested flesh from thee and enriched the faithful, have become known.
O Lord, who didst dwell in the womb of the Virgin, and didst in her refashion Adam, blessed art thou unto the ages.
As with tongs thou bearest the coal in thy hands, O Virgin, which pours forth divine dew upon those who are endangered in the fire of error, while it burns up the passions of those who celebrate his kingdom with praises.
O Virgin immaculate, pure from every stain, who hast brought forth the light, petition for light, and for the remission of sins, and the salvation of souls for those who acknowledge thee to be the true Deipara, O undefiled Virgin all-pure.
From the Canon on the Feast of the holy martyrs Peter, Dionysius, and those with them, day 18.
As a throne of the king, in which he sat, we venerate thee, O Virgin, who hast prepared a heavenly seat for the faithful, and we bless thee with affection.
Thou alone remainest a Virgin while bringing forth, thou alone wast recognized as the true minister of the greatest mystery when thou didst bring forth God, O Deipara Mother Virgin.
O most praised Virgin Mother of God, save those who praise thee, who trust in thee, from every surrounding danger and tribulation.
O Bride of Christ, unwedded, through whom, having been freed from the ancient debt, we have been made sons by grace of the heavenly Father, protect those who praise thee.
As a fruit-bearing field, thou hast sprouted forth the ear of life, O Deipara, by which the faithful are nourished, and the famine of error is truly driven from the earth.
The ark of God, the urn of the divine manna, the golden lampstand and the table, the holy mountain, the Deipara let us all faithfully praise.
You have become a spiritual propitiatory, receiving the prayers of all, and you offer them, O all-pure one, to your Son for the ransom of those who chant: "Bless the Lord, all you works."
Gladly do we faithful offer to you the voice of the angel, O Bride of God. Hail, help of mankind, strength of martyrs and apostles, and echo of all the prophets, O all-blameless Mother of God.
From the Canon for the holy martyr Thallelaeus, day 20.
Virgin Mother of the Lord, boast of the pious, joy of the angels, salvation of Christians, expiation for those who sin, bridge leading the faithful from earth to heaven, save your servants.
Irradiate me, O Virgin, with the light of repentance; for I lie in the darkness of sin due to my own folly; and grant me the remission of my transgressions, that I may glorify you, O devoid of every stain.
The holy prophets once proclaimed your child-bearing, calling you a great and shady mountain, and a gate through which the Lord alone passed, O only pure one.
You have made those darkened by passions to be sons of light, having given birth to Christ the Giver of Light, the radiance of the Father, O all-holy Lady; therefore, with longing we call you blessed.
You have loosed me from the bonds of sin, having brought forth the Lord, who loosed the bonds of Hades, O Theotokos, and who gathers all toward the knowledge of himself.
For our aid, O Maiden full of God’s grace, we beseech you clearly: arise and deliver us from eternal temptations and every threat.
Ask for me, O all-holy and pure one, the propitiation of my transgressions, and stretch out your hand to me, who am severely tossed on the sea of terrors, that I may call you blessed, that I may faithfully proclaim your steadfast protection.
You have become a vessel of light, O Virgin, and a throne of the King of all, O immaculate one; seated upon which, He raised us from our ancient fall, and by His divine session honored those who in faith and longing magnify you.
From the Canon for the holy martyr Basiliscus, day 22.
Gideon foresaw your immaculate womb as a fleece, O Virgin Maiden, receiving the heavenly dew, drying up the sea of ungodliness, O Maiden, and watering minds that were melting [with desire].
May I find you, O all-pure one, always guiding me toward virtues and leading me into the paths of repentance.
Co-essential with the Father, He appeared in all things like unto men, having become incarnate, as He was pleased, from your blood, O all-blameless one.
In the likeness of flesh you brought forth, O Theotokos, the Lord who is incomprehensible and uncircumscribed.
The contrite fractures of my wretched soul, and the lingering
passions, O Virgin, heal, for you brought forth the Physician of souls and bodies in an ineffable manner; and save me, O most immaculate one, who have placed all my hopes in you.
Behold the Virgin, whom the great Isaiah foretold in the Spirit; she conceived God in her womb and brought Him forth, to whom we sweetly sing: O Lord God, blessed are You.
You appeared wider than the heavens, O wholly-holy Maiden, containing in your womb God, who delivered those who sing to Him from the wicked straits; praise the Lord, and supremely exalt Him throughout all ages.
By nature You are God; yet You endured to be clothed in human nature, having willingly entered an immaculate womb, O Lover of mankind; wherefore, recognizing in You two natural wills, we magnify You, faithfully calling Your Mother blessed.
From the Canon for the feast of the holy Apostle Carpus, day 26.
Giving birth in an ineffable manner, O Virgin, and renewing the laws of nature, you have become a Mother and ever-Virgin; therefore we call you blessed.
As a new child, you brought forth Him who before the ages shone forth ineffably from the Father, O Theotokos; therefore we glorify you.
Spiritually, O Theotokos, the God-bearing prophet saw you as a great and shaded mountain, O Maiden, from which our God came forth in the flesh.
From the defilements of mind and body, cleanse me now, O blessed one, by your merciful nod and inclination, that I may praise and magnify you as is due, O most worthy of all praise.
You brought forth the Creator without pain, O most immaculate one, for He takes away our pains and labors, and makes the human race worthy of delights devoid of all pain.
As one wider than the heavens, O Virgin, you received in your womb the Word who can be contained by nothing, and who redeems the human race from every distress.
You became a heaven, O Theotokos, from which has dawned upon us the Sun of righteousness, who illuminates us with the light of knowledge, O pure Theotokos.
We offer you the voice of Gabriel, O Virgin, crying out: Hail, light cloud; hail, earth untilled, which brought forth the beautiful ear of grain, the Nourisher of all creation.
From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyr Eutychius, day 28.
Having appeared in the likeness of flesh, the Lover of mankind, born of you, O most immaculate one, saved the world that was perishing and subjected to error; therefore we honor and call you blessed.
The darkness of my mind, O Theotokos, with the light that is in you, as the gracious one, I implore you to dissipate; and intercede for me, that through ways of repentance I may be improved, so that with faith I may glorify you.
The assembly of the prophets wrote beforehand that you are the scroll, O immaculate Virgin, betrothed to God, in which the Word of the Father was written by His finger, describing the faithful in the book of life, O Bride of God.
Having been rendered lifeless by passions and thoughts, O all-immaculate one, I flee to your mercies, I run to your fervent protection and aid, O Lady, solely glorified by God, make me alive, save me.
Become a harbor for me, O all-immaculate one, guiding me to the haven of salvation as I sail the waves of this present life, and deliver me from the scandals of the adversary.
The incomprehensible Son, sitting in the bosom of the Father, sits as an infant in your bosom, O pure one, for our recall, to whom we cry out: O Lord and God of the fathers, blessed are you.
You joined that which was once divided, O God-graced Virgin, by your birth-giving; therefore, as the cause of all good things, we call you blessed, crying out with uprightness of soul: Praise the Lord, you works.
Illumine, O chaste one, the eyes of my soul; calm the storm arising from the disturbance of the demons, and direct toward the way of Christ’s commandments the stress of my mind, O all-pure one, so that in faith I may ever call you blessed.
*From the Canon to the holy martyr Hermylus, day 31.*
O holy Virgin, Mother of Christ, glory of the martyrs and joy of the angels, together with them, as a suppliant, entreat your Son to have mercy and save your servants.
With mouth and tongue I confess you to be the all-holy temple of God, O all-chaste one; therefore deliver me from every punishment.
O all-praised Lady, you gave birth in an ineffable manner to Him who rests in the saints; for this reason we honor you with hymns.
The prophet of old saw you in the Spirit as an intellectual lampstand possessing the lamp, Christ the Lord, who with ineffable light illuminates us all, those who faithfully honor you, O all-immaculate one.
*Ex Canone in SS. Theodulum, ac Therapondem, die 28.*
The most sacred choir of prophets foretold from afar that you would be truly the Mother of God, O Virgin, higher than the Cherubim and human creatures.
The secret and inscrutable depth of your birth-giving no human intellect can follow in any way, O Augusta; for God, emptying Himself for the sake of His own mercy in your womb, fashioned me entirely anew.
As a gate leading to the divine entrance, as another Paradise, as an intellectual place of sanctification, as the dream of Jacob, let us call the Virgin blessed.
After the awesome birth-giving, O Virgin, you remained as you were before; for it was God who was being born, who changes all things by His will, O unwedded Mary, most full of divine grace.
The Word within your womb became a body without seed, appearing as perfect man, renewing natures as it befitted God, as He alone knew, O gate most dear to God, immune from every stain.
He who sits in the bosom of the Father in an uncircumscribed manner, now resides in your bosom, O undefiled one, in a circumscribed manner, garbed in your form, for the salvation of Adam made the new Adam.
Redeemed from the ancient curse by your birth-giving, O Maiden filled with every blessing and most full of divine grace, we send up to you the voice of Gabriel: Hail, cause of the salvation of all.
By your light illumine me, I pray, O Virgin most pleasing to God among women, and redeem me from the eternal fire, that I may magnify you, that I may glorify you, that with due praises I may extol your great deeds.
*From the Canon in the feast of the Holy Martyr Hermylus, day 31.*
O holy Virgin, Mother of Christ, glory of the martyrs and joy of the angels, together with them, as a suppliant, pray to your Son that He may have mercy and save your servants.
With mouth and tongue I confess you to be the most holy temple of God, O totally chaste one; therefore deliver me from every torture.
O Lady, superior to all praise, you gave birth in an ineffable manner to Him who rests in the saints; therefore we venerate you with praises.
Long ago, O Maiden, the prophet in the Spirit saw you as an intellectual lampstand having the lamp, Christ the Lord, who bathes us all in ineffable light, we who faithfully honor you, O most immaculate one.
You nourish in a manner befitting God Him who nourishes all things by His nod, holding and embracing in your arms, O most pure Lady, Him who contains all things: wherefore we faithfully glorify you as is our duty.
You were made beautiful, O Virgin, having given birth to the most beautiful in form, Christ, who became like us, and refashioned all who were crushed unto life: whence we faithfully glorify you always with hymns.
You were seen as wider than the heavens, having contained God in your womb, whom always entreat to deliver me now from the sin which restricts me, O Virgin, so that, being expanded by works of piety, I may faithfully call you blessed.
He who fashioned me, God, proceeded from you; He clothes me in the garment of incorruption, when I had been stripped of the divine robe on account of my wicked thoughts; O Mother of God, Lady, refuge of all men, wall of the crown-bearing martyrs, and fortress by which they are crowned, and exultation of the angels.
120 MENSIS JUNIUS.
From the Canon on the feast of Saint Dorotheus the martyr, bishop of Tyre, on the 5th day.
Rain down upon me, O Virgin, I pray, a drop of compunction, which may wash away the filth clinging to me, so that I may glorify you.
Illumine my whole heart with divine light, O gate of light, driving away the darkness of sin.
Save me from temptations, and from the soul-destroying storm of life, so that with faith I may call you blessed, O most holy Girl, Mother-Virgin.
You became the rising of the Sun that shone forth before the morning star, through whom those who were in the darkness of evils, O immaculate one, beheld the light.
Entreat Him, O Virgin, whom you bore as God become man, that He may deliver me from fire and torment.
O Mother of God, snatch my wretched soul from the bonds of sin; and through the perfect charity of Christ, render it free, so that I, O Mother of God, may faithfully glorify you unto the ages.
You were made most beautiful, O Virgin, conceiving and bearing in your womb the most beautiful Word, to whom we sing: Bless the Lord, all you works.
O pure one, who bore in your hands Christ, who bears all things by His divine nod; assiduously entreat the same, that He may direct the lifting up of our hands as incense in His sight.
121
From the Canon on the feast of Saint Theodotus of Ancyra, the martyr, on the 7th day.
By an excess of mercy, the Son of God inclined the heavens, and descended, and was incarnate of you, O chaste one, that He might save men from the seduction of the serpent.
The choir of divinely-speaking prophets, having beheld from afar the depth of your mystery, with multiform voices preached you as the chaste Mother of God, O most chaste Spouse of God.
Since the Creator had preserved you after the birth as a virgin incorrupt, just as you were before the birth, He dwelt in your womb,
and as one full of mercy, He restored and renewed those who had been corrupted by the deceit of the devil.
The true Word of the Father, having been embodied from your venerable blood, O chaste Virgin, you brought forth in two perfect natures, but in one hypostasis, O most dear to God.
He who is truly beyond all creation that can be understood or seen, truly entered your womb and became flesh, in order to reform mankind, O perpetual Virgin.
You gave birth to the Word, who bears one hypostasis, O Mother-Virgin, while He possesses in a manifest way two wills and His natural properties; for He who was incarnate for our sake is both God and man.
An eloquent and learned tongue cannot express the ineffable depth of your mystery; for you brought forth the Word of God, who is beyond words, O most chaste Virgin, for the salvation of all.
Through the voice of the angel, you brought forth the Word without beginning, who took on flesh endowed with mind and soul, O most holy Virgin, from your pure blood, and He defeated the bodiless enemies and saved us all who confess you to be the true Theotokos.
From the Canon for the Holy Martyrs Alexander and Antonina, day 10
He who created as God the invisible powers by His decree, had you as the cause of our reformation, O Virgin. Therefore, entreat Him, O most immaculate one, for the salvation of the world.
Having brought forth God, you appeared as a Virgin after the birth, O undefiled one; and now choirs of virgins entreat your divine countenance, with whom you should ask for us propitiation and mercy, and total liberation from terrible things.
Because she had you, O all-praiseworthy one, as her strength and support, Antonina endured harsh and severe tortures; she cast down the tyrant and trampled him with her beautiful feet, by the grace of that Word who shone forth from your womb.
Cast down the demons who are always warring against me, and make their counsel of no effect, O undefiled one, saving me, O Maiden, from their expectation, so that I may always call you blessed.
I have an- soul deadened by transgressions; visit and vivify me, you who brought forth Life, Christ, whom the illustrious and great martyrs confessed to be the God of all, O Virgin Mother.
Just as the Chaldean furnace did not burn the three youths, so, O inviolate one, the fire of the Godhead kept your womb unburned. But I cry out to you: Burn up the bitter forest of my passions, O chaste one, that I may glorify you.
Without the experience of man you brought forth God, who became like us, O Virgin, whom you should supplicate assiduously, O one free from every stain, that He may save those who cry out: Bless the Lord, all you works.
Make light to arise for me now, most pure one, as I lie in the darkness of sloth, dissolving the clouds that blind my mind, and granting ever-deepening peace to my soul, O all-blameless one, that I may glorify you.
From the Canon for the Holy Martyr Acylina, on the 13th day.
He who is understood together with the Father, who is without beginning, entered your womb and became man, O Maria, betrothed to God, and saved us who had succumbed to malice and had been enslaved by the deception of the enemy; therefore, we glorify you with faith and longing.
We know you, O chaste one, to be an unwedded bride and the pure tabernacle of the Creator, and more holy than the Cherubim.
The sleep of sin has weighed me down in the drowsiness of negligence; by your wakeful intercession, raise me up to repentance.
Redeemed, all of us, from the condemnation of our first parents through your offspring, we cry out to you: Hail, full of grace, most worthy of all praise.
That God might become man, God was seen by men, O Virgin, having been born inexplicably from your womb, remaining what He was without any change.
You have brought forth Him who redeemed us from all corruption; therefore, we all glorify you, O Virgin.
We cry out to you with the voice of the angel, O most chaste one: Hail, salvation of all men, and divine crown of the most glorious martyrs.
From the Canon for the Holy and Wonderworking Tychon, on the 16th day.
You raised us up, O chaste one, who had fallen into the depths of perdition, by bearing Christ, O pure one, from your immaculate womb.
From the Canon for the Holy Martyrs Meletius, Stephen, and John, on the 10th day.
O most immaculate one, you who brought forth Life, transform the tempest of the passions into tranquility, and be my helper, rescuing me from the dangers of this life.
Lift me up now, as I am stuck in the mire of sin, O Bride of God, sole Theotokos, and direct me toward dispassion as I fervently cry out, etc.
That bush which was once shown to Moses as it burned and was not consumed prefigured you; for truly, O most chaste one, you bore the fire of the divinity, which consumed you in no part; to Him we cry with faith: Bless the Lord, you children, etc.
O Virgin, lover of all that is good, who brought forth the good Lord and Master, make my soul, now corrupted by a multitude of evils, good, just as you are good, and free it from the hardness by which it is now held, by your prayers, that it may magnify you without ceasing.
As God became man, God was seen by men, O Virgin, born of your womb by an inexplicable reason, and He remained what He was without any change.
You brought forth, O Virgin, Him who redeemed us from all corruption; therefore, we all glorify you.
With the voice of the angel, O most chaste one, we cry to you: Hail, salvation of all men, and divine crown of the most glorious martyrs.
Since you possess such confidence, entreat Him whom you brought forth from your womb, that He may free your servants from perils.
You brought forth the One of the Trinity, O most pure one, who restored us who had been previously crushed by the malice of the warring serpent. Me, caught in sloth and totally darkened by the blackness of passions, and serving sin—do you, who gave birth to the sinless Word, enlighten and guide to life.
Appear as a deliverer of your servants, O immaculate one, from the invasion of enemies and the incursion of the Barbarians, for they possess you as a mighty defense and an unashamed intercession.
O holy Virgin, make my soul healthy, which the enemy has craftily stained with sin, as you are good, I beseech you; and illuminate it with your light. You have appeared superior to all incorporeal spirits, as you are truly the Mother of God, whom, O Virgin, I beseech to make my mind superior to carnal pleasures.
Priests and people celebrate you, O all-blessed and most pure maiden, who have crowned all with blessings, singing with faith: Bless and praise the Lord.
Your most holy womb has become the dwelling place of light, O most pure one, by which being enlightened, we are redeemed from the darkness of error, singing your praises and with true longing calling you blessed, the only restoration of men.
From the Canon for the Holy Apostle Jude, day 19.
Let faith alone, and not demonstration, be the guide to your miracles which are beyond the mind, O Mother of God, all-pure one, the incomprehensible...
126
From the Canon for Saint Fortunatus the martyr, day 19.
You were the sunrise, O most immaculate one, at the sunset of our nature, because of the kindness of the Sun of righteousness, who appeared. Begetting, O Virgin, Him who is coeternal with the Father, you also brought forth the One who became like men, the ornament of the apostles and the crown of the martyrs. Through you, the unsetting Sun shone upon us, O Maiden Mother of God, who were sitting in the shadow of death. Clothed in a body, He appeared from you, O inviolate one, God who was immune to flesh, so that by His passion He might free all from carnal passions, who with faith assiduously call you blessed. Break, O maiden Virgin, the chains of my sins, and by your illumination brighten my dark mind, O salvation of the faithful.
When Adam had died because of the transgression of the precept imposed by the Creator, he was most truly recalled to life by your life-giving birth, and received back the dwelling of paradise, singing: Blessed are you, who brought forth God in the flesh. You truly brought forth for us on earth a new Child, O pure one, who before all ages was born ineffably from the eternal Father, O inviolate one; and He recalled us, aged by corruption, to newness. You carry Him who carries all by His divine power; and you nourish from your breasts, O most chaste one, Him who nourishes everything in which is the spirit of life. Your miracle, superior to all thought, strikes angels and men with amazement, who celebrate you with perpetual praises and with affection call you blessed.
From the Canon for the feast of the holy Apostle Jude, day 19.
Let faith alone, and not demonstration, be the guide to your miracles which are beyond all mind, O...
most holy Mother of God: you have brought forth the Word of God, who is incomprehensible, clothed in human flesh.
Behold, you, O chaste one, have been filled with grace above all; you have surpassed all in holiness, you have transcended all; you have appeared clearly as more exalted than all the heavenly powers, having become the Mother of God.
Having ineffably conceived your Maker and your God, O most tender one, entreat him to keep us unharmed from dangers, and to grant the salvation of their souls to those who praise you, O Lady.
Mortify my passions, O Mother of God; and raise up my soul, which has been destroyed by the bite of sin, O Mother of the true Resurrection.
Most holy Lady Theotokos, deliver me from corruption, and quiet the tumult of the passions, you who have brought forth the source of dispassion.
With mouth and mind we all proclaim you Theotokos, O all-chaste one; for you have given birth to God, to whom we all sing: Blessed are you, O God.
Come, let us honor the beauty of Jacob, Mary the immaculate, crying out in unison: All you works, praise and superexalt the Lord.
As having brought forth the Maker of all creatures, O most chaste one, you bear the rule over everything created, possessing an incomparable and preeminent excellence; wherefore, adoring your offspring, we glorify you.
From the Canon for the holy hieromartyr Eusebius, bishop of Samosata, day 22.
O blessed one, who gave birth to God, bless now, O immaculate one, those who bless you, and fill them with divine virtues, and grant strength to sing to those who chant to the Lord, saying: For he has been gloriously glorified, etc.
By the will of the Father, with the coming of the Holy Spirit, you brought forth the Word, O most holy Mother-Virgin, the glory of priests; wherefore we celebrate you with hymns.
With mouth, and tongue, and heart, I confess you, O chaste one, as Mother of the Creator, and I beseech you, enlighten my soul, which is covered in the darkness of transgressions.
You are known as the enlightening candelabra, O Mother of God, bearing the divine lamp which illuminates all the ends of the earth.
Perceiving the infinite depth of your mystery, O maiden, the god-speaking prophets clearly foreshowed this, by riddles and divine predictions. For you, O chaste one, gave bodily form to the Word of the Father, who is beyond words.
You renew the laws of nature, O Virgin, by your birth-giving in a paradoxical manner, and you refashion us who were corrupted by the most evil transgression; wherefore we praise you as is our duty.
As one higher than the divine heights, you brought forth the Most High Word, O most laudable one; who exalted from the earth the substance of men which had fallen.
O Virgin who loves what is good, make my soul good.
Ex Canone in festo S. Michaelis archangeli, die 22 (64*)
O Virgin, to be celebrated with every praise, adornment of angels, help of men, assist me who am tossed on a surging sea and constantly shaken and endangered by the tempest of sins.
He who created immaterial minds by His own will, voluntarily dwelt in your material womb, O most pure from every stain; when He who was invisible was seen in the flesh.
The paradox of your birth-giving, O Virgin, the master of sacred mysteries once signified intellectually, seeing in the spirit the shadowy mountain most manifest, from which came the holy God incarnate.
God showed you to be more sublime than the intellectual angels, entering into your womb, O inviolate one, and immune from every spot: whom intercede with assiduous prayers for the salvation of our souls.
Blessed is the people who always blesses you, O blessed one, who brought forth the blessed God, who because of His mercy deified men by an ineffable union.
Seeing the eternal Word of the great Mind inhabiting you truly, O maiden, the archangel Gabriel ineffably and stupendously cried out: Hail, throne of the Most High, O blessed one.
The divine archangel, the mediator of nuptials, standing, cried out to you: Hail, O unblemished Bride of God, glory of angels, salvation of men, and bulwark.
At the voice of the angel Gabriel, you conceived, O all-sinless one, God the Word, who by a word created the heavenly hosts, and provides the word by which we can praise His holy humiliation and condescension, which is above every word and thought.
Ex Canone in Festo S. Patris David Thessalonicensis, die 26
You have appeared adorned with the beauty of virtues, and you brought forth, O Virgin, the beautiful Christ, who has adorned men with the beautiful splendors of divinity, O ever-virgin.
You have appeared more honorable than the angels, having brought forth, O Virgin, Him who created them; wherefore I beseech you, O pure one, sanctify my mind and enlighten my heart, driving away the clouds of passions.
We praise you, O most laudable Lady, who ineffably brought forth the supremely laudable God, you who have surpassed the choirs of angels in beauty incomparably.
Direct my life and the movements of my mind, O pure Virgin, toward the divine counsel of Him who in an inexplicable manner proceeded from you to us.
From your most pure blood was woven flesh, in a manner above nature, for Him who created man, O Theotokos; wherefore we worthily praise you.
By your birth-giving the human race is freed from the curse, O only all-blessed one; therefore we glorify you as full of grace, O Theotokos, unto the ages.
We honor you as the beauty of Jacob, whom God loved, whom He chose, altogether as the only pure and blessed one do we hymn you unto all the ages.
Ezekiel foresaw you as a light-bearing gate, through which passed the true light, Christ our God, whom earnestly entreat, O pure one, that I pray He may open to me the gates of repentance.
Ex Canone in festo S. P. Sampsonis Xenodochi, die 27
Thee, the ineffable Genitrix of God, as a most powerful defense for all who through labor are
moved, we glorify unceasingly, and we call blessed, O most pure one.
Dispel the shadows of my soul and mind, O pure one, and grant that I may walk and live honestly as in the day, and follow Thy saving commandments.
Thee, O all-pure Lady, the luminous palace of the Word, we sing with hymns and call blessed.
Thee, O most holy, chaste one, the beauty of Jacob, we praise with the divine voices of faith, for Thou didst bear for us God clothed in flesh, before whom all things tremble.
Thou hast become a high heaven of the all-king God, O all-blameless one, and a pure palace, and a bridal chamber glistening with divine grace. B 
The fleece once foreshadowed Thy most chaste womb, O venerable one, which received in itself the divine dew sprinkling all who labor with the thirst of sin, O worthy of all praise and blessed one, who didst bear God in the flesh.
Still now the grave tempest of my passions, O chaste and blessed maiden; and fight against all the bodiless enemies who savagely insult my poverty, so that I may faithfully praise Thee.
By the most luminous lamps of Him who was incarnate of Thee, O most holy Virgin, above the reach of the mind, may we who faithfully acknowledge Thee as Theotokos be enlightened, and may we be delivered from the darkness of passions, and from dangers, and from all the tribulations of life.
From the Canon for the feast of the reception of the relics of the saints Cyrus and John, on the 28th day.
As one who, out of excess of goodness, makes us familiar to Thee, O most chaste and most pleasing to God, deliver all from every darkness, tempest, and danger.
Virgin most undefiled, who didst bear Him who takes away the diseases of men, apply Thy healing hand to the contritions of my soul and the infirmities of my flesh.
Sprinkle Thy opulent mercies upon us, O Virgin, according to Thy custom, curing the various diseases of the souls of those who approach Thee in faith, for Thou art the cause of good things, O most praised. C 
Calm, I beseech Thee, the waves of my wretched soul; and settle the pains of my flesh, Thou who alone didst bear God made body without pains.
Make me superior to the intellectual powers, and superior to all the malice of the seducer, by Thy intercessions, while I glorify Thee always with thanksgiving.
From hostile men, from evil demons, and from every other adversity, mishap, and all injury, deliver me, O holy Virgin, and guard me as I sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our Fathers. D 
In the likeness of flesh, He who is above divinity appeared from Thee, O chaste Virgin, whom unceasingly entreat to have mercy on us who, with malice...
living together and trembling at the eternal punishment, O Virgin.
