Thou art become as a cloud of light, holding in thine arms, O pure One, the Sun of righteousness that sets not; therefore I cry to thee: Illumine me, who am darkened by many evils, while I unceasingly honor thee.
133 From the Canon for St. Hypatius, on the 28th
Thou didst give thy body, O inviolate Virgin, to the Savior and God out of thy chaste bloods, who gave to us his wise Hierarch, a saving and fervent defender, the truly admirable Hypatius.
Be propitious to me on the formidable and terrible day of Christ, O Mother of God, Virgin Mother Mary, who art more sublime than all the creatures of thy Son, seeing that thou alone didst suckle Him supernaturally.
O Virgin Mother, who didst bring forth the incarnate God, cleansing the grave and innumerable lapses of my soul, save me by thy intercession.
The rivers of thy graces, and the fountains of healings, and the distributions of divine riches are divided, O Bride of God, from that hand whence life, of the Omnipotent who was born from thy womb, had its beginning.
Thou didst bring forth the subsistent Wisdom of God, O inviolate Virgin Mother of God, who made the saints most wise, by whom the pride of the architect of malice fell, and his worst stratagems.
O miracle of all miracles! The greatest, that a Virgin conceiving without male operation did not straiten in her womb Him who embraces all things.
O Virgin Bride of God, who without the experience of a bridal chamber, and without the corruption of seed, didst conceive the Only-begotten of the Father and bring Him forth in the flesh from thy immaculate bloods, cease not to pour forth prayers for the salvation of the world.
Me, surrounded by many perils and most dangerously tossed by the tempest of sins, guide now, O Lady Mother of God, by the breath of the Holy Spirit to the most peaceful harbor; for thou art the haven of Christians; wherefore we praise thee unto all ages.
Most lucid Mother of the Creator, consolation of those who mourn, protection of those in danger, and aid of those who labor, and swift visitation of the sick, guard me so long as I shall live.
MONTH OF JULY
From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyrs Cosmas and Damian, on the 1st
Thee, the seat and possession of God, the spiritual table, the beauty of Jacob, the bridge most happy and easy for crossing, and the stable and immovable ladder, O immaculate one, all the generations of men call blessed with affection.
He who is formidable to the celestial armies dwelt in thee in an ineffable manner, O chaste Virgin, having found thee purer than every nature, visible and intelligible; therefore we call thee blessed.
The lamp of divine light, superior to all creatures, which deified man, inasmuch as it brought forth God, is glorified as Mother of God.
Make to arise upon me, O Lady, a ray of divine knowledge, since I am severely oppressed by the darkness of ignorance; and lead me to the light of repentance, O immaculate one, as thou art the gate of light.
Save me, thou who brought forth the Savior; for the depth of sins disturbs me, and the tempest of desires tosses me, and the storm of the spirits of wickedness afflicts me.
Christ shall descend, as rain upon the fleece, into thy womb, O most dear to God; and He shall cause the torrents of iniquity to cease, as God; and He shall pour forth immortality and life as a fountain to those who sing: Blessed is the God of our Fathers.
From your sacred blood the Creator of all has been incarnate, and has come forth from your womb, guarding you as a virgin. O miracle of miracles! O manifestation of new mysteries, accomplished in you for all ages!
Having appeared, O Virgin, higher than the Cherubim, make my mind higher than carnal pleasures and the temptations of life, and grant me to walk steadily in the paths of salvation, which lead, O Immaculate One, to the city on high.
From the Canon to the holy Thomas in the Palaion, and to the holy martyr Kyriake, day 7.
You stayed the violence of death, O chaste one, having given birth to Christ, the Bestower of immortality, at whom Hades trembled when it saw Him dead by voluntary decree.
Having given birth to the substantial Wisdom of God, O Virgin, deliver me from the sophist of malice by your intercession, O only all-blameless one.
Deliver from every evil of the enemy, O Virgin, those who truly know you to be the Mother of God, O all-pure one.
From another Canon to the Holy Unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian.
The Creator of all, as God, became incarnate from your pure blood, and came forth from your womb, guarding you, Virgin. O miracle of miracles! O manifestation of new mysteries, which have been wrought in you for all ages!
Having appeared, O Virgin, higher than the Cherubim, make my mind higher than carnal pleasures and the temptations of life, and grant me to walk steadily in the paths of salvation, which lead, O Immaculate One, to the city on high.
You fashioned the Savior and God from your chaste blood, O pure and inviolate one, who gave us as doctors of our passions, and fervent defenders, the wise Unmercenaries in spirit.
God chose you, most beautiful among women, and it pleased Him, who rests in His saints, to be born of you corporally, O chaste one.
Make me worthy through your compassion, O inviolate Virgin, who gave birth to the uniquely compassionate Word, who granted to all the ends of the earth holy, compassionate doctors and miracle-workers.
You gave birth to the substantial Wisdom of God, O inviolate Mother of God, who granted us the holy, all-wise ones, through whom the pride of the architect of malice and his most grievous stratagems have fallen.
The most pure Word made you a clean temple, O Lady, and He ever magnifies the divine Church of the Unmercenaries with signs and wonders.
O Maria, rod that sprouted from the root of Jesse, you brought forth, O inviolate one, the flower, Christ, who adorns His servants, the Unmercenaries, as with flowers, with miracles.
Death is destroyed in you; for you gave birth to the substantial Life, Christ the Lord, O inviolate one, protector of our life, who gave the Unmercenaries as doctors to those who cry: Bless all things.
You have become, O Virgin, the dwelling-place of that Light which has illuminated all things, and has now granted the light-bearing saints, who eliminate the darkness of deadly passions in the spirit, O only ever-inviolate Virgin.
From another Canon to the Holy Unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian.
Pour out upon us now, O chaste one, the drops of your mercies, you who ineffably gave birth to the good, the pious, and the merciful one, and who now exist as the protection of all.
He who alone is good, alone intimately merciful, has entered your immaculate womb, O totally immaculate one, wishing to reform us who are defiled by passions.
In you, O Virgin Mother of God, I have placed my hopes, that I might be delivered from all the malice of the enemy.
O chaste Lady, who gave birth to the incarnate God in an incomprehensible manner, ever entreat Him to deliver me from carnal passions and from eternal torments.
 He who joined the lower things to the upper in your birth, O most chaste one, let Him keep in a tranquil state us who exalt you with praises.
He who is the Mountain of God, from whom the Truth is manifested, you are, O chaste Virgin, in whom He who is incomprehensible dwelt, and wished to become similar to men because of the excess of His mercy: to whom we chant: Blessed are you, etc.
Behold, O my soul, the gate of light, which now opens the entrances of repentance: behold the ladder of Jacob; the sole protection and defense of men: hasten through her intercessions to obtain mercy.
Acknowledging you, O Lady, to be the truly lucid cloud of the Sun of justice, may we be delivered through your intercession from the darkest shadows and from eternal punishment, O you who are free from every stain.
From the Canon in the feast of St. Thomas of the Palaion and St. Cyriaca the martyr, day 7.
You stayed the violence of death, O chaste one, having given birth to Christ, the Bestower of immortality, at whom Hades trembled when it saw Him dead by voluntary decree.
Having given birth to the substantial Wisdom of God, O Virgin, deliver me from the sophist of malice by your intercession, O only all-blameless one.
Deliver from every evil of the enemy, O Virgin, those who truly know you to be the Mother of God, O all-pure one.
(64****) This canon, with the following one, is missing in the printed Menaia.
You have dissolved, O undefiled one, the curse of the first parents, having brought forth without the will of the flesh, O venerable one, Him who by His own divine will clearly produced all things.
Having brought forth Christ the King, as a queen, O God-graced one, make those who run to you worthy of the kingdom of heaven.
The only God found your womb alone to be pure, and is embodied and is recognized as man, saving man; whence, acknowledging you as the cause of good things, we sing: Blessed are you, who brought forth God in the flesh.
The supersubstantial God was made substantial according to us from you, O Virgin, and was seen as an infant, He who is from before the ages with the Father and the divine Spirit; whence we glorify you as His mother.
By the most radiant lamps of Him who was incarnate from you, O all-holy Virgin, we who know you above human thought to be the Theotokos are illuminated by faith, and are set free from the darkness of passions, and from all dangers and every tribulation.
*From the Canon to the holy martyrs Patermuthius and Copres, day 9 (64****)*
Put to death the affections of my heart, you who ineffably brought forth for us Christ our life, O Virgin who knows not the nuptial chamber, hope of those who run to you.
O salutary gate, open to me the gates of repentance, as a benign protectress, and deliver me from the gates of sin, keeping me by your divine power.
The Word of God received a body from your womb, O maiden Mother of God, and was seen as an infant, exhibiting to all an admirable generation full of wonder.
He who was most perfect, having been made man from you, O unwedded Virgin, deified the corrupted essence of men.
With unceasing voice we cry to you: Rejoice, O most undefiled one; for you brought forth Christ, the joy of all, and have driven away all the sorrow of the first mother, Eve.
Behold that legal Ark prefigured your womb, containing Christ, our Manna, our food, O Mother of God, alone chaste, blessed.
You appeared higher than the heavens, when you brought forth the Word of God, who raised us to the heights, whom every spirit greatly exalts as our God, unto the ages.
Illumine with the rays of your light, O Bride of God, my soul, lying in the deep of sloth; arise, and disturb and cast down the enemies, who always vex my heart and drive me to pursue my lusts.
*From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyrs Proclus and Hilarion, day 12*
The poison which the first mother Eve had drunk in by hearing, Gabriel, by hailing you "Rejoice" (Ave), truly cast out, O Lady: for you alone brought forth beyond all thought and speech the destroyer of the malice of the serpent.
Dissolve, O Virgin, the chain of my evils, binding me with the love of the Word who was born from you, O all-pure one; and save me, Lady, by your prayers.
Having compassion on the work of Your hands, broken by the transgression, O Word, You dwelt in a womb that knew no marriage, and You proceeded in two substances, renewing the paths of immortality for those who know You.
Who is able to explain your mystery, O Lady?
O Mother of God, for you ineffably clothed the Creator of all with flesh.
Behold, the Virgin shall conceive, Isaiah once cried out, the angel of the great counsel, Emmanuel, the God and Lord and Savior of our souls.
As holier than all creatures, O chaste Virgin, you gave birth to the Creator and Lord, O undefiled Virgin, blessed Mother, ever-glorified.
God, who made and fashioned me, having become incarnate from your undefiled blood, O Lady, Mother of God, has reclaimed the world, which cries out thus: Bless and praise the Lord.
You have become the dwelling-place of Light, O chaste and most holy Virgin-Mother, in the visible matter of a body, by whom all who draw life in shadows are illuminated: wherefore we faithfully call you blessed.
From the Canon for the Synaxis, or assembly, of the Archangel Gabriel, day 13
Where Gabriel, etc. (The same is as the Canon for the day of 26 March.)
From the Canon for the feast of St. Golinduch the martyr, day 13
The Creator, wishing to cleanse our nature from the filth of malice, became incarnate from your pure womb, O Mother of God; therefore we all glorify you.
We have clearly seen God incarnate from your chaste blood, O Virgin, and having assumed our form through mercy; wherefore we faithfully glorify you.
You have dissolved the bond of transgression, having given birth to the Giver of good things with an excess of kindness, O Virgin-Mother. Wherefore we the faithful glorify you.
Since my mind is stained and rendered useless by many transgressions, O Mother of God, only undefiled one, I beseech you to pity me and save me by your mediation.
The Most High, having woven for Himself a garment from your pure blood, O undefiled one, adorned those who had been stripped of divine raiment; wherefore we longingly call you blessed.
Having you always as a propitiation before God, O most immaculate one, deliver us from the terrible torments of the life to come, and free us from all threats and the attempts of enemies, both visible and invisible.
You who by your birth-giving rendered the whole malice of the seducer barren, O chaste one, make my heart, which is barren of all good works, fruitful, by rendering God propitious to me.
At the voice of the angel, O chaste one, you conceived the Word of the Father, whom He had prepared as a dwelling-place for Himself; God, the infuser of grace. Consider the birth of the Mother of God, and you will not marvel at a conception without stain. Great are the things that are spoken, but they are true, they are holy, and they are fitting for the Mother of God, whose conception grace preceded, and hence the world marvels. Thus he.
who willed to become like unto us, whom do thou entreat that we might find mercy and the remission of sins, O most immaculate one; whence we ever glorify thee with grateful voices.
From the Canon for the Holy Apostle Aquila, day 14.
By the Word, O venerable one, thou didst conceive in thy womb the Word who through the Word created all things; therefore do we hymn thee with divine words, O thou full of the grace of God.
The only pure one, the only Lord, as He knew thee alone to be purer than all creation, O most immaculate one, was incarnate from thy chaste blood.
We address thee, O Theotokos and Lady, as a spiritual palace and the most high throne of the King.
Thou art become both Mother and handmaid of Christ, who was incarnate for our sake, whom do thou ever earnestly entreat to save us who call thee the chaste Theotokos.
O immaculate maiden, whose name echoes lordship, who hast brought forth God the giver of good things, save those who hymn thee from manifold temptations at all times.
Adam died of old through the corruption-producing food, O most pure Virgin, but thou, who didst bring forth our Life, hast quickened him; whence, as the cause of good things, we hymn thee and cry out: Blessed art thou, who didst bring forth God in the flesh.
Since truly, O chaste one, thou didst conceive in thy womb God the cause of all causes, who is above every cause, and didst bring forth for our sake Him who appeared as we are, O most immaculate one, do thou entreat Him for those who hymn thee.
The prophet foresaw thee as an illuminating lamp, O Virgin-Mother, bearing the Light sprung from Light, which richly illuminated what was before darkened by the rays of His ineffable divinity, O most immaculate one.
From the Canon for the Holy Martyrs Cyricus and Julitta, day 15.
Death is brought to naught through thee, and the sting of Hades is wiped away, O chaste Mother; for thou didst bring forth the immortal Master who died in the flesh.
Without emptying the Father’s bosom, O undefiled one, the Word who gave essence to all things dwelt in thy most immaculate womb, and appeared as flesh without change, and deified mortals, He who is supersubstantial.
The laws of nature, O all-chaste one, are changed in thy birth-giving which was above nature; for thou didst bring forth the Creator in a way beyond mind and reason.
God, the Word of God, took from thee flesh endowed with mind and soul, O all-holy one, and through compassion became man, and deified me who had been cast away through transgression; Him do thou entreat to save all things.
With the sharp scythe of your intercession, cut away, O Maiden, the wicked thoughts from the roots of my soul, and make me fruitful, I pray; for you have given birth to God the Sower of all, and Savior.
Clinging to your words, all generations call you blessed, O Maiden, having been shown to be the Mother of the blessed God, who makes those who believe in Him blessed.
The Word, incarnate from your most immaculate blood, O immaculate Maiden, deified those who had previously inclined toward the most irrational passions of the flesh, through divine knowledge; therefore we exalt Him above all forever.
Illumine, O gate of light, my soul blinded by affections and darkened and endangered by wicked thoughts; and deliver me from temptations, dangers, and tribulations, that I may glorify you, the hope and fortress of the faithful.
*From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyr Athenogenes, day 16.*
You gave birth to the eternal Word, O unwedded one, having become flesh from your blood, beyond the comprehension of mind or word.
You appeared higher than the heavens, O chaste one, and ever holier than the Seraphim, since you supernaturally gave birth to the King and Lord of all.
You rendered the super-substantial One, equal in power and throne to the Begetter, incarnate, O most immaculate one, He who for compassion dwelt among men.
Recognizing you as Mother and Virgin, we unanimously venerate you as all-holy, and devoutly call you blessed.
As an intelligible ark, you carried the Lawgiver; as a radiant lamp, you brought forth the Light; as an unwatered root, O Theotokos, you sprouted the cluster of life.
The Word, whom you brought forth beyond word, O Mother of God Mary, entreat for us who faithfully praise you and call you blessed, O immaculate one.
Having been delivered through you, O most undefiled one, from the ancient fall of our first parents, we cry to you, "Hail," and with faith glorify Him who through you delivered us from corruption.
You carry in your arms the God who carries all things; you nourish the Nourisher, O chaste one, who became like us; entreat Him to deliver your people from all hardships and adversities.
*From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyr Marina, day 17.*
You have become a capacious vessel of divine grace, O immaculate Mother of God; therefore, Marina, pursuing and desiring you with virginal affection, was led after you to your Son.
Truly and properly, we the faithful venerate you as Theotokos, O most immaculate one; for you have given birth to God, who has become flesh. The most immaculate and only holy...
one, who appeared holier than the Cherubim, save our souls from every surrounding adversity, as we praise you with faith, O immaculate Virgin, Bride of God.
The Creator, who surrounds the sea with cloud as if with a swaddling cloth, by His own will is born as an infant from the virgin maiden who has not known man, and is wrapped in swaddling clothes in an ineffable manner.
O unique Virgin, because the pure Word loved you as pure and incorrupt, He became incarnate from you and refashioned man, He who glorified Marina with miracles.
You appeared higher than the heavens, having given birth to the heavenly God, O most chaste one, who has made the whole mass of earth-born creatures heavenly, and has brightened the revered memory of Marina; to whom we cry out: "All you works, praise the Lord."
You have caused light to rise for us from your inviolate womb, O Virgin, who, being illuminated by divine splendors, became light, O Mother of God, Virgin Mother, whose name resonates with joy.
From the Canon for the feast of Saint Emilian the martyr, on the 18th.
My strength, and my praise, and the illumination of my heart is Christ the Lord, whom you gave birth to, O most immaculate one, who is understood in two substances, but in one hypostasis.
Ignoring the laws of nature in your childbirth, which was above nature, O Virgin Mother, you remained a Virgin after birth; for you gave birth to the Creator of all creation, O inviolate one.
We glorify you, O all-holy maiden, as the only one found to be the place of the Sanctification that sanctifies us, through whom those inhabiting the earth were made heavenly, and were rendered worthy of true life.
Heal me, who am wounded by the sword of sin, with your most effective medicine, you who gave birth to the Savior Christ, who was wounded by a lance for my sake, and himself wounded the heart of the serpent.
Eve indeed plucked the fruit of the death-bearing tree; but you, O most chaste one, brought forth the tree of life, the taste of which brought to life all who were dead.
O Bride of God, adorned with a name of lordship, to you we cry out "Rejoice" with faith; for you gave birth to Christ the Lord, the ineffable joy, to whom we cry out: "Blessed are You, the God of our fathers."
Rain down upon me a drop of mercy, you who gave birth to the fountain of mercy, and dry up the showers of my sin, and calm the wild waves of my soul, O Virgin Theotokos Mary, that I may glorify you unto all ages.
Illuminate me with your light, O most worthy of all praise, as I walk in darkness; reach out your hand of help to me; the
clouds of my soul dispel; the tempest of my passions calm, O refuge of those in despair.
From the Canon for the feast of our holy Father Dius, on the 19th.
You have become a tabernacle of the spiritual Sun, O most pure one, who has illuminated us with the divine splendors of piety and dispersed the mist of ignorance, O ever-Virgin.
He who dwells in the heavens has dwelt within you, O immaculate one; whom earnestly entreat to save the souls of those who praise you.
We have known you to be a light-bearing lampstand, carrying the divine radiance in your womb, O Virgin: wherefore we suppliants pray you, that with your light you may illuminate the souls of all who praise you.
Mortify the passions of my soul, O most praiseworthy one, you who brought forth the Life of all by an ineffable Word; and calm my troubled mind, O Maiden.
God the holy one has manifestly made you holier than the Cherubim, O Maiden, sanctifying those who cry out: Blessed are you among women, O most immaculate Lady.
You have appeared more spacious than the heavens, having contained God, O Mary most chaste; whom entreat to deliver me from the passions that hold me fast, and to rescue me from the future fearful judgment, as I cry aloud: All you works, praise the Lord.
Spare me, O Christ, when you come to judge the world with glory, having to entreat you, O Word, the Theotokos ever-Virgin, the orders of angels, and the assembly of the saints.
From the Canon for the feast of the holy Prophet Elias, on the 20th.
The supersubstantial God, O most clean one, has become incarnate from you, and for our sake appeared as man like unto us: whom earnestly entreat, O most chaste one, that I, who have sinned above all men, may be saved and delivered from torment.
O impervious gate, through whom one passes to God, open to me the gates of repentance, I pray, washing away the filth of my sins with the showers of your mercy, O maiden most dear to God.
With all the heavenly hosts, with all the prophets and martyrs, with the apostles and confessors, pour forth your prayers, O most clean Lady, that I, who have sinned much, may attain salvation and be snatched from future punishments.
Upon you, as rain, the supersubstantial Word has descended; whom entreat, O most innocent maiden, that He may now rain down upon me pure drops of compunction, by which all the filth of my measureless evils may be washed away.
O gate of God, show divine entrances to my miserable soul, by which I may enter with confession, and receive the absolution of my evils, O Theotokos.
I praise you, O most praiseworthy one, and I magnify you, O maid beloved of God,
your pure childbearing; assist me, who am tossed about by the waves of life, and grant compunction to my humble soul, as a cleanser of its defilements.
The Legislator of piety and Master of repentance, Emmanuel, appeared having been born of you, whom now entreat, O all-holy Lady, to open for me the gates of righteousness from above, and to save me as I cry out: "Priests, bless the Lord."
Do not disregard the voices of your servants, as you are good, O most blameless Lady, but earnestly ask the Creator of all for the king to grant him victories, and for strength of soul, O Virgin, and for the participation and splendor of the divine kingdom.
149 Ex Canone in S. Focam martyrem, die 23 (65).
The punishment of our first parents was dissolved: for you brought forth God, who is before the ages, O undefiled one; who, having become a new infant, hath completely renewed the whole of human substance.
God, having been incarnate of you, because of the bowels of His mercy, was united to men, and took away the curse, O Lady alone heaped with every blessing.
Virgin immune from nuptials, Virgin blessed, glory of bishops, crown of all martyrs, free those who sing your praises from perils and tribulations.
The Wisdom of God built for Himself a house, as it was pleasing to Him, from your pure and holy blood, O Lady.
As a saving rain, the Word was poured forth in your incorrupt womb, O most holy girl, and by His divine power dried up the torrents of malice.
Restore the shattered and ruined house of my soul, you, as most benign, by acts of repentance, O most chaste girl, who didst reform the whole nature of men by your childbirth.
The Ark of the Law, and the urn that contained the manna, prefigured you, O most chaste one; the divine table, and the lamp shining with gold, which brought forth that Light for the revelation of the Gentiles, which illuminated the whole world with divine knowledge.
Illumine, O pure one, my soul, wrapped in the darkness of sin, and free me from the flames and eternal darkness by your mediation, that with exultation of soul I may celebrate your greatness.
150 Ex Canone in festo S. Christine martyris, die 24.
You conceived the Word of the Father united to flesh according to the hypostasis that was from you; which, as she ardently loved, Christina obtained the glory of martyrdom.
Calm, O chaste Lady, the tumult of my thoughts, take away all consternation of soul, you who gave birth to Christ.
The most glorious of the prophets, Isaiah, once named you a rod, bringing forth the flower, the Lord, O Theotokos, mother and ever-virgin.
Enliven me who have become dead through sin, O chaste Virgin, having given birth to the immortal life.
The divine-speaking prophets, perceiving the depth of your mystery, O Virgin, prophetically foretold it when illuminated from afar by the divine Spirit, that you would truly be the mother of the Lord of all.
Having transcended the laws of nature, O Virgin, by your divine conception, you gave birth to God above the order of nature, crying: "Blessed are You, Lord God, unto the ages."
O perpetual Virgin, most powerful help of the faithful, deliver me from the seduction of the deceitful dragon, who grievously wars against me and hastens to humble me; for you...
are the unerring guide of those who trust in you and cry out unceasingly: "People, exalt the Lord above all."
O Virgin who loves the good, make my soul, corrupted by sins, good, and deliver me from the eternal flame by your intercessions.
From the Canon to the holy martyr Hermolaus and his companions, on the 27th day.
O most pure one, who brought forth the divine and immaculate light into the world, dispel the darkness that is in me, dissipate the clouds of my heart; illuminate me, O gate of light, who with faith magnify you and glorify God; for He has been gloriously glorified.
He who is understood as possessing a twofold nature, God and man, while in no way abandoning the Paternal bosom, sat in your bosom, O inviolate Virgin, circumscribed, while being uncircumscribed by His own nature.
The celestial God dwelt within your womb, O Maiden, and deified man, and constituted you the protection and safeguard of the universe.
Legal types prefigured the mystery of your conception, the outcome of which we behold and glorify you, O Virgin, who have become the cause of all good things and have filled our race with grace.
Look upon me, O Queen most pleasing to God, and make Christ propitious to me, O all-undefiled one, on the day of judgment, removing the fearful sentence of condemnation.
Deliver me, O most immaculate one, from the grievous tempest of sins and of thoughts which cruelly invade my heart.
Like a fire-bearing throne, you carry the Master, O one most filled with divine grace; whom you should entreat to keep us safe when we are in danger in the sea of sin.
Having you, O Virgin, as a protection, a refuge, and a firm defense, may we through you be delivered from every tribulation.
The tempest of my boundless transgressions disturbs me and continually casts me into the abyss of despair, O Maiden; but anticipating this, reach out your hand to me and grant that I may enter secure into the calm harbors of repentance.
O all-holy Virgin, who gave birth to God in the flesh, save your people who cry out to you from every sin and tribulation: "Blessed are You, O God of our fathers."
O most pure one, who brought forth the divine and immaculate light, dispel the darkness that is in me, and dissipate the clouds of my heart. Illuminate me, O gate of light, for I praise you with faith, and glorify God; for He has been gloriously glorified.
Those who are troubled by the most wicked demons, who disturb me with vexation, deliver me from the fire of Gehenna, O you whom I praise with faith.
Just as the fire of the furnace did not once burn the most prudent youths, so the fire of Divinity did not now burn your womb, O Virgin Mother of God, which renewed the bounds of nature within you.
The Lord Almighty, having inhabited your womb, saved those who were afflicted with disease, bowed down to the earth, and openly serving sin; whence they now cry out to Him with firm faith: "O children, etc."
You have restored the corrupted substance of earth-born men by your incorruptible birth-giving. Wherefore I cry aloud: Restore me, who am entirely corrupted by wicked desires, as you are the most benign, and show me the paths that lead to life; for you are the guide of all who have recourse to you, O most pure one.
We praise you, O most holy Lady, as the delightful palace and bright dwelling-place of the King of all, beseeching you to show us to be temples of your Son, cleansed of all opposing wickedness, and crying out unceasingly: "O peoples, exalt Christ unto the ages."
Spare me, O Savior, who were born and kept your Mother uncorrupt after the birth, when you shall sit to judge the universe; do not look upon my iniquities and my sins, as you are sinless and merciful, as God and lover of mankind.
From the Canon for the feast of the holy apostles Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, and Parmenas, day 28.
The ways of God made manifest in you have become known, O most immaculate one, through your wondrous birth-giving and incomparable union; whence we glorify you as the Lady of all creation.
You have brought forth the good Lord, who distills sweetness and redemption from evils, O inviolate Virgin, lacking every stain.
Without the union of a man you gave birth to God the Word, made flesh, O most chaste one, beyond mind and word; whence we duly glorify you, O Virgin, and as is our duty, we call you blessed.
We praise you, through whom we were redeemed from corruption, O most immaculate one, from the abyss, and from the wickedness of the avenging foe that formerly tyrannized us.
The ranks of the bodiless angels venerate you, O Theotokos, together with the choir of the apostles and the multitudes of the martyrs; for you have ineffably brought forth the King of all.
By the Word you gave birth to the Word of the Father, O maiden, who by a word created heaven and earth; and you glorify him, O most immaculate one, as he provides the word to those who now purely believe in him.
Behold, the voices of the God-speakers have received their end, by your bearing the supersubstantial Lord, declared and demonstrated by them for the salvation of the faithful, who cry out, O most graceful one: "All you works of the Lord, bless the Lord."
We cry out to you, O Virgin, with the voice of the archangel: "Rejoice, the joy of the angels, the honor of the apostles, the proclamation of the prophets, and the crown of the martyrs."
From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyrs Silas, Silvanus, and their companions, day 30.
You have ineffably brought forth God, who is above all praise, having taken flesh from you for the sake of his goodness, O most praised and chaste one; whence with voices of thanksgiving we praise you and call you blessed, as you yourself once prophesied.
The One who inhabits inaccessible light, having found you, O Theotokos, holier than the angels, entered into your holy womb and became man, taking flesh from you, known in two natures.
The miracle that took place in you is the most eminent of all miracles; for beyond the accustomed laws of nature, you brought forth Christ the Lawgiver, who blotted out the transgression of our first parents, O most immaculate one. David previously described you as a coagulated mountain, the mountain of our God, a fertile mountain. For in you, O maiden, were made known the paths of Him who requested flesh from you, and who led us back to our pristine dignity.
When the Creator found you adorned with beauty, He placed His tabernacle within you, and, becoming incarnate, He appeared more beautiful than all the sons of earth, O most holy Virgin, worthy of all praise. Dissolve the bonds of my sins through your intercession, O chaste one, and bind me perfectly with the love of your good Son; for day by day I depart farther from Him through deformed desires. Spare me, O You who are to come again with the glory of divinity to judge the world, O omnipotent Lord, through the intercession of her who bore You without knowing man, and do not cast me into the fire, having been condemned for my sins.
From the Canon for the Feast of the Holy and Just Eudocimus, Day 31.
As a living bridal chamber of God and a censer of the spiritual and life-giving coal, let us hymn the ever-blessed Theotokos, crying out: Hail, cause of our salutary restoration. Being more honorable than the angels, you carried in your womb the Creator of the angels, and you brought Him forth, O Mother of God, for the redemption of those who sing to you: there is no one holy, O immaculate one, besides you, O Lady. O Virgin ever-praised, you gave birth to God, who is hymned by the orders above, having truly become man; do not cease to entreat Him on behalf of your servants, O ever-virgin. Always entreat, O Virgin Mother, on behalf of us who hymn you, the One who became incarnate from you, that we may be delivered from passions and deadly dangers, from soul-destroying evils and tribulations, and from the eternal flame and punishment.
You were chosen by God, for you were most beautiful, O Virgin, and you became a spacious dwelling place for Him, and a bridal chamber, and a lamp, and a table. Always entreat Him whom you bore, O Lady, to deliver me from the slavery of passions of damnation, from the heavy hardness that holds me, and from the rule of those who always trouble me, O most dear to God. The Former of Adam is fashioned from your blood, O chaste one, and He who nourishes every living thing is nourished by your milk, O Theotokos Virgin; whence we glorify you as the Mother of God. You are seen as the dwelling place and tabernacle of the Light that illuminates all, and a bridge and ladder to the heights of the earth
leading the earth-born on high, O Maiden, wherefore we revere you and faithfully call you blessed.
MONTH OF AUGUST
From the Canon for the Translation of the Precious Cross from the treasury, day 1.
The all-pure one was saying as she wept: "When I gave birth to you, O Son, ineffably, I escaped labor pains, and how am I now all filled with pain? For I see you hanging as a malefactor on the wood, you who hung the earth without support."
Beholding Life dead upon the cross, and not bearing the pain of her heart, the venerable Virgin was shaken, crying out: "Woe is me, my Son, what has the assembly of the lawless done to you?"
"From a virgin womb I gave you birth, O Son, and seeing you now hanging on the wood, I am at a loss and do not understand the height of the mystery and the depth of your many judgments," the all-pure one cried out, whom we bless with unresting voices as the Mother of God.
Beholding on the cross Him who, for His goodness, was born of you, O all-immaculate one, beyond the comprehension of the mind, your heart was shaken and you were saying: "Woe is me, divine Son! How are You in pain for all? I worship Your tender mercy, O Lord."
Strengthen us, O Pure one, to fast from all malice, and ever empower us to abstain from vile and wicked deeds, as you are the protector of all mankind.
Expand the narrowness of my mind by your intercession, O Lady, who brought under and confined all the stratagems of the enemy, and guide me along the narrow path to walk toward the expansion of life, O Mother of God.
"Now, as I behold You hanging like an innocent lamb, and fastened to the cross by lawless men, O my Son, who are without beginning and before all, I am cut to the heart, and I am encircled by maternal pains," the all-pure one cried out, whom we hymn divinely with unresting voices unto all ages.
"Without corruption I bore You from my womb, whom the Father begat before the ages; and how do corrupt men now rend You, O Son, and pierce Your side with a lance, and inhumanly nail Your hands and feet?" The all-pure one cried out, whom we worthily magnify.
From the Canon for the Holy Seven Youths, day 2
He who is by His own nature pure, when He had found you, O all-pure one, more pure than all creation, dwelt within you, desiring, as the lover of mankind, to eliminate the guilt that had dwelt in Adam.
When Christ had taken me from your divine blood as a garment, O inviolate one, He clothed me, who was once naked, with the garments of grace.
You gave birth to a new infant, O Virgin, who has renewed the world, long since worn out by age, with divine knowledge; therefore we glorify you.
Dissolve, O Virgin, the hardness of my soul: and grant me to promptly and easily obey and cleave to the divine decrees of your Son.
Mortify the pride and ferocity of my flesh, O pu-
rissima, you who gave birth to that Life which took away death by death, and miraculously brought the children back to life. You have appeared more excellent than the angels, O Mother of God; you have appeared truly as the strength of athletes, you have appeared as the salvation of all those who truly acknowledge you as the Mother of the Lord. Apply a healing hand to my ailing soul, O Virgin, and wash away the filth of the passions clinging to me, and set me before the tribunal of Almighty God with perfect salvation, so that I may sing: All you works, etc. Bear within your arms Him who holds all the universe with His divine hand, O Virgin, and supplicate Him, so that He may embrace me, who am more condemned than all others, through the bowels of His immense mercy, and make me whole.
From the Canon for the Feast of the Holy Fathers Isaac, Dalmatus, and Faustus, on the 3rd
O glorious one, who gave birth to God, deliver me from the disgrace of the passions, and grant me, O Virgin, a mind of compunction, and illuminate my mind, O chaste one, with the light of repentance, so that I may magnify you, who have magnified all. We have known you as a spiritual lamp and a luminous vessel, receiving within yourself, O Virgin, an intolerable fire; a divine palace and a most high throne, in which the heavenly and supersubstantial One rested. Sleep—the slumber of sin—has cast me down into drowsiness and sloth; but do you, O chaste one, rouse me with your wakeful intercession to repentance. All generations glorify you as the true Mother of God, O immaculate one, you who were clearly shown to be holier than the angels, O all-holy Maiden. Wherefore I cry out to you: Sanctify my soul, which has been defiled by the passions. Visit my soul, ailing with sins and the various vexations of the enemy, O all-holy Virgin, with your saving visitation, and heal me quickly, as you are good, O Mother of God, my hope, and all-praised one. You have checked and restrained the onslaught of death, having brought forth the immortal God, O only chaste Mother of God, whom we believingly praise, saying: Blessed are you, O Lord God. The Lord, having dwelt in your undefiled womb, made you entirely pure and luminous. Wherefore, cleanse me, O Virgin, who have been defiled by venomous bites and the harmful attacks of enemies, and make me worthy to sing: O ye people, superexalt the Lord throughout all ages. O gate of light, illuminate my heart, which has been blinded by malice; and do not allow me now to fall asleep in death, I who am always enveloped in the darkness of impure thoughts, so that I may glorify you with thanksgiving, O Mother of God, all-immaculate one.
From the Canon for the Holy Martyr Eusignius, on the 5th
The curse is abolished, and sorrow has ceased through your birth-giving, O all-blessed Maiden, the joy of the faithful, immune to any stain. I direct all my desires toward you, O chaste Queen. Deliver me most speedily from carnal desires. O all-holy Maiden, perpetual Virgin, you have brought forth the Word, co-equal and co-throned with the Father.
whom I entreat to save me.
The Word in your womb, O immaculate one, takes on a body, delivering the world from the irrational passions of the flesh. A Having dried up the plants of malice by the sprouting of the Word within you, O chaste Mother, cut away from the roots of my soul my wicked thoughts, and plant there, O Virgin, the beautiful blossoms of the virtues. You have brought forth a new child, whom the Father begat before the aeons, O chaste Theotokos, to whom we all sing: Blessed are you, O Lord. O compassionate Virgin, who have brought forth the most compassionate God, make all who sing to you worthy of divine compassion. Bless the Lord, all you works.
Illumine, O gateway of light, the eyes of my heart, I beseech you, which are blinded by the shadows of sin, and show them to be receptive to divine illuminations, that I may honor you with angelic voices, O all-blameless one.
From the Canon for the holy martyr Euplus, day 11.
When Christ, O chaste one, had illumined your light-bearing womb with His awesome descent, He arose to those in the world as the sun, dissolving the mist of polytheism that brought on the evening of evils, and illumining the ends of the earth. God having dwelt in your midst, did in no way disturb the barriers of your virginity, O chaste one; entreat Him earnestly to strengthen all who praise you. The rich of your people beseech you, O maiden, who gave birth to Christ our God, who has enriched all with divine knowledge. You have appeared truly higher than the angels, having given birth beyond understanding to the Maker of the angels, who glorified the holy martyrs, O all-holy Mother-Virgin. O miracle full of awe! How do you give birth without having known the experience of a man? How, O Virgin Mother, do you nurse with milk Him who is truly the author of milk and the nourisher of all creation? That your divine womb might be prefigured by that Persian furnace, it preserved the youths without burning, as they cried out: O Lord God, blessed are You. You have been made beautiful, O chaste and all-blameless one, above all the beauty of the angels, having given birth to the Maker of mortals and angels, to whom we sing: Bless the Lord, all you works. With the splendors of the light that is in you, O Bride of God, illumine my soul. Raise me up while I lie in the pit of destruction, putting to shame my enemies who always afflict my heart and incite me to pursue the passions.
From the Canon for the holy martyrs Photius and Anicetus, day 12.
Virgin both before childbirth, O immaculate one, and after
you have been shown to be the one who truly brought forth; for you gave birth beyond word to God, who crowned the holy martyrs who competed in the struggle. B The Lord who dwells in the heavens dwelt in you, and He banished from us every deception, O Theotokos. As one beautiful, you brought forth the Beautiful One, O Mother-Virgin immaculate, who showed the most beautiful martyrs to have struggled stoutly and to have diminished impiety. Who is able to explain your mystery, O Lady Theotokos? For beyond mind and word you have ineffably given birth to God. Beyond the laws of nature you gave birth, O most immaculate one, to the true Lawgiver; entreat Him to have pity on my soul, which is enslaved to the laws of sin, and to save me. As one wider than the heavens, O chaste one, you received the Word, who is contained by nothing, beyond what can be conceived by the mind, and you lead those who walk the very narrow road, O most immaculate one, toward the breadth of divine life. O holy Virgin, who brought forth God, the One beyond all holiness, who by grace crowned His holy martyrs, save and sanctify us who readily sing: Bless the Lord, all you works. Shine upon us, O you who brought forth the Light inaccessible, O Virgin; fill us with gladness, and cheerfulness, and divine knowledge, as we piously and prudently call you blessed with a pure heart. From the Canon for the holy martyr Myron, day 17. D You alone, without marital union, brought forth God, whom the victor-martyrs, confessing that He became like us, rendered the wiles of the deceiver void, O Lady untouched. You brought forth for the whole creation, laboring under the disease of impiety and faithlessness, God the Healer, O Virgin, and wonderfully healed it; therefore, giving thanks to you, we cry out: There is no one without stain except you, O Lady. The great and awesome mystery of your childbearing, O chaste one, strikes every mind with wonder, because God was pleased to become man from you for His own goodness, for the salvation and restoration of the world. Entreat Him who was incarnate from you by an ineffable word, O blessed one, so that we may be delivered from all enemies, both visible and invisible, O most immaculate one, we who proclaim you the chaste Theotokos.
The laws of nature are made new in you, O Virgin; for you have miraculously brought forth above nature God Emmanuel, who cannot be comprehended by nature, for the regeneration of us the faithful.
You have appeared as a region and possession of God, and a delightful palace and divine throne, in which He who sits prepared a heavenly seat for all, O most holy Virgin; therefore we cry out to you: Blessed are you, who gave birth to God in the flesh.
Struck in my soul by the dart of the enemy, I am wounded all over and suffer incurable pains; do you, O most pure one, who ineffably gave birth to the Savior Christ, heal and save me, O hope of the hopeless.
With angelic voices we all cry out to you, O Virgin, the palace and throne of God: Rejoice, you through whom we have been made worthy of the kingdom of heaven, we who of old were thrust away by corruption and foolishly lost our first beauty.
From the Canon for the Feast of the Holy Martyrs Florus and Laurus, Day 18
From a virginal womb you brought forth, O root never watered, the planter of all, made man and prone to suffer the passions, for whose love the divine martyrs, allured, fought faithfully, O undefiled Virgin, to be celebrated with every praise.
O maiden who knows not the nuptial chamber, through whom the Word, who is understood as being beyond all beginning, shone upon us, save your city and every other city and region from every surrounding adversity, O most beloved of God.
The Creator of all and God chose you, O Theotokos, as pure out of all generations, always a Virgin; and the only King of the ages made your womb an immaculate palace, and from you He appeared to men.
great mystery, hidden before all ages, which was by no means known to preceding generations, has been made manifest through you, O most inculpable one: the Word of the Father, who was before the ages, incarnate and made man.
Heal my soul, which is sick with sin, with your medical hand, O most chaste one, you who gave birth to the physician of souls, whom the divine martyrs confessing became physicians of the passions.
As a rose of the valleys, O maiden, God chose you out of this life; and having dwelt within you, He went forth according to the flesh, breathing upon us with the most sweet breath of divine knowledge, O most pure one, us who always confess you as Theotokos.
You have become holier than the angels, having given birth, O most holy maiden, to the Holy of Holies, who out of compassion became a man such as we are, without confusion, to save those who cry out to Him unceasingly: O children, bless; O priests, exalt the Lord above all.
Your childbirth is terrible, O chaste Mother; for the Word of God, whom the hosts of heaven tremble before, having become man on earth, you bore beyond the order of nature, remaining
a virgin just as you were before. Therefore, both with tongue and heart, confessing you as Theotokos, we magnify you.
From the Canon for the Holy Martyrs Andrew the General and his two thousand five hundred and ninety-three companions, the 19th day.
He who, out of the superabundance of His goodness, truly clothed Himself in flesh from you, O most immaculate one, for the salvation of all the faithful, is known as God and man at once, twofold in natures.
You have given birth to the Lord of all, O Lady, Virgin Bride of God, who delivers mortals from the tyranny of the enemy.
All tongues of men celebrate you, the glory of martyrs and the preservation of the faithful, O cleansed of every stain; for you gave birth to God, while remaining an undefiled Virgin.
The swords of the enemy have now failed even to the end, since you, O Theotokos, gave birth to Him who was wounded by the spear and recreated the world.
You have given birth ineffably to Him who is co-eternal with the Father, who became like unto men beyond reason and speech; entreat Him, O Mother of God, that He may deliver your servants from dangers.
You, O Maiden, who clearly deified men by your supernatural and divine childbirth, inasmuch as you ineffably gave a body to God, are blessed among women, O most immaculate Lady.
O holy Virgin, who ineffably gave birth to the supersanct holy God, whom the most holy martyrs confessed in the stadium, send down sanctification and illumination to the peoples who cry out: All works, bless the Lord.
Carrying in your arms Christ, who by His nod bears all things, beseech Him, O Lady, to deliver me from the hand of the alien, I who unceasingly magnify you with orthodox faith.
From the Canon for the Holy Prophet Samuel, the 20th day.
He who was with the Father as Son before the ages, having been incarnate in the last times, truly became your Son, O most pure one, making all those who were oppressed by the service of the cruel adversary the sons of God through faith.
From you proceeded Jesus Christ, having become embodied, and was incarnate. It also retains the same proportion to its parts as a successive whole, such as life is, compared to all the successes and steps of its course, which a permanent whole has to its parts. Moreover, if a positive and limited name, once applied to a part, extends itself to denominate the whole; how much more will a negative name, such as "Immaculate," being more universal and as it were not knowing how to be restricted, when attributed to one whole, spread out to denominate the part? Therefore, the rationale of "immaculate," which is attributed to the Virgin and the entire course of her life, will be able to denominate the conception as immaculate, as being the principal part initiating such a successive whole of this kind. So Nierembergius.
And deified us by the assumption of our flesh; wherefore, O all-immaculate one, we venerate thee as the Mother of Him.
Not emptying the bosom of the Father, He was pleased to be reclined in thy bosom as a new infant, for the recall, O Virgin, of our souls, to whom we cry out: Glory, O Christ, to Thy power.
Having become with us through compassion, the Savior was incorporated from thy sacred blood beyond the reach of the mind, O all-immaculate one; and the lover of mankind is recognized as both God and man.
Eva has been liberated from the pangs of labor, O all-immaculate one, as thou, without labor, didst bear Christ our God, who clearly healed the sufferings and pains of all.
Thou didst appear unburnt, O most pure one, having truly borne the fire of the Godhead; wherefore, O Mother of God, burn up my material passions, as thou art compassionate and a lover of good.
Make me worthy of thy compassion, O compassionate and good-loving Lady, and deliver me from Gehenna and from that outer darkness, that I may venerate thee with faith and affection.
Not having known the corruption of a man, thou didst receive in thy womb the incorruptible Word, who delivers us who are corrupted by many transgressions, by the passion of His incorruptible flesh, O incorruptible one, alone all-immaculate.
B 167 From the Canon to the holy Apostle Thaddaeus, and the holy martyr Bassa, on the 21st day.
Thou hast appeared as Lady of all created things, having ineffably borne Him who rules over all, O Theotokos Virgin, all-hymned.
Thou didst conceive the Word of the Father without maternal pains, O most holy one, and ineffably, beyond speech, didst bring Him forth for our salvation.
The prefigurements of the Law and the voices of the prophets, O Lady, clearly declared thy fearful birth, O Mother of God.
Thou didst save me who had died through the tasting of disobedience, thou alone having brought forth the subsistent Life, O maiden all-immaculate.
of an innocent man, Adam, and lost her innocence, finding for us original sin: but Mary, from the mass of perdition, being conceived without perdition, lost original sin, first found innocence, and brought forth immaculate Him who washes away the sins of all, [having been rendered] immaculate. He says this.
Sanctius also, of the Order of Preachers, in his 13th Marian sermon, speaking of this innocence of the Virgin, said: "Eve had two names: the first, in the state of innocence, 'virago' (woman); the second, in the state of fallen nature, 'Eva'. But from the word 'virago', remove 'A', namely Adam, who lost that state, and there remains 'virgo' (virgin), to signify that the state of innocence, lost through Adam, is recovered and brought back through a Virgin."
Hence, Father Hortensius Pallavicinus of the Society of Jesus, in his *Elogia*, part 1, elogium 4, speaking of the immaculate conception of Mary, says among other things: "It would be a monster if the progenitor of the Blessed Virgin were not innocent, she who alone is conceived under the horoscope of innocence. Eve, the guilty one, first conceived sin: Eve, the innocent one, is first conceived without sin."
But concerning this same innocence of the Virgin, Peter Pázmány, Cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, speaks most excellently in his sermon on the immaculate conception of the Blessed Virgin, when he says: "It can be said with all the greater assertion that the most blessed Mother of God was not only innocent of every original stain, by which original sin is worse and more destructive than all the venial sins of the whole world C (that itself is the fountain and root of actual sins), but—arguing from this point also, Augustine against Julian, ch. 9, near the end, proves that Christ never sinned, because He was not infected with the original stain, and adds: 'Assuredly, He would have committed a greater sin, had He possessed one as an infant.'—so he says. Who also adds below: 'It is a great axiom of the tribunal that if a question arises concerning anyone, whether he be guilty or innocent, he ought to be considered innocent, until it can be demonstrated by undoubted proofs and light clearer than the day that he is guilty.' See Aristotle, *Probl.* 29, p. 13: 'We would rather free a guilty man than condemn an innocent one.' Therefore, since it cannot be shown by certain and light-clear proofs that the most blessed Virgin is guilty of the original blight, nay rather, it is lawful by the Church to defend her without any error, we are bound not to deny it to her. Moreover, on the day of judgment it would not seem less unbecoming to complete in this the divine omnipotence and mercy, nor glorious to Judge Christ, who will then take an account from men of the divine precepts, if He had not so honored His Mother that the least of the angels of heaven would appear more innocent than she on that day, whereas they will appear throughout their whole eternity most innocent without any fault, yet their Queen, and the Mother of the most holy and omnipotent, had at one time been with a stain. Clearly, it does not seem less becoming that Christ should have cared less about the honor of His Mother and the manifestation of His own all-encompassing purity and mercy, both by withholding from His Mother a lesser prerogative, which the angels could say, upon the proclamation of that day, that they were more innocent than their own Queen, as well as by exalting His mercy, which was not lacking in the most excellent mode of redemption even preserving her from original sin. For, as Antonius Navarrus of the Dominican family says in a sermon on the conception of the Blessed Virgin: 'If God made the angels most pure spirits, why would He not make their Queen purer? [end of page 1175] beginning of column 1176〗 A vessel pure, A Eliseus chose, in which salt would be placed to heal the waters of Jericho; so also the most pure vessel, and adorned with every precious stone, was the Blessed Virgin, in whom was to be stored Christ, the true salvation of peoples, who are signified in the waters, according to that of John: 'Many waters, many peoples.' Into a malicious soul wisdom will not enter, nor will it dwell in a body subject to sins, otherwise, the devil would have mocked and derided in a voice of exultation that he had possessed it before God later chose her for a Mother. God did not allow the demon to assume a dove to deceive Eve (for under the aspect of a dove, just as under the clothing of sheep, a feigned fraud would be better concealed than under a serpent's skin), because the Holy Spirit was about to assume a dove at the baptism of Christ; so neither was it fitting that she, from whom the Son of God was to be born, should ever have been the lot of Satan." So he says. Therefore, that on the day of judgment the celestial spirits might not appear more innocent than their Queen, she was conceived without any stain of sin, and perhaps for this reason she is called by Saint Joseph by the title of "the most innocent." [(71)] Because she is as alien to every contamination in body as in soul. Saint Anastasius Sinaita favors this when, in Book 1 of his *Hexaemeron*, he calls the Mother of God: "The full moon, which never waned nor failed, nor was deprived of essential light, namely her virginity." For the essential light explaining virginity does not speak of the virginity of the body alone, for this cannot be called the essential light of grace and sanctity, for its lack can be combined with exceeding sanctity from the light of grace, as happened to Saint Anne; but it speaks of integral virginity or the purity of the virgin, namely of body and soul, whose purity the Fathers also called integrity and virginity. Therefore, the most sacred Virgin did not suffer a waning or defect in her integrity, either of body or of soul, which, although created in sanctity, was never bereft of the essential light of grace in the soul, nor of the superadded splendor of incorruption in the body, namely, all-encompassing virginity and purity. Saint Augustine and other Fathers said that the Virgin conceived the Word in her mind before her flesh, denoting her faith and will required for the assumption of humanity into her womb. And so the virtue of the soul was required for the divine conception. Wherefore it was fitting that the soul of Mary should have been no less pure, and integral, and a virgin from every contamination of fault, than her flesh pure and incorrupt. And lest anyone should understand Saint Anastasius himself to speak only of the perpetual virginity of the body, Saint Anastasius himself explains this, adding: "Mary remains a virgin as regards the soul": but perpetual virginity as regards the soul is perpetual integrity as regards sin, whether actual or original. See Nieremberg in *Exceptionibus*, ch. 13.
Blessed Albert the Great, ch. 181, on the *Missus est*, defining the most proper essence of virginity, says thus: "Virginity is a withdrawal from every evil, comprising as much the evil of the soul as of the body." And indeed, a greater account was taken by God of spiritual purity than of corporal integrity, because, as Augustine taught, Book x, *De mendacio ad Consent.*, ch. 20: "Whatever can be violated in the body is less than whatever can be violated in the soul."
Abacuc once foresaw you in the Spirit as a mountain untouched by the hand of a stone-cutter, from which God was manifested and brought salvation to us, O Virgin. You have brought forth the Word made flesh, bearing a twofold power of operation, O maiden who knew not wedlock, and you remained an undefiled Virgin. You have now undone the defeat of the first mother Eve, having given birth to the Redeemer of all, and Savior and Creator and Lord, O Mother of God alone, blessed among women. Therefore, we glorify you with faith. You have brought forth for us a new infant, consubstantial with the Father, O pure one, restoring again to its ancient beauty the human nature that had been corrupted.
The seas of sins and the waves of despair toss my mind; have mercy, O Lady, and stretch out your hand to me and save me, you who gave birth to the Savior. Slipping of my own will, and encompassed by shameful deeds, I flee to you; help me, O Lady, providing ways of repentance to my humble soul, that I may glorify you. Break the manifold chains of my offenses, O Bride of God, who gave birth, beyond words, to the God who takes away the sin of the world, blessed, pure, eternally glorified.
The shadow of the Law ceased, when you, O Lady, gave birth to the Giver of the Law, who illuminates the world with grace; him you always entreat, that he may quickly take pity on me, who am subject to the law of sin. The Word of the Father, who created the heavens by his nod and the earth by his will, and fashioned man, O immaculate one, did not disdain, as you plainly know, to build a body of flesh for himself from you, wishing to restore our nature, which had been crushed by the deceit of the serpent, O Virgin, only merciful one.
O Virgin, lover of goodness, make good my soul, which has been corrupted by sins, O you who brought forth the all-good Word. Having given birth to the Lover of mankind and Redeemer, O admirable and goodness-loving Lady, grant me release from my sins by your prayers, and make good my soul, O all-pure one, which has been perverted by evil thoughts, and show it redeemed from deadly passions, O all-blameless one.
From the Double Canon on the feast of the holy martyrs Agathonicus and Lupus, day 22
The great miracle, surpassing wonders, is seen in your delivery; for you gave birth to Christ, who came in the likeness of flesh, without change or confusion. Like a beautiful dawn you bring forth from your womb, O Lady who knew not wedlock, Jesus, the illumination of all and God of all; he who diminishes the night of idolatry with undying rays, and illuminates the world.
He who is by nature uncircumscribed, having received our form from you, O Lady, accepted circumscription according to the flesh, being known in two substances and wills. God having dwelt in the midst of you as He knows, He did not disturb the barriers of virginity, O chaste one, but established all upon the immovable rock of faith.
He who rides upon the shoulders of the Cherubim, having become incarnate in a manner befitting God as a man from you, O chaste one, is set in your arms like an infant, and acts as an infant, saving the first-formed man who once acted with childish folly.
Upon you, the abyss of wisdom, Jesus, descended like rain, finding you alone pure, O Mother of God and Virgin, and He flooded the grievous torrents of impiety with divine grace.
Foreseeing your wonders in the divine Spirit, Isaiah cried out: Behold, you shall have in your womb Him who is incomprehensible, becoming incarnate, O immaculate one.
Let us venerate the chaste one with a chaste mind; let us adorn the beauty of Jacob with divine deeds, and piously praise her as the Mother of our God.
You remain a Virgin after you have brought forth Christ, as you were before; you nourish with milk, O chaste and adorable one, Him who grants food to all. O mystery full of wonder and incomprehensible!
You have brought forth Him whom the Father generated from eternity before the ages, and you have suckled at your breasts the Nourisher. O miracle exceeding all mind! O mystery surpassing all speech, O chaste one!
God became man from you; He deified the mass of men, O inviolate one, and made those who call you blessed partakers of the divine nature, O truly blessed among women, O chaste one.
The Only One who dwells in the heavens chose you alone as the beauty of Jacob; and having dwelt in your midst, O untouched and blessed one, He in no way disturbed the barriers of your virginity, O blessed one.
We name you the Tabernacle, and the table, and the divine ark, and the vessel holding the manna of life, and the holy mountain, O Virgin Mary, ever blessed.
(73) When the Blessed Virgin was blessed, she was such also in her creation, and consequently she avoided the curse of original sin at that time. The Church favors this in the Responsorium of the feast of the Circumcision, when it says: “And blessed forever, she brought forth to us God and man.” As if the Church were to say: Because the Blessed Virgin brought forth to us God and man, she was blessed forever. But what is “blessed forever,” if not always blessed, that is, from the beginning of her creation and thereafter? For eternity looks to every difference of time, and excludes no moment of time, but comprehends every part entirely and totally. Therefore, Mary was always blessed, and in every difference of time; she could not, therefore, incur original sin, the grace of blessing, which went before her, standing in the way.
All creation blesses your birth-giving, which has crowned us with blessings and removed the curse. O blessed alone, O glorious One, who have filled our race with grace!
I, the prodigal, having a mind given to sin, a corrupt life, a soul laden with offenses, and a defiled heart, prostrate myself before you, Lady. Help me and grant me correction before the cutting sickle of death overtakes me.
With the rays of the Light that dwells in you, O Bride of God, illuminate my soul; raise me up as I lie in the pit of perdition, terrifying the enemies who always afflict my heart and compel me to pursue the passions.
*From the Canon for the Holy Hieromartyr Eutyches, the 24th day.*
In you, O Virgin, I place the hope of my salvation; wash me entirely clean from the filth of sins and make me pure, perfectly pleasing to your Son, and doing His most holy will.
Rejoice, you who alone gave birth to Joy inexpressibly! Rejoice, chariot and cloud of the Word; rejoice, throne of God, Virgin who knowest no man; rejoice, glory of the holy ones; rejoice, crown of martyrs.
Alone among women, you remained a virgin both before and after childbirth; for it was God who, beyond the reach of speech, was innovating the natures, becoming incarnate of you ineffably; He who is above before the ages, and was born on earth at the end of the ages, O wholly immaculate one.
O Mother-Virgin Maiden, who gave birth to the incomprehensible Word; O Bride of God, glory of the angels and wound of the demons; make my heart, wounded by sins, worthy of divine healing.
My mind’s wanderings and the troublesome and terrible movements of my soul, O Virgin, correct, and save me; guard me from those who cruelly attack me day by day.
Venerable prophets, looking from afar with the eye of the mind into the depth of your ineffable mystery, manifested your childbirth to all in various figures and ways, O Virgin, crying out: Blessed is the God of the Fathers.
My soul is dead from the serpent’s bite; you, who alone clearly gave birth to Life, O most immaculate one, bring it to life! And guide me happily along the way so that I may perform the wills of Him who was born of you for our sake, O Virgin, crying: Priests, bless the Lord.
We cry out to you with the voice of Gabriel: Rejoice, chosen earth; rejoice, golden table; rejoice, refuge of men; rejoice, boast of martyrs; rejoice, delight of the angels, holy Theotokos, bulwark of those who call you blessed with sincere faith.
*MONTH OF SEPTEMBER.*
*From the Canon for the Holy Martyr Anthimus, the 3rd day.*
The Lord, who arose from you as He knows how, [guides] the choirs
of athletes, O chaste one, those who represent within themselves all His life-giving passions and the unjust death that justified us sinners.
You have become beautiful, O most chaste one, having brought forth the Son and Word of the Father, who is more beautiful than all those born of earth, whom the noble martyrs, loving, were shone upon by glory.
The Word, not leaving empty the Paternal bosom, was reclined in your bosom, O maiden, as an infant, wishing to restore me who am subject to corruption.
The shadows of the Law declared that radiance which arose from you, O most immaculate maiden, and illumined the choirs of athletes who praise you.
O unwedded one, you who dried up the plants of malice with your sprout, root out the thorns of my passions, and cause divine thoughts to sprout from my soul.
Because of the excess of His love for mankind and kindness toward men, the Word appeared from you incarnate, O Virgin, saving those who sing: Blessed be the God of our fathers.

The flaming sword, which of old prohibited the entry to Paradise, now retreats and turns its back to those who voluntarily represent in themselves the venerable passions of Christ, wounded by the lance, and who honor you, O Virgin, who are superior to all honor.
*From the double Canon in memory of the miracle wrought at Colossae, or Chonae, by the holy Archangel Michael, day 6.*
O Virgin, totally pure, the adornment of angels and help of men; help me who am tossed in the sea and always falling and perishing in the storm of sin.
O unintelligible miracle, how the incomprehensible God has been united to mortals, born of you in flesh according to hypostasis, O unwedded one, that He might save me who am subject to corruption through the deceit of the serpent.
He who created immaterial minds by the nod of His will, voluntarily dwelt in your material womb, O most pure one, becoming visible in flesh, He who was invisible.
Daniel describes you as a great mountain, O inviolate one, but Habbakuk as a mountain overshadowed by virtues, and David as a curdled mountain: for from you God was incarnate to redeem the world.
That master of sacred things formerly understood intellectually in the Spirit the miracle of your birth-giving, seeing you most manifestedly as a mountain overshadowed, from which the holy God came incarnate.
Gabriel came from the highest, bringing you "Hail," O most chaste one: with him, therefore, we cry out: Hail,
gate, through which alone Christ God passed, saving the human race. A God made you higher than the intellectual angels, when He descended and entered into your most pure womb, O inviolate one. Therefore, pray always to Him that He may have mercy on those who praise you. O Virgin, who surpass the angelic Powers and have given birth to the God and King of all, together with them pour forth prayers, O most holy Lady, for our salvation. Blessed is the people that always calls you blessed, O blessed one, who gave birth to the blessed God, who for His mercy’s sake deified men through an ineffable union. The prophet foresaw you as a scroll, O Virgin, in which the Word is written by the finger of the Father: entreat Him, as a suppliant, to inscribe in the book of life us who piously glorify you. Gabriel the archangel, seeing the eternal Word of the great Mind truly dwelling in you, O maiden, ineffably and formidably, cried out: "Hail, throne of the Most High, O blessed one." Since you have given birth in the flesh to the Savior and God, the Redeemer and Master, O most chaste Lady, pray to Him always, O immaculate one, that we may receive from Him the removal of most grievous evils, and the remission of many sins, singing the praises of His mercies which surpass all thought. The divine archangel, the nuptial announcer, standing near, addressed to you the "Hail," O unwedded Bride of God, the glory of the angels, and the salvation and rampart of men. You conceived Fire, yet it did not consume your womb, O Virgin; you gave birth to the Word of the Father, who delivers from irrationality those who obeyed the words of the seducer, and were disobedient to God their maker, the lover of mankind. By the voice of the angel Gabriel, O most clean one, you conceived God the Word, who created the heavenly hosts by a word, and provides the word by which we may praise His holy descent and emptying, which surpasses all word and thought. O Virgin, you appeared more spacious than the heavens, containing within yourself ineffably God, whom the choirs of the incorporeal ones mystically praise. From the Canon for the Holy Martyrs Menodora, Metrodora, and Nymphodora, Day 10
As a living bridal chamber, as an incorrupt tabernacle, as a heavenly gate, as a divine table, as a palace and throne of the Master, let us honor the immaculate Mary with hymns.
