You entice the hearts of the faithful ever to glorify you with insatiable desire, O Mother of God and Lady; for you are accounted the glory of men, having brought forth the Lord of glory, O immaculate one.
For in the Old Testament, Christ and the most blessed Virgin did not exist, who are truly, and properly, and entirely, and antonomastically immaculate. But indeed, since such persons did not exist in the Old Testament, it is no wonder if the name "immaculate" were attributed to the holier ones, especially since it is not attributed to them absolutely. Thus, when it is said: "Blessed are the immaculate," it is added, "in the way," that is, in the mode of operating, not absolutely and entirely. David also said, "I will be immaculate," [which] indicates that at some time he was not such. Job also, who had acknowledged and supposed himself to have been conceived in sin, afterwards called himself immaculate regarding the present, not the past, just as others are signified as immaculate regarding the future in Scripture. However, the mode by which Josephus and other Fathers call the Virgin immaculate, absolutely and antonomastically, is not found elsewhere among other saints; and it indicates something most special and greater than all the sons of Adam, as Nierembergius observes in his *Epistolary Dissertations*, epistle 8.
You have become a luminous tabernacle of purity, and you bear the Giver of Light, made flesh as a man, who for the sake of his love for mankind appeared as one of us, and abolished corruption; O incorrupt recovery of mortals.
You have become a pure dwelling-place of the wisdom of the Father, beyond reason, O chaste Virgin, through whom we have now been delivered from the malice of the sophist.
Rain down upon me, O all-pure one, the forgiveness of transgressions; visit me, who am sick and tossed by the storms of life and the passions of the body.
The Lord of glory was incarnate from your virginal blood in the manner which He alone knows, O all-praised one, saving us by His goodness.
You appeared, having deified the human mold by your divine birth-giving, O Virgin all-immaculate; wherefore we the faithful rightfully glorify you.
Distill upon us your mercies, O maiden, according to your custom, and beseech, O chaste one, the forgiveness of all transgressions, whether committed in knowledge or in ignorance through negligence.
Beseech for me illumination, you who gave birth to the Light that shone forth from Light, driving far away from me the darkness of temptations and pleasures, O undefiled Lady, protection that is not put to shame.
From the Canon for our Holy Father Eumenius, Bishop of Gortyna, Day 18.
The prophecies concerning you are now fulfilled, O Lady Theotokos; for Him whom the prophets announced in sublime speech, you held in your womb in two perfect natures.
O Mary, golden censer, drive away the foul odor of my passions, and strengthen me, who am shaken by the assaults of the deceitful enemy.
In the apostolic liturgy of the Ethiopians, also, since it is said to have proceeded from the apostles, it is said thus in the prayer to the Virgin Mother of God: "Rejoice, Immaculate, truly Queen. Rejoice, glory of our parents." As if it said (as Nieremberg says in his *Exceptions*, cap. 13): "You, who, as a true queen and august one, did not lie under the severe law of the servants' penalty concerning the contraction of a stain, and thus restored the lost beauty of the human race, rejoice, Lady. Truly queen, because you were immaculate in such a way that you never had to serve anyone except the One God, to whom to serve is truly to reign. Therefore she did not have any sin, when that is of a certain most miserable servitude. Rejoice therefore in such a good, in such glory, which our parents can call their own, since with this their disgrace was compensated. Thus you restored with great honor the ruined state of justice and the beauty of the original glory of our parents."
Sacred voices long ago announced the depth of your birth, the fulfillment of which we now behold, O immaculate one. As a new infant you have brought forth for us the Pre-eternal Son, who is before all ages, O most immaculate one; who is twofold in two voluntary operations, being at once man and God, O all-blameless one. When the heavenly rain had descended upon you, O perpetual Virgin, it irrigated the desolate earth with the streams of divine knowledge and showed it to be fecund. Your womb has become a dwelling place for the immaterial light, which by the dread splendors of divine knowledge diminished atheism, O immaculate Virgin-Bride, whom we praising cry out: Blessed are you, O God of our fathers.
The most sacred chorus of the prophets truly described you beforehand, O venerable Virgin, calling you a mountain untouched by the hand of a stonemason; a rod and a gate through which the Most High passed, in the manner He Himself knows, and left you closed once again. From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyrs Trophimus, Sabbatius, and Dorymedon, day 19.
Generously illuminated by the enlightening fount of your graces, O most dear to God and only gate of light, the noble martyrs, praising you, passed through the deepest darkness of intolerable torments. As the pure palace of the King, the threefold assembly of martyrs invoking you as a helper, O immaculate Virgin, cast down the temples of demons, and were transferred to the temple of supernal glory, always honoring you with praise.

the manna, and the divine table, and the lamp flashing with gold; for you brought forth the light for the revelation of the nations, the light which illuminates the ends of the earth with the knowledge of God.

C Dei Genitricem, or Mother of God, they add almost always the title "immaculate." Thus the sixth general synod held at Constantinople under Pope Agatho, in action 5: "We confess our Lord Jesus Christ to be incarnate of the Holy Spirit, from our immaculate Lady, the Mother of God." Thus the Council of Trent, sess. vi, Can. 4: "The holy synod declares that it is not its intention to include in this decree, where it treats of original sin, the immaculate Virgin Mary, Mother of God." St. James in his Liturgy, which is found in the *Bibliotheca Veterum Patrum*: "Commemorating our most holy immaculate Lady, the Mother of God." Thus Origen, homil. 1: "Mother of God, immaculate." And the Fathers, both Greek and Latin, everywhere call the Mother of God not only immaculate, but often plainly, fully, entirely, and altogether immaculate, or most immaculate. Whence I conclude the privilege of immunity from original sin in the Blessed Virgin from her divine maternity, as follows: "The word 'immaculate' (as an anonymous author says in a certain suppliant booklet offered to the sacred Congregation of the Inquisition) expresses holiness through a negative term, that is, through the negation of any stain whatsoever; therefore it seems to exclude a stain for any instant. Therefore this word 'immaculate,' without any other restrictive addition, attributed to the Mother of God, signifies entirely that she was, absolutely and simply, and thus throughout her whole life, and consequently in the first instant of her conception, devoid of every stain. For just as a woman would in no way be called a 'virgin' absolutely who, although she might be chaste for a time, had nevertheless at some point fallen from the flower of virginity; so the Mother of God, or theotokos, could not be called immaculate absolutely and by antonomasia, however much she might have shone thereafter, if at any time she had been subject to an original stain, since the word 'immaculate' denotes the negation of any contracted stain whatsoever, specifically. But if you object that the argument is weak which is drawn from this word 'immaculate' for the Mother of God's immunity from original sin, since in Scripture those are often called 'immaculate' who are subject to an original stain (see Psalm 36: 'The Lord knows the days of the immaculate'; and Psalm 18: 'Then I shall be immaculate, and I shall be cleansed from the greatest transgression'; and Psalm 17: 'And I shall be immaculate with him,' and elsewhere; answer with Velasquez, *De Maria concepta*, book iv, Dissert. 3, single annotation: 'Names and epithets are to be understood according to the persons to whom they are given, and Christ is called "immaculate" in one way, as in Heb. ix: "He offered himself immaculate to the living God"; and 1 Pet. i: 'With the precious blood as of an immaculate Lamb, Christ"; but the Blessed Virgin is called "immaculate" in another way, and other humans are called "immaculate"]. For as Christ the Lord, subsisting in a divine person, is immaculate by his nature, so it is fitting for the Blessed Virgin to be immaculate in that way which becomes the Mother of God, and consequently to be immaculate in every respect, according to the proper signification of the word, through the negation of any stain whatsoever for any instant. Which indeed, as it does not befit other men when we call them 'immaculate,' we do not mean to signify that, but that they possess such purity as is possible for human nature (subject to original sin). From which it seems to me I can infer that in the view of the councils and the Fathers, the Mother of God is called 'immaculate' in the sense that she is entirely beautiful and without any actual or original stain, and that nothing else rings in the ears of all the faithful than that it is the Mother of God who was immaculate, just as her very conception was immaculate. For from the fact that we can—as we ought—say with "full cheeks" that the Mother of God is immaculate, it is clearly deduced, according to the doctrine of the anonymous doctor, that the conception of the Mother of God herself is to be honored with the same title. For, with the anonymous author being the assertor in the cited suppliant booklet, the word 'immaculate' expresses holiness through a negative term, that is, through the negation of any stain whatsoever, and therefore excludes a stain for any instant. Therefore, if the Mother of God is immaculate, any stain whatever is to be denied to her, for any instant whatever. Therefore, original stain, even for the first instant of life. Otherwise, if at that instant she is not called 'immaculate'... this word (in the judgment of the anonymous author) excludes both any stain whatsoever and for any instant whatsoever. Whence by contradiction, as I think,
be merciful, have mercy on my most unhappy soul, which, on account of the passions of sin, has been gravely darkened and weakened.
You brought forth a new infant as a babe, O inviolate One, He who is before the ages and shone forth without time from the Father who lacks beginning. Him, as a suppliant, entreat for the world, O Bride of God.
Beyond mind, you have brought forth Him who lacks time; beyond the reach of speech, you have brought forth the Creator, O most holy One, who redeems from all corruption those who praise you as the Mother of God.
You have brought forth the incorporeal God clothed in a body, O most pure One, who redeems us who chant with fear: Blessed art Thou, O God.
Altogether elect, altogether beautiful you have appeared, O Virgin ever-glorious, whom God has sanctified and chosen; therefore we praise you unto all ages.
By the light of your countenance, O intellectual gate of light, illuminate me who lie in the darkness of passions, that the night of death may not overtake me, O chaste and immaculate One, cutting short the hopes of my salvation.
From the Canon for the Translation of Saint John the Evangelist, the 26th day.
You who conceived God, who for our sake became man, entreat Him, O chaste One, that in the day of judgment He may have mercy on us, who have committed many sins against Him.
When the Word, incarnate from you ineffably, O Mother of God, hung uplifted upon the wood of the cross, He commended you, a maiden, to the virgin disciple as a virgin.
Let us praise the divine temple of God; let us all with clear voices bless the holy Virgin, we who through her have been deified and delivered from the gravest evils.
When you stood by the cross of your Son together with the beloved disciple, O most immaculate One, you were groaning, shedding tears, and marveling at His great compassion toward men.
In the likeness of flesh, God was made known to mortals from you, O most pure One; whom do you ever entreat, O most holy One, that He may bring to death the ruinous carnal reasonings of our flesh.
We bless you, O most immaculate One, who brought forth the blessed Lord, who with divine blessings crowned human nature that was cursed, and renewed us who had been reduced to the oldness of corruption.
Jesus the Savior, whom you clothed with a body from your own chaste blood, O most glorious of God, entreat C that He may have mercy on your servants, and raise them from eternal punishment. [Let us bring a voice of thanksgiving...]
care, that He may have mercy upon us, who are Your servants, and deliver us from eternal punishment. A Let us raise up clear and manifest voices in thanksgiving to the Mother of God, and let us exclaim: Hail, most high throne of God; hail, cloud of light; hail, paradise, through whom we have been made worthy of the paradise of delights.
From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyr Callistratus, on the 27th day.
Alone among women, O most immaculate one, without the knowledge of man, you bear in your womb, beyond the order of nature, One of the Trinity; therefore we glorify you, and Him who was born from you above all cause and reason.
Make urgent supplication to your Son, O Virgin, to save us from the dangers we fear, and from eternal punishment.
My heart, defiled by passions, O Maiden, cleanse, and make it a pure vessel of divine illuminations.
You were shown to be the Rising of the Sun of justice, O most immaculate one; Him, beseech for the salvation of those who sincerely glorify you.
Sanctify my mind and enlighten my heart, O holy Mother of God, and deliver me from the straits that overwhelm me, that I may glorify you, O Theotokos, ever-Virgin.
Him who was incarnate of you, beyond mind and speech, O full of divine grace, beseech for the salvation of those who honor you with affection, and who shout in unison: Blessed are You, O God of our fathers.
As you are higher than all creatures, O Maiden most pleasing to God, and immune from every stain, make my mind higher than the scandals of the deceiver, O most immaculate one.
With the voice of Gabriel, we cry out to you with rejoicing mind: Hail, joy of the faithful; hail, golden lampstand and table; mountain and intellectual gate; hail, divine
vehicle of Christ the King; hail, dissolution of the curse, O you who are blessed in all things.
From the Canon for Saint Epicaris, the 27th day
Behold, the laws of nature are renewed in you, O you who are immune from all stain; for you gave birth to God and man above the laws of nature and reason, whom the young girls have fervently loved with desire.
You remained supernaturally a virgin after birth, O most dear to God; and wounded by love for you, this virgin and martyr struggled eagerly, and after you, O chaste one, she was led to her Spouse, leading the dance together with the faithful virgins.
The substantial Word of the Father, without any change in Himself, was incarnate from you, O Virgin, with whose love the soul of Epicharis was kindled and made worthy of the celestial bridal chambers.
You embrace, O Mother of God, filled with divine grace alone, within your maternal arms, Him who embraces and contains all things.
Perceiving the most sweet fragrance of the Son incarnate from you, the most illustrious maiden, after you, O inviolate one, was led to Him with exultation of soul.
You have imparted new laws to nature, O Virgin, when you gave birth above the order of nature; for He who was incarnate from you in an ineffable manner was God and man.
O chaste Virgin, you remained after childbirth a matter of venerable wonder, O inviolate one: for you gave birth to the Word of God, whom the virgin Epicharis, confessing in the midst of wicked tyrants, proclaimed: Blessed is God, etc.
With the most sacred voices, the most sacred prophets manifestly foretold you as the Mother of God, O chaste and inviolate one: whom we superexalt above all, as the ruler of all, through all ages.
Light-bearing cloud, you who gave birth to the divine light, dispel the clouds of my miserable soul, O Mother of God, and illumine me with the light of salvation, you who alone are good; that I may unceasingly magnify you with faith and affection.
From the Canon for the feast of Saint Gregory of Great Armenia, and the Holy Martyrs Ripsimia, Gaiana, and their companions, the 30th day
Women, strengthened by the cross of Him who was incarnate from you, O chaste one, struggled steadfastly, and were led to Him after you, O Virgin: and they shine with the splendors of virginity and the blood of martyrs.
Ripsimia the martyr, knowing you alone to be the Virgin Mother, was charmed by your beauty, and was led after you to Christ, gleaming with her contests.
As one beautiful, as one chosen, as one fair, the young maidens loved you, who struggled with Ripsimia, O Virgin-Mother Mary, and after you they were led to your Son, rejoicing.
Sensing the fragrance of the ointment of the Word that shone forth from you, O chaste Virgin, they were pleasing to Him through athletic contests, rejoicing.
As soon as Ripsimia learned that He who was incarnate from you, O Mother of God, had been crucified, she was at the same time crucified with Him, as a lamb with the shepherd, as an immaculate victim of God.
Adorned with the crowns of martyrdom, the maidens were led to God, who blossomed from a Virgin, melodiously crying out: Blessed are You, O God, etc.
Not fearing the multitude of torments, and not yielding to the pleasures of the flesh, Ripsimia confessed the Lord born of a Virgin, crying out: Bless and praise the Lord.
Illumined by the light of the countenance that shone forth from you, O perpetual Virgin, Ripsimia with affection endured His sufferings, and expressed His death in her own flesh; whence she now exults with Him.
MONTH OF OCTOBER
From the Canon for the feast of Saint Charitina the Martyr, the 5th day
You have become a vessel capable of the divine nature, O Mother of God,
undefiled; wherefore Charitina, having longed with virginal love to follow you, has been brought to your Son.
Thee alone, blessed among women, O chaste one, the martyr Charitina, loving, has been glorified by your good graces.
You gave birth to the Word of God made flesh, O undefiled Mother of God, whom Charitina, loving most fervently, overcame by her struggle against fire and multiform tortures.
Human thought is unable to conceive your conception, which is beyond understanding, O Mother and Virgin; for you gave birth to God.
Finding you to be her strength and support, O Virgin, Charitina endured scourging with constancy, and joyfully she is led behind you to the Lord of all.
O unique Virgin, the pure Word loved you, pure and incorrupt, and in you He fashioned the whole man in becoming incarnate, having glorified Charitina through your miracles.
You appeared higher than the heavens, having given birth to the heavenly God, O most pure one, who made heavenly the whole lump of earth-born men, and who adorned the venerable memory of Charitina, to whom we cry: All you works of the Lord, bless the Lord.
light has risen for us from your womb that knew no man, O Virgin, by whose rays the one named for joy was immediately illuminated, O Mother of God who knew not marriage.
From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyrs Eulampius and Eulampia, the 10th day
We, redeemed from the condemnation of our first parents by your birth, O undefiled Virgin, clearly and with voices of songs, we the faithful always call you blessed as the Mother of God.
Entreat, O most chaste Mother of God, that those who always honor you may be delivered from every evil invasion of enemies, from soul-destroying passions, and from grievous and troublesome dangers.
Habakkuk, having perceived you from afar most expressively, O chaste one, called you a mountain overshadowed by virtues, from which appeared to us He who illuminates our souls.
All the swords of the enemy have truly failed in the end, O undefiled, all-pure, chaste one; for you gave birth to the God of all, who by His cross cast down the pride of that enemy.
As rain, God has been poured out into your womb, because of His ineffable compassion, and He has watered all with a torrent of delights, O Lady, and has renewed the corrupted creation.
The furnace did not burn the three youths, prefiguring your birth; for the divine fire, not burning you, dwelt within you, and illuminated all who cry out: Blessed are You, the God of our fathers.
O Maid who knew not marriage, hail, all-pure, the harbor of those in a storm; hail, Bride of God, the [refuge/aid] of sinners.
Hail, propitiatory for sinners; hail, you who bore God incarnate. O receptacle of light, which from you, O Pure One, worthily shone forth, enlighten the eyes of my soul, O most immaculate one, and banish the darkness of ignorance, and cast down and utterly destroy the mists of sin.
*From the Canon for the feast of the holy Apostle Philip, one of the seven Deacons, day 11.*
He who created all things from that which was not, had you, O inviolate Mother of God, as the cause of His incarnation; therefore the faithful, as is due, call you blessed. You became a mystical candlestick, O Maiden, truly carrying that lamp which, by its supreme goodness, illuminated those previously held in the night of ignorance. Your Son, O most immaculate one, made those who were sons of men to be sons of God, being incarnate from your pure blood and born of you; therefore we glorify you. We who truly confess you as Theotokos are delivered from temptations and most difficult affairs by your intercessions before the God and Lord of all, O Virgin, most full of divine grace.
Beyond the laws of nature, your holy Mother bore you, Christ, the Creator of nature, and beyond nature she truly remained a virgin inviolate, O One superior to all goodness. We name you a Virgin-Mother, O Mary, Bride of God, we who through you, day and night, are delivered from the harmful violence of enemies, from all kinds of temptations, and from the defilements of the soul. Make my soul, shaken by the wickedness of the enemy, firm and stable, O chaste Virgin, you who received without disturbance Him who by His divine gaze shakes the universe. Every living thing sends forth towards you a grateful voice, crying out with joy and saying: Hail, fire-formed throne of the Most High; hail, most spacious region of God; hail, O chaste and most beautiful crown of the apostles.
*From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyrs Probus, Tarachus, and Andronicus, day 12.*
The Word, co-eternal with the Father and the holy Spirit, willingly inhabited a virginal womb and became flesh without change; and having suffered voluntarily, He prepared the divine hosts of martyrs to contend with faith. As beautiful, as fair, as elect, having chosen you, O inviolate one, the Word who gave existence to all things, desiring your undefiled and God-containing womb, dwelt within it, He who is above all substance. You alone bear in the womb God incarnate, who gave being to all things, whom confessionally and unshakably the divine martyrs contended [to proclaim] in the stadium, O Virgin Theotokos, the wonder of angels and the wound of demons, most worthy of all praise. You have become superior to the powers above, O Virgin, [as] the Word
brought forth from the Father, O Virgin, co-eternal with the same Father and likewise without beginning; by whose splendors the athletes, being illuminated, fled beyond the night of godlessness.
You conceived in your womb Him who is before the ages, O immaculate one; and you brought forth in the flesh Him who is by nature inaccessible; and you fed with milk Him who nourishes all things, O Mother of God, who have known not a man.
The most complete Word is emptied in your womb, not departing from the Father’s bosom, and flesh is seen, and an infant is born, to whom we sing joyfully, O Virgin: Blessed be the God of our fathers.
With the ranks of the incorporeal ones, with the armies of martyrs, with the apostles and prophets, let us all religiously and piously praise the Lady of all created things, as being holier than the Cherubim, and the only most chaste Mother of God, exalting Christ unto all ages.
Spare me, Savior, who were born and kept the one who bore you incorrupt after childbirth, when you sit to judge my works, overlooking my iniquities and my sins, as the sinless One, merciful God and lover of mankind.
From the Canon to the holy martyrs Carpus and Papylus, on the 13th day.
O gate of light, which from your incorruptible entrails shone forth, shed upon me the illuminating rays of repentance, and dissipate the darkness of my sins, O most divine and full of grace.
We have known, O Lord, that while you were God without beginning, you sustained having a beginning, and to proceed from the Virgin without mutation, whom you also preserved incorrupt and pure after childbirth.
The incontaminate bridal chamber of God, the mountain untouched by the hands of the stone-cutter, the holy ark and the table, and the censer of the immaterial coal, we all the faithful proclaim you to be, O chaste Virgin, totally immaculate.
Having you as a saving harbor, O Virgin, we who are constantly tossed on the sea of the direst evils, flee to you, and hoping in you, we do not fear the evil counsels of our enemies.
You conceived without experience of marital union, and brought forth beyond the manner of nature the incomprehensible God, the Creator of nature. O great mystery! O unintelligible miracle, O Virgin alone without any stain.
Draw me out of the mire of the passions, out of the abyss of sins, and rule me, your servant, who always confess you as the Mother of God. For you are always the raising up of those who fall.
You manifestly loosed the curse of our first mother, Eve, O Virgin.
The sacred chorus of the divine prophets proclaims you, O most pure one, to be the future Mother of God, to whom we all cry: Bless the Lord, all things, etc.
You carry in your arms, O most chaste one, like a Cherubic throne, Him who carries all, who for our sake was clothed in our flesh, and though He was simple, he appeared dual; whom do you always entreat for us who praise you.
From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyrs Nazarius, Gervasius, Protasius, and Celsus, on the 14th day.
Let us praise the most immaculate maiden, who alone in her womb comprehended the Lord who is before the ages: for she was made wider than the heavens, clothing God with a body for the sake of His own goodness.
The legal tabernacle prefigured you as being the future holy tabernacle of God, O chaste one, in which our propitiation would come, which grants sanctification to us all.
Not leaving empty the Paternal bosom, He
sat down in your most pure bosom, preparing a divine throne for all by His goodness, and glory that abides forever.
The sword which formerly guarded Eden is turned away from the faithful who are signed with the precious blood, which was once poured out from the side wounded by the lance, of Him who rose from you, O chaste one.
You innovated the laws of nature, O maiden Virgin, having brought forth God immortal, clothed in mortal flesh, that He might deify mortals by His goodness.
God, finding your womb a most luminous palace, dwelt within it, O most immaculate one, making those who cry out "Blessed are you, O God and Lord of our fathers," to be sons of light.
United to you in flesh according to substance, He who grants existence to all things reformed me entirely, and entirely renewed me who had grown old through transgressions; therefore we, the Virgin, praise you, O most chaste one, and superexalt you unto all ages.
The voice of the divine Gabriel we bring to you, O most chaste Maiden, rejoicing: Hail, full of grace, boast of martyrs and apostles, and salvation of all the faithful, Virgin Mother who knew not wedlock.
From the Canon for the Holy Martyr Longinus the Centurion, on the 16th day.
The Word of God was conceived in your womb by the Word, wishing by His goodness to free mortals from irrationality, O Virgin Mother, immaculate, blessed, all-blameless.
Heal my soul, laboring with the malady of the passions that assail it, O Mother of God, most chaste, and guide it toward salvation.
You brought forth beyond speech the Word, united according to hypostasis in your womb, and having become man, O immaculate one, showing Him to be twofold in wills and in energies.
Let us praise the Theotokos, who alone conceived God without the work of a man, we who have been saved through her, and let us bless her with affection.
Dry up and root out, O most immaculate one, the thorny follies of my heart, and show it to be fruitful through your mediation, O most immaculate Maiden.
As in a pure vessel the pure Word dwelt within you, O Maiden, willing through you to cleanse the pollutions of men.
For blessed is the fruit of your womb.
With mouth, and tongue, and soul I proclaim you, O God-bearer, and I entreat you, O immaculate one, enlighten my heart with your illumination, and deliver me from terrible darkness, while I cry out: All you works of the Lord, praise the Lord. You have appeared as the dwelling-place of the unsetting light, O Theotokos, through whom those who dwelt in darkness and in the shadow of death have seen the light: therefore illuminate the senses of my heart.
From the Canon for the feast of Saint Andrew of Crete the martyr, on the 17th day.
Always burdened by the sleep of negligence, I run to your protection, O immaculate Virgin Mother; rouse me to the vigilance of repentance, delivering me from the everlasting punishment that follows.
In the likeness of flesh you gave birth to the God-Word who is consubstantial with the Father, O all-blameless one, in a way surpassing reason, remaining a virgin after childbirth; therefore we call you blessed in faith.
You have cultivated, as a most fertile ear of grace, the one nourishing all who honor you in an orthodox manner, O all-praiseworthy Lady, the Lord who was incarnate from your womb.
You carry, O immaculate one, in your arms the one in an ineffable conception embracing those cast down by malice, and miserably enslaved to the deceiver, O all-praiseworthy Maiden; hence we glorify you as Theotokos.
The prophet of old foresaw thee as an intellectual lampstand, O chaste one, bearing the divine torch, Christ, by whom we all have been illuminated. Thou didst become a temple of the living God, in whom He who inhabits the heavens—having deigned in His great goodness to become man—ineffably made His dwelling, O Virgin worthy of all praise. Thou didst appear, O Virgin, to be wider than the heavens, containing in thy womb the God whom nothing can contain; entreat Him, O inviolate Lady, to deliver from lethal distress those who religiously praise and hymn thee. Thy womb became a dwelling-place of Light, which illuminated the world with the splendors of divinity and utterly banished the darkness of ignorance from the world; wherefore we glorify thee, O Maiden, who art free from all stain.
From the Canon for the feast of St. Varus the martyr, Day 19.
The supersubstantial Word dwelt in thy womb beyond the capacity of words, O immaculate one; and being born in a manner befitting God, He drew to Himself choirs of martyrs, with whom we sing hymns to thee. O Virgin Mother of God, I beseech thee, dispel the deepest darkness of my sloth and the clouds of my passions by the illumination of thy grace. Bring me up, O Lady, from the mud of passions and from the misery of thoughts that alienate me from God, who alone is pure, so that in faith I may call thee blessed. Having appeared truly holier than the Cherubim and Seraphim, O most immaculate one, sanctify all who now faithfully call thee blessed, and save those who celebrate thee with praises. Guide, O Lady, my miserable soul, which is always tossed about in the sea of most grievous evils, and bring it to a serene and tranquil harbor, while with a firm mind it calls thee blessed. Restore me, O Virgin, broken and contrite as I am from immeasurable transgressions, through thy mediation, applying a remedy to my soul and granting me speech to cry out: Blessed art thou, who gave birth in the flesh to God. I join sins to sins, and I do not tremble at the future formidable mystery; take away, O chaste one, the hardness of my soul, and by thy intercession convert me and save me. When the Lord had appeared from thee like a shining cloud, O Virgin, He utterly abolished the idols of Egypt; and He deemed worthy to bear the palm a multitude of those who strove, who imitated Him in enduring His venerable sufferings.
From the Canon for the feast of St. Artemius the martyr, Day 20.
The incorporeal Word, having been incarnate from thee in the manner that befitted God, O most chaste one, through an excess of love for mankind, joined Himself to sufferings
and brought about impassibility for men; for the glorious Lord has been gloriously glorified.
He has been incarnate by His own will from thy blood, O Lady, O spotless one, the Lord, saving humanity; and He drew to Himself the throngs of martyrs.
God, O unpolluted and incorrupt one, preserved thee a virgin after childbirth, He who was well-pleased in thy womb to take upon Himself my whole humanity through extreme goodness.
He who was born of thee by His own will for our sake, O Lady, having for us endured the cross and burial, as a mighty one made Artemius a most steadfast witness of His sufferings.
O Theotokos and Virgin, save thy servants who are tossed by the surge of afflictions and beaten by the uprisings of the billows.
Thou didst give birth in a manner befitting God, O all-blameless Virgin, to Him who caused the spring of immortality to gush forth for the dead; therefore, entreat Him, O pure one, to put to death the passions of our body and to make us worthy of eternal life.
Thou didst recreate us, O all-holy one, who had flowed away by the bitter tasting of the tree and had fallen by sliding, having given birth to the Creator and the subsistent Word, O undefiled one, to whom we cry: "All the works of the Lord, bless the Lord."
Illumine me with the light of thy countenance, O Lord, as I am covered by the darkness of negligence, having to intercede for me, O Word, thy true, most chaste Mother, together with the splendors of the angels and the glorious Artemius.
From the Canon for the feast of St. Abercius, Bishop of Hierapolis, and the seven holy youths in Ephesus, on the 22nd day.
Eloquent and expert tongues are not able to declare thy conception, which surpasses speech; for thou didst give birth in the flesh to God, O all-holy one, who became like us through goodness.
Having found thee purer, O all-holy one, than all creation, the Pure One dwelt within thee, wishing to dwell…
in the one who had inhabited Adam, to eliminate the iniquity that had dwelt in Adam, as a lover of mankind.
He who was before God invisible, was seen, O Virgin, out of compassion, becoming incarnate from thy womb; for this reason we bless thee with faith.
Christ, having taken me from thy divine blood as a garment, O undefiled one, clothed me—the same one who had once been stripped—with the stole of grace.
Thou hast healed the contrition and ancient misery of the earth-born, bringing the remedy, O all-immaculate Bride of God, having given birth to Him who, for the sake of His ineffable mercy, bore our infirmities.
Thou hast brought forth a new infant, O Virgin, who refashioned the world, worn out by old age, with divine knowledge; therefore we glorify thee.
The laws are miraculously innovated in thee, O Virgin: for thou bringest forth without seed God the Saviour, and thou remainest a virgin as thou wast before. O strange wonder! For this reason we religiously and piously proclaim thee the Mother of Emmanuel.
Dissolve, O chaste one, the very hard callous of my soul; and grant me, with easy and ready sense, to attend to the divine commandments of thy Son.
Through thee, O most holy Bride of God, we who were dead have been accounted worthy of life; and being slaves of corruption, we have clearly obtained the riches of incorruption.
Mortify the wisdom of my flesh, O Virgin, who brought forth Life, who took away death by death, and glorified the young children by a wondrous rising.
He was born of thee, O Maiden, whom the Father begat before the ages, who is known in two substances and wills (God, that is, and man) by all who cry out with faith: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.
Thou hast appeared, O Theotokos, higher than the angels; thou hast appeared truly the strength of athletes; thou hast appeared, O most chaste one, the salvation of those who recognize thee as the truest bearer of the Word.
Behold the couch of Solomon, which the mighty ones now surround, namely the prophecies of divinely inspired Scripture, in which Christ God rested through divine incarnation, O blessed and full of grace.
Heal my sick soul, O Virgin, with a healing hand, and wipe away the filth of the passions clinging to me, and set me, made whole, before the tribunal of the Almighty God, that I may sing: All ye works, praise the Lord.
The prophet of old foresaw thee as an enlightening lampstand, O most chaste Virgin, truly bearing within thyself the divine lamp: that is, the only supersubstantial God, who for the sake of the depths of His mercy became man from thee.
Thou bearest in thine arms Him who holds all things by His divine palm; whom supplicate, O Virgin, that I, who am alone
condemned, may be received into His arms on account of His ineffable piety, and be saved.
From the Canon for the Holy Martyrs Marcianus and Martyrius, on the 25th day.
Thou who didst conceive the timeless Son of God didst clothe Him with a body, O pure one, He having become man for the sake of His ineffable mercy; wherefore, worshipping Him, we piously glorify thee, the cause of the deification of all.
Thou art adorned with fringes of gold, as a Queen, and now standest at the right hand of the Master and God, O Lady, interceding for thy servants.
The holy prophet of old called thee a divine mountain of virtue, O all-pure Virgin, shaded on all sides, from which the saving Word has been made manifest for the restoration and illumination of our souls.
Truly, O pure one, thou didst bring forth the Son of God, consubstantial with the Father and the divine Spirit, O Mother of God; whom cease not to entreat, that He may have mercy upon our souls.
With mouth and tongue we confess thee in truth to be the Mother of our God, O Virgin; earnestly entreat Him, O pure one, for the salvation of our souls.
Having been redeemed by thy birth-giving, O Mother of God, from eternal condemnation, we cry out to thee always, "Hail, O blessed and full of grace."
Thou didst revive us who were dead, having brought forth the Life of all, O Mother of God and Lady, the glory of martyrs and the salvation and rampart of men.
Thou art the dwelling-place of light, O pure one; illuminate the pupils of my soul, darkened by carelessness, and wrapped forever in the deepest darkness of sloth, O all-undefiled one, so that I may in faith call thee blessed.
From the Canon for the memorial of the earthquake, on the 26th day.
Suppliantly we cry to thee, Mother of God, showing your accustomed compassion toward this city and people; deliver us from a most severe earthquake and destruction.
We pray thee, O unblemished Mother of God, who alone art good, earnestly entreat the all-good Word to deliver us from the distress of the earthquake and from every wrath.
Acknowledging thee, O Lady, to be the temple of God, we lift up our wretched hands in thy holy temple in prayer; look upon our affliction and grant us thy help.
Now is the time for help come, now is the need for reconciliation, O pure one, with thy Son and Lord, so that He may have mercy upon us who have offended, and deliver us from the impending wrath.
Holy Bride of God, have mercy now upon thy people who are in despair, and by thy motherly intercessions...
avert the indignation of God against us, we entreat thee.
Assent, O inviolate one, to the salvation of thy servants who are near to destruction because of the anger of God, and the heavy and horrible fury of the threats now hanging over us, on account of the multitude of our many sins.
Domina endowed with compassion, who gavest birth to the Savior who is supremely compassionate; look upon the affliction and the groaning of thy people, and hasten to intercede, that He may have mercy upon us.
Thou who didst not suffer corruption in childbearing, deliver us all, O Virgin, from all corruption and from the most heavy earthquake and tribulation, appeasing the indignation of the Lord with thy motherly reconciliations, O thou who art most dear to God.
From the Canon to Saint Demetrios, day 26
Pour forth constant prayers to God, O Maiden, that He may have mercy on me, who am ensnared by the many deceptions of this life and am wrapped in the blind night of sin.
Domina, most pleasing to God, thou who didst bring forth the Sun, dissipate and dispel from every side the dark clouds of2 my soul.
Mother and Virgin, who didst give the Word of God a body, deliver me from bodily passions, and heal all the contritions of my soul.
Thou hast been made beautiful, O Virgin, inasmuch as thou didst give birth to the most beautiful Word; entreat Him with constant prayers, that He may have mercy on the sinful people, and that He may keep safe from every demonic deception the world which hopeth in thee, O Mother of God.
Do not despise the supplication of my miserable soul, O Virgin Mother of God: but by thy kindly intervention make me one who is domestic to God, and save me from the punishments of the future age prepared for me, O most immaculate one.
Having thee, O inviolate Virgin, as a bulwark and a wall, and a harbor, may we be snatched away from harmful temptations and various tribulations by thy prayers, while we praise thee as is thy due.
Perform thy embassy for those who acknowledge thee as Virgin Mother, O blessed one, that they may be liberated from the pressing temptations, from the darts of the serpent, and from everlasting torments, O Virgin.
O Virgin, friend of good things, who didst give birth to God the Word, who is good in every way, make my soul, which is badly affected by the very heavy weight of sins, good through thy prayers, so that it may be able to accomplish those things which lead to life, and to flee those which bring one to the death of malice; and I, with faith, shall call thee blessed.
From the double Canon for the feast of the holy great martyr Anastasia the Roman, and of our holy father Abraham, day 29
We venerate thee as that ladder which reached unto heaven, and on which God rested, making men heavenly, O Maiden.
The Word of the Father of God was incarnate beyond the way of nature from the holy blood of thy flesh, O Virgin Mary: pray to Him that He may mortify the impulses of my flesh.
Burn up the forest of my sins with the fire of thy intercessions, O Mother of God, bringing to me the divine dew of forgiveness.
In thee, O most holy one, the Author of the universe, because of the excess of His compassion, willingly dwelt, and sanctified the substance of men, which had previously slipped into ruin because of the transgression.
After the birth thou didst remain inviolate, O Virgin, just as thou hadst been before the birth; for thou didst bring forth as a new infant Him who is known to have existed before the ages.
Me, who am oppressed by sloth and sunken in sin,
redeem by thy intercession, O Theotokos, Mother ever-virgin.
We praise thee, O all-praiseworthy Lady Theotokos, who in the flesh didst give birth without seed to God, who is to be praised above all.
Mother-virgin maiden, enlightened by the divine Spirit, O all-pure one, the holy prophets, illuminated by the light of the divine Spirit, proclaimed thee with holy voices—thou from whom God the Word was incarnate beyond cause and beyond speech, out of measureless compassion.
Thou who didst give birth to God who is a lover of mankind, O Lady who lovest the good, entreat Him to deliver me from the fire of Gehenna.
Awaken me, burdened by the slumber of negligence, by thy mediation, O Mother of God, and do not permit me to fall asleep in the death of sin, O Virgin; for I hail thee as the protectress and guide of my life.
He who is above God, wearing the whole man without sin, came forth from thy womb, O chaste one, bearing flesh; entreat Him to save those who in faith honor thee.
Thou alone didst bring forth the one of the Trinity, visible in two essences in one hypostasis, O Virgin, to whom we sing sweetly, O all-pure one, without ceasing unto the ages.
Pursuing thee, the chaste and immaculate one, the virgin (Anastasia) kept both body and soul without stain, having reduced the burning passions to ash by patience, and having endured the trial of many torments; and now she dances in the heavenly bridal chambers, rejoicing with thee unto all ages.
Thou wast made the most holy tabernacle of the living stream, from which we who were dead, having drunk, inherit life, crying out: Bless the Lord, all ye works.
As soon as thy martyr (Anastasia) recognized thee, O Lord, as having worn flesh taken from a woman, she—adorned with virginal rays and garlanded with the blood of martyrdom—was brought gloriously to thee, O Christ, as to the King of creation, following thy Mother.
O Virgin who lovest the good, make my soul, which has been corrupted by the evils of sin, good, and make it partaker of eternal goods.
From the Canon for the Holy Martyrs Zenobius and his sister Zenobia, day 30
Hail, O most holy temple; O fleece bedewed with divine dew, O fountain sealed of the immortal stream: guard thy flock, O Lady, so that it may be besieged by no enemies.
Thou didst bring forth the one of the Trinity, having put on human nature, O all-holy Mother-virgin, whom entreat for the salvation of those who praise thee.
By thy strange birth, thou hast made those who had become strangers to God domestic to Him, O all-praiseworthy one, whence we glorify thee with great-minded faith, and cry out: Hail, salvation of all earth-born men.
I am always oppressed by the heavy burden of my sins, O Immaculate one, and I cry out to you: by your mediation, deign to relieve me of them; for you are the glorious patroness of sinners, having given birth to the Redeemer and Savior.
Make my soul beautiful, O Virgin, which is deformed by the foulness of the passions, and fortify my wretched heart with thoughts of true repentance, and save me, O Chaste one, who take refuge in you steadfastly and unshakeably.
You have been shown to be a place of sanctification, O Virgin, from whom God appeared, sanctifying us who sing with faith: Blessed, O most pure one, is the fruit of your womb.
Having conceived the uncultivated cluster, from which the wine of forgiveness has flowed forth, O Virgin Mother, deliver me, I pray, from the drunkenness of the passions.
Illumine, I beseech you, O gate of light, the eyes of my heart, driving far away the deepest darkness of sin from my wretched soul; that I may magnify you, and with affection praise you, who are worthy of all praise.
*From the Double Canon for the feast of the Holy Apostles Stachys, Amplias, Urban, Aristobulus, and Narcissus, and the holy martyr Epimachus, on the 31st day.*
Let us call blessed the most luminous mountain of God, the holy ark, and the table, the entirely golden urn, the pure palace of God, the blessed among women.
I will sing to you, O Lord my God, because without seed you were born from the womb of a Virgin, through whom also you save all men, as you alone are full of mercy.
You have been shown to be a light-bearing bridal chamber of Christ, and a most high throne, Mother of God, O all-blameless one; for He who alone rested in you took away our labors, and prepared the future rest for those who are worthy.
Hail, Mother who knew not man, who contained God the Word in your womb, and gave birth to Him incarnate, as God and man at once.
You appeared more exalted than the angels, O Lady; for you were deemed worthy to contain in your womb in an ineffable manner Him who is terrible to them, and to carry in your hands as an infant Him who precedes all days and times.
Hail, O Deipara who has not known marriage, who were more sublime than the Cherubic orders, and carried God incarnate, borne in your arms.
Beyond the conception of the word, you conceived and brought forth the Word, O you who are to be celebrated with all praises, whom the Father brought forth from His womb before the ages. Whence we, O inviolate one, as His Mother, fittingly call you blessed.
Who shall be able to explain, O Chaste one, the miracle of your birth-giving?
For you gave birth in a manner surpassing reason, even to God Himself, who is by nature God, incarnate beyond the reach of words.
We praise you, through whom we who were formerly condemned have been justified, and bound to the immaterial ministers, and made worthy of paradise, O blessed among women, full of divine grace. Supplicate, O Bride of God, Theotokos, the One who was incarnate of you, our God, on behalf of your servants, for we faithful ones know you as our only protection. Deliver us, O Lady, most worthy of all praise, from temptations, and tribulations, and calamities of every kind, and from the incursion of Barbarians, so that we may glorify you, and Him who was born of you, O Bride of God, the praiseworthy and super-glorious God of our fathers.
In the unconsumed bush and the dew-filled furnace you were prefigured, O Mother-Virgin, having ineffably brought forth God incarnate, O chaste and blessed one. Knowing you as a wall, and a refuge, and a ladder leading the human race to the heights, O all-blameless and chaste one, we cry out: Bless the Lord, all you works of the Lord, praise Him... Save me, O chaste one, you who brought forth the Savior Christ, who became like us, so that we may always call you blessed with praises, O blessed one. You carry Him who carries all things, and you nourish with milk Him who gives food to all; great and terrifying is the mystery of you that transcends all mind, O Ark of the venerable sanctification, Virgin Theotokos, whence we faithfully call you blessed. You have become the dwelling-place of light, O chaste one; therefore I beseech you, enlighten, I pray, the pupils of my wretched heart, heavily darkened by the grievous passions, so that in faith I may call you blessed.
NOVEMBER.
From the Canon for the Holy Unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian, on the 1st day.
You gave flesh, O chaste one, from your pure blood to the Savior and God, who showed us in spirit the venerable Unmercenaries, the holy healers of our passions and our fervent defenders. God chose you as the most beautiful among women, O chaste one, and He who rests in His saints was pleased to be born of you bodily. Make me worthy, O Virgin, of the compassion that is in you, you who brought forth the Word who alone is truly full of supreme compassion—He who showed the holy ones to be healers and wonder-workers in signs, and made them partakers of His compassion toward us. You brought forth the subsistent Wisdom of God, O inviolate Virgin Theotokos, who rendered the holy ones all-wise, through whom the arrogance of the malignant sophist and his hostile craftiness have fallen. He made you a pure temple, O Lady, a most pure...
Word, Who ever magnifies the divine house of the Anargyroi with signs and wonders.
You sprouted as a rod from the root of Jesse, O Mary, having blossomed forth the flower, Christ, Who adorned His servants, the Anargyroi, with miracles as with flowers.
Death is put to death in you; for you have brought forth the Life-subsistent, Christ the Lord, O inviolate one, Who appointed the Anargyroi as physicians who protect our life, crying out: Bless the Lord, all you works of the Lord.
You have become a dwelling-place of Light, O chaste one, which has illuminated all things and shown forth the holy ones as light-bearers, now dispelling the spiritual darkness of death-dealing passions in the Spirit, O inviolate, alone most worthy of all praise.
From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyrs Acepsimas, Aethalas, and Joseph, on the 4th day.
You who gave birth to the incomprehensible God, circumscribed in body, Who became flesh by the excess of His goodness, entreat Him, O Virgin, to rescue your servants from perils.
From you has risen for us the unsetting Sun, O most immaculate one, Who with the light of His rays illuminates the world, which was occupied by darkness and perishing through the guile of the enemy, O most holy Virgin, Bride of God.
You have truly become the sacred ornament of the holy martyrs, O Virgin, and the refuge of the faithful, a wall, and a support, and a perfect redemption; therefore we glorify you with a loud voice.
He who kept you a pure virgin as you were before birth, O most pure one, having dwelt without seed in your womb, came forth as two-fold, God and man, deifying that which He assumed because of His goodness.
The enemy is slain by your life-giving birth, O inviolate Virgin, and Adam, who had long since been slain through disobedience by tasting of the fruit, has been recalled to life; wherefore he praises and blesses you, O most immaculate one.
You have truly become the divine ornament of hierarchs and the crown of glorious athletes, O most immaculate one, the strength of all who ever chant: The praiseworthy and super-glorious God of our fathers.
Jacob once saw you as a ladder, O Virgin, through which the supersubstantial One descended to earth, and led us up to the heights; Him we ceaselessly praise, O Theotokos, and superexalt unto all ages.
The tongue is in no way able to express the fearful mystery of your giving birth; for you embodied the Lord of heaven and of all creatures, He Who begged for flesh from you, O chaste Virgin-Mother; wherefore we glorify you with a concordant voice.
From the double Canon for the feast of Saint Joannicius the Great, and the holy hieromartyrs Nicander the bishop, and Hermaeus the presbyter, on the 4th day.
The recall of those who have fallen, and the stability of those who stand...
is. You are the confirmation of all, O immaculate one; wherefore I supplicate you, Lady, raise up my mind which has collapsed into sin, that I may glorify you. The Incircumscriptible is circumscribed in the flesh within the bosom of the Mother, within the bosom of the Father, He who after this birth preserved her as a true virgin beyond the reach of the mind, to whom we cry out with a loud voice: Let us sing unto our God, for He has been glorified.
With the drops of your mercy, O Virgin most chaste, extinguish the coals of my sins, O all-pure one, and kindle the extinguished lamp of my heart, O golden lampstand, most immaculate one. No heavenly mind can interpret your birth-giving, which is beyond the mind, O maiden; for you conceived in your womb the Word of the primordial Mind, O chaste one, who established all things by the Word.
You, the propitiatory for all mortals, I supplicate and beseech with faith, O blessed one: render your Son, the Judge, propitious to me, that I may glorify you as is due.
He who sits terribly upon an exalted throne, sits in maternal arms having made Himself an infant, raising up the collapsed image, and granting deification to the children of Adam.
Cure the wanderings of my mind, O all-pure one; heal the passions of my soul; expel the darkness of sloth, that I may always celebrate you with praises, O Theotokos worthy of all praise.
O Virgin maiden, immaculate and venerable, who gave birth in the flesh to the Lamb and Lord, O divine ark, O venerable lampstand, illuminate my soul.
O maiden, most heaped with divine grace, who alone are the help of all, aid us who are in danger, and stretching out your hand, lead us to the harbors of salvation, O maiden full of grace.
You have obliterated the disgrace of the first mother, O maiden, by giving birth to Him who crowns us with blessings, and you have changed her sorrow into joy, O most gracious one.
Having given birth alone to the immutable Lord, O maiden full of grace, supplicate Him, O chaste one, that His right hand may change my mind toward better things, as it is sorely tossed about by the occupations of life.
You gave birth to the Word, who became incarnate in a way beyond explanation, O chaste Virgin, redeeming from death those who cry out: Blessed are You, O God of our fathers.
You appeared higher than the angels, having ineffably given bodily form to God; therefore, O Lady pure from all stain, supplicate Him to render me superior to carnal passions, celebrating your greatest grace with hymns in high humility of mind.
Dry up the sea of my evils, O Virgin, you who gave birth to the ocean of mercy, the Redeemer and Lord, to whom we cry out, O Virgin: All you works, bless, praise the Lord.
Illuminate, O chaste one, the eyes of my mind, you who gave birth to the Light; let not the deepest darkness of sin overtake me, nor let the abyss cover me with despair,
but you, 213 save me, and act as the pilot to the port of the divine will for me.
Irradiate me with your light, O you who are cleansed of every stain, who brought forth the inaccessible Light; disperse the clouds of my soul, and rescue me from the darkness, I implore you, and make me worthy of divine salvation, that I may praise you, who are worthy of all praise.
From the Canon to the Holy Martyrs Galation and Episteme (92*), day 5.
Guardian of the troubled, salvation and hope of the despairing, Mother of God to be celebrated with all praise, pray for us with earnest entreaties, that we may be delivered from dangers.
Dissolve the cloud that surrounds my heart, O most chaste one; strike into me a ray of true repentance, O blessed gate of light, adorned with every kind of purity, and grant that, as in the day, I may walk honestly in the commandments of God.
Bring to life me who am destroyed and deadened by harmful affections, O maiden, who gave birth to that Life by whom all the force and power of death has been dissolved.
The tongue of earth-born men is in no way sufficient to praise you, who have become the Mother of God, O Mistress, and most immaculate Virgin, and refuge of Christians.
214
From the Canon to the Holy Martyrs Taurion and Thessalonica, day 7.
The height of your trembling mystery, and the incomprehensible depth of it, who could avail, O Virgin, to explain in words? For you brought forth God made man without any cause or reason.
I always take refuge in you, O Mistress, surrounded every day by a multitude of temptations. Have mercy on me and save me, O you alone worthy of all praise, who gave birth to the Savior and Lord of all.
Caught in the storm of sins, and placed in danger, steer me, O Mother of God, as a pilot, and direct me to the tranquil port of compunction.
I am oppressed on every side by the most heavy burden of sins; and I cry to you, O most chaste one, that you may deign to lift this from me, and impose upon me the light yoke of the Son, which I may bear without obstacle, by your divine intercession, O you alone most pure from every stain.
The Word, the beautiful bridegroom, as if from the bridal chamber of the Father, proceeded from your womb, and when He had rendered human nature beautiful, He illuminated it with divine knowledge, and took away the deformity of malice, O Virgin, Bride of God.
Have mercy on my soul, wounded by the most evil arrows of sin: illuminate my mind, heavily darkened by transgressions, Mistress Mother of God, who gave birth to Christ, the giver of light.
Restore to life my soul, destroyed by passions and very many sins, O inviolate Virgin, who brought forth the Life, who by His death and passion dissolved all the forces of death; and grant me, that with a grateful heart I may sing: O people, superexalt Him, etc.
215 Illuminate, O gate of light, my soul, which the enemy has darkened with the shadows of sins: and from all the perturbations of this life, and from perpetual darkness, and from the fire and the worm, deliver me, that I may glorify you, O Mother of God, the restoration of men.
From the Canon to the Holy Archangel Michael, day 8.
Virgin crowned with all praise, beauty of angels, help of men, bring aid to me tossed by the waves, and always agitated by the storm of sin and almost submerged, and standing in the greatest danger.
He who by His own will created immaterial minds, voluntarily dwelt in your material womb, O most immaculate one, and appeared in the flesh as a visible man, who was invisible.
The wondrous mystery of your birth was taught long ago by the holy Prophet, seeing you in the Spirit as the shady mountain, from which God, most holy, came forth incarnate most openly.
God showed you to be higher than the intellectual angels, entering into your womb; whom implore, O totally pure and inviolate one, always for the salvation of our souls.
Blessed is the people who always bless you, O blessed one, who gave birth to the blessed God, who by an ineffable union mercifully deified men.
When the eternal Word of the great Mind in you, O maiden, in a truly ineffable and stupendous manner dwelt—
when the archangel Gabriel saw this, he exclaimed: “Hail, O blessed one, throne of the Most High.” The divine, attendant archangel cried out to you: “Hail, O unwedded bride of God, glory of the angels, and salvation and bulwark of men.”
At the voice of the angel Gabriel you conceived the Word of God, O most pure One, who by a word created the hosts above us, and who grants the word by which we can praise His holy condescension, which is beyond every word and thought.
From the Double Canon for the Feast of the Holy Martyrs Onesiphorus and Porphyrius, and the Holy Matrons Matrona and Theoctiste, on the 9th day.
You have put an end to the tyranny of death, having brought forth Life and immortality to the world, Christ our Redeemer, O Virgin who have not known wedlock.
You who brought forth divine salvation and restoration to the world, save by your intercessions those who faithfully flee to you, O Immaculate one.
Incline your ear, O all-holy one, to save me; for you embodied the God-Word who moves all things by His divine nod, in a way surpassing word and mind.
The Creator is united in your womb to flesh, O all-holy one, remaining what He was, that He might bestow happiness upon men.
You gave birth to the God-Word made flesh, O girl and most immaculate Lady, who was pleased to be made like unto all through the bowels of His mercy.
Without leaving the heavens, O immaculate one, God is emptied in your womb, and the Immeasurable is measured, dissolving my immeasurable transgressions.
The Incomprehensible dwelt in you, receiving containment, and He showed you to be broader than the heavens, O Virgin; therefore we call you blessed.
Having given birth to the Lord of the dead and the living, O all-immaculate one, put to death the passions of my flesh.
Contrary to the laws of nature, O Virgin, you give birth to the Lawgiver, who refashions our broken nature; entreat Him to grant salvation to me who am broken by sins.
The nature of men had been enslaved to sin, but you, O Theotokos, redeemed it from that cruel slavery by giving birth to the Lord of all, who showed us all the entrances to life, O all-immaculate one.
You give birth to the Word become flesh from your blood, O Virgin, who was pleased to deify men who sing: “Blessed art Thou, the God of our fathers.”
Loosing the curse of Eve, O most immaculate one, you gave birth, O Virgin, to the God of all, having conceived Him in an ineffable manner, and having brought Him forth beyond understanding for the salvation of men.
When the Word of God found you, O maiden, as a chosen rose in the valleys of life, He was captivated by the love of your beauty, and being incarnate, He filled the world with His fragrance.
“Behold the Virgin,” as Isaiah says in the Spirit, “had in her womb” Him who redeemed us from the womb of Hades, for whom we piously cry aloud: “Praise the Lord and exalt Him above all.”
Bearing me entirely from your divine blood,
O most immaculate one, the Lord has come forth like a bridegroom; and He who nourishes all creation by His will is nourished by your milk, O blessed ever-virgin. O maiden, who carried in your hands Him who bears all things with a nod, deliver me from the hand of the alien by your intercession, and illumine my mind with your light, and make me a stranger to the passions that impudently assail me.
From the Canon for the feast of the holy apostles Olympas, Rhodion, Sosipater, etc., day 10
You reformed the human race by your childbirth, O Virgin: for you gave birth to the Word of the Father, who wore mortal flesh and showed us the paths of immortality. The only-begotten Son of the Father, who formerly was without mother, now that we acknowledge Him born of you without a father, we confess you to be the Mother of God, who gave birth without pain and remained a virgin in an ineffable manner, O Maria, bride of God. That new miracle which was clearly manifested in you, O most pure one, surpassed all miracles: for you gave birth corporally to God, who for pity was united to mortals in an unmixed union, O bride of God. You conceived the Word through a word, O most immaculate Mother of God, and you gave birth to Him who became man beyond all words; wherefore we bless you evermore with divinely inspired words. As another heaven, more sublime than the former, we glorify you, O Lady, who brought forth the Sun of justice for us and dispelled the deep darkness of ignorance. The coeternal Word of the Father, having appeared to mortals, you placed in flesh; and in the flesh, O maiden, you gave birth to Him becoming man, to save mankind. Praiseworthy is the God of our fathers and super-glorious. The urn which once carried manna, O chaste one, prefigured you: for you carried Christ, our sweetness, O venerable one, and in the flesh you gave birth to Him who delivers those who exalt Him unto the ages from every bitterness of most foul sins. Spare your people, O Lord, delivering us from the incursion of barbarians, and from sins, and temptations, and eternal punishment, by the prayers of the Virgin Mother of God who gave birth to You, and of Your glorious apostles.
From the Canon for the Holy Orestes, Menas, Victor, Vincent, Stephanides, and Theodore the Studite, day 10
O most praiseworthy one, who alone, above the order of nature, gave birth to the Creator and Maker of the universe, who in you renewed natures, redeem me from sins and snatch me from torments. Heal my mind, corrupted by depraved affections, O inviolate one, and bedew my soul with the joyful light of divine grace. Agitated by a whirlwind of malice and tossed on the stormy sea of passions, save your servant who flees to you, O inviolate one. From the violent waves of sin, from the ignominy of the passions, and from every evil that surrounds us, make your servants safe, O chaste one. Mortify the prudence of my flesh, O inviolate Virgin, you who conceived Christ, who by divine power vivified the dead nature of men.
The Word of God, the laws of nature having been renovated, though He was without beginning, was incarnate from your pure blood, O Virgin, beyond the grasp of reason, and having become an infant, He restored corrupted man. The Lord most high, though He was true God, took human form from you, O most chaste Virgin, and deified man, and delivered him from corruption, to whom we all sing, O spouse of God, Mary.
The orders of angels shudder, O immaculate one, considering the mystery of your childbearing, which is above nature: for you have brought forth God, and as a son you have suckled Him who nourishes the universe.
From the Canon for the feast of St. John the Almsgiver, day 12.
That He might join the things below with the things above, God alone of all entered a womb untouched by marriage, and appearing in the likeness of flesh, having destroyed the middle wall of enmity, He mediated peace, and bestowed life and divine redemption.
In you, O most holy one, the author of the universe, because of the excess of His mercy, voluntarily dwelt and sanctified the substance of men, which had fallen because of the first transgression.
Heal the wounds of my heart, O maiden Virgin, and direct the movements of my soul toward the fulfillment of God’s will along a happy path.
My soul, darkened by the pleasures of life, O chaste and all-blameless one, illuminate with your light, for you have brought forth Christ, the Light who dissolves the darkness of ignorance.
The God-speaking prophets, having reached the depth of your mystery, O Virgin, prophetically proclaimed it, enlightened by the light of the divine Spirit. And now we, seeing the outcomes of their prophecy manifest, believe.
You alone, O Virgin, brought forth the one of the Trinity recognized in two substances and one hypostasis, to whom we sing: Blessed are You, Lord God, etc.
You have appeared as the tabernacle of the living river, O most holy one, from which we who were dead, having drunk, inherit life, shouting: Bless, all you works, the Lord, and exalt Him throughout all ages.
Having appeared as more spacious than the heavens, O Virgin, broaden my narrowed mind, showing it to be capable of divine gifts.
From the Canon for St. Philip the Apostle, day 14.
O most holy and most pleasing to God, be for me an assistant and patroness before Christ, that He may deliver me from eternal judgment and from every kind of harm from the serpent.
Heal the wanderings of my mind, the passions of my body, and the diseases of my soul, O Virgin, and direct me to good paths, that by doing the will of God, I may find eternal life.
As the living palace of the Lord, and the asylum of the faithful, and the aid of those who are in tribulations, and an infallible guide full of grace, we praise you.
You, who brought forth the supreme Lord, entreat Him, O most benign Mother of God, to snatch your people from every evil.
The prophet saw you as a spiritual candelabra, O inviolate one, truly having a lamp, the illumination and propitiation of our souls.
With tongue and heart I proclaim you the Mother of God, O most inviolate one; for you brought forth the immortal God, to whom we all singing in harmony say: Blessed art You, God, etc.
Him who is before the ages, a new infant on earth you brought forth, O Virgin, renewing us, who formerly...
through malice were gravely inveterate; therefore, break the audacity and pride of all our enemies, that we may acknowledge you with faith, O Mother of God, as blessed, we praise you, O chaste one, forever.
Guard your servants, O most holy Virgin, inviolate from the wounding of all the enemy’s darts; and B
From the Canon for the Feast of the Holy Martyrs Samonas, Gurias, and Abibos, on the 15th day.
You have become a tabernacle of that Wisdom which exceeds all wisdom, O most immaculate one; for the Lord of all was well pleased, O venerable one, to build for Himself a house from your most pure blood, for the salvation of our souls.
He who entered your womb, O most chaste Mother of God, has shown you to be a fountain of healings; therefore, heal my soul.
Beyond the grasp of the mind you gave birth, O Virgin, and after birth you were seen to be a virgin still; great is the mystery of your childbearing, O ever-virgin, undefiled one, whom we praise.
He who is alone good, and by the sea of His goodness holds and sustains all things, O Mother of God, deigned to be held in your arms.
Having found you alone like a most pure lily in the midst of thorns (95), and the flower of the valley, O Mother of God, the spiritual Bridegroom made His dwelling in you.
As a most highly polished mirror (94) sending forth a light of brightness, you received the radiance of the divine, O Virgin, flashing upon you; blessed are you among women, most immaculate Lady.
(95) The Blessed Virgin was like a most pure lily, because she was conceived without any stain of origin, whereas the rest of the sons of Adam were, on account of original sin, not lilies but thorns. Federicus Nausea, Bishop of Vienna, supports this in his Homily 81, while explaining those words from Canticles chap. 2: *As a lily among thorns, so is my friend among the daughters*, he says: "Although by the law of nature all daughters of men are thorny—that is, conceived in sin—yet the most holy Virgin Mary remained immaculate through the law of grace, not otherwise than a lily among thorns, which, however horrid, rough, rigid, and swollen they may be, the lily itself grows beneath them most beautifully without a stain, losing nothing of its virtue." And St. Anselm, in *De conceptu virginali* cap. 4, says: "A lily can be born among thorns and not be stung by them; so the Mother of Christ could be conceived among sinners and not be touched by sin." Hence, Adam of St. Victor in his Rhythms greets the holy Virgin with these words:
Hail, sacred Parent of the Word,
Flower from thorn, of thorns devoid,
Flower, the thicket’s glory.
We are a thicket, we by the thorn
Of sin are stained,
But you are ignorant of the thorn.
He called the Virgin a flower from a thorn because she was descended from ancestors conceived in sin, but he does not say she was a flower made out of a thorn, because the Virgin was always a flower or lily, whence he also says she is "ignorant of the thorn," as if the Virgin knew nothing else of herself, nor could know, except that she was always a lily, never a thorn. See Bustus in his *Mariale*, sermon 5 on the Conception, part 2, where, proving the Blessed Virgin is signified in the lily of Canticles, *As a lily among thorns, so is my friend among the daughters*, he says among other things: "Although a lily may be born among thorns, yet it exists without thorns and is entirely white and fragrant; so too the Blessed Virgin Mary, although she was propagated from our first parents through thorny sin, yet she was without stain, and through cleanliness and purity remained entirely white and fragrant." So he.
Furthermore, St. Sabas in the Greek Menaea, January 29, ode 6—which St. Joseph also asserts here—testifies that the Blessed Virgin alone was found by Christ the Bridegroom as the purest lily in the midst of thorns, in these words:
From you alone, found as a most pure lily in the midst of thorns,
Inhabiting your womb, that Bridegroom of yours proceeded.
So he. Indeed (as Fr. Simon Wagnerek says in the *Mariana Pietas Græcorum*), in the mind of St. Sabas, Christ found Mary among men conceived in sin, not as one similar to them—that is, as a thorn among thorns, for thus He would have had to first make a lily out of a thorn, when in truth He had not found Mary a lily, but a thorn. But what craftsmen do, this is said to be finding, not imagining. Thus St. Sabas and St. Joseph assert that Christ, in the midst of thorns—that is, all men who are conceived in sin—found Mary not a thorn, but a lily, because He chose her to exist from the beginning as a lily, not a thorn, nor a lily from a thorn—that is, without any stain of origin.
(94) If it was fitting that the slightest stain of venial sin be kept far away from the Marian mirror, so that it could truly be called most polished and most lucid, it was certainly far more worthy and decent that the blemish of original fault be kept away from it as far as possible. For venial sin is indeed a stain, but a most slight one, inasmuch as it does not destroy the beauty of the soul,
but diminishes it, though it does not destroy it; by which the fervor of charity is indeed cooled, but not extinguished; which diminishes the health of the soul, but does not secure death; which perhaps also causes the fervent love of God towards us to cool, but by no means provokes or incites hatred. On the contrary, the stain of original sin corrupts the beauty of the soul, excludes charity, brings death, and draws upon man the hatred of God the Most High and Almighty. Legal uncleanness—that, namely, which women were wont to contract on account of the filth with which they were imbued from childbirth—God wished to be absent from the most shining mirror of His Mother, as Cyprian teaches in his *Sermon on the Nativity*, Augustine in *On Heresies*, Epiphanius in *Compendium of Doctrine*, Nazianzen in his *Oration*, and others.
If, therefore, God thought that the cleanness and candor of this mirror could be not a little harmed or violated by the shadowy stain of legal uncleanness, and on that account prohibited that uncleanness from it, in what way did He permit the most terrible filth and squalor of original sin to be sprinkled upon it and to adhere to it? See what I have said concerning this mirror in my *Vindication of the Holy Dominican Order*, book 1, part 1, argument 8, upon those words of St. Thomas: *The Supreme Architect made one mirror*, etc.
From the Canon to the holy Gregory the Decapolite, day 20.
The celestial ladder reaching from earth to heaven, through which the Word of God conversed with mortals, O blessed and all-pure one, inexplicable wonder, incomprehensible vision, save those who take refuge in you. Rejoice, you who alone brought forth the Lord of all; rejoice, you who procured life for men; rejoice, shady and unhewn mountain, the bulwark of the faithful; rejoice, all-blameless one. Mother of God, blessed and all-blameless, heal the wounds of my soul, extinguish the pleasures of the flesh, enlighten my darkened heart, grant peace to my mind, and deliver me from every harm and the assault of enemies. Preservation of the world, Mother and ever-virgin, guide me and lead me on a straight path, and direct my mind toward righteousness, strengthening my right paths and guiding the courses of my soul. Mary, pure palace of the King, cleanse me, who have become an unclean cave of robbers, by your prayers, and show me to be a holy temple of the One born of you. O all-pure Virgin, who brought forth Life, bring to life and save me, who have been called dead through sin and am perishing, and snatch me from Gehenna as I sing: Blessed is God, the God of our fathers. You who ineffably brought forth the Judge and Lord, entreat Him, O all-holy one, as your Son, at the hour of judgment, to deliver those who with faith and piety sing to Him—namely, the peoples—from condemnation, fire, lightless darkness, and the gnashing of teeth; He who is superexalted unto the ages... With the voice of Gabriel, we the faithful joyfully salute you: Rejoice, paradise, who have caused the tree of life to spring forth; rejoice, the undoing of the curse, of the martyrs...
dissolution, the crown of confessors, and the firmament of pious men.
From the Canon for the Feast of the Holy Apostle Philemon and his companions, day 22.
The divine catalog of prophets long ago in many forms, O Immaculate One, truly and from afar proclaimed you as the only one destined to give birth to the Lord. Having appeared pure and altogether spotless, you received in your womb God the Word, who purified our nature, defiled, O Virgin, by transgressions.
