I truly praise you, most praiseworthy one, who gave birth in a way beyond nature to God the Word, who is beyond all praise; and I entreat you, as you are good, O Bride of God, to heal the diseases of my humble soul.
O Lady, save us, tossed by the grievous tempest of temptations, and afflicted by the incursions of most savage Barbarians and the cruel attacks of demons. The Word is embodied in your womb, and out of compassion He is known as man, so that He might make man God, O maiden entirely without blemish (96). You have become the strength of the humble, a shining lamp, a divine table, a mountain and an unpassable gate, the throne of God and a palace, the rod of Aaron and a golden-shining urn, O Virgin, bearing Christ, the manna of life.
Your womb has truly appeared to us as a new paradise, O chaste Mother of God, in which the tree of life has sprouted, through which those who were dead from tasting the fruit of the tree are again brought back to life and led into paradise, O Theotokos. You bear Him who sustains all things, and you nourish Him who nourishes all, in no way knowing the manner of childbirth, O most pure one; your miracle surpasses every mind, striking with wonder both angels and mortals who see you alone as the Virgin Mother of God.
From the Canon for the Feast of our Holy Father Gregory of Agrigento, day 23.
I confess you truly and properly as the Mother of God; for you gave birth to the Lord in an unsearchable manner, O inviolate Theotokos, who is understood in two substances and wills.
The words of the divinely speaking heralds have been fulfilled: for behold, while He kept the virginal house of His delights from every fault. Nor could the cunning serpent find an entrance into this paradise; for it was a closed garden, nay, the Virgin herself crushed the head of the serpent. Thus he. And Father J. Eusebius Nieremberg, in his Exceptions, ch. 13, when he had related from Saint Athanasius, in a homily on the Encounter of the Lord, that the Blessed Virgin had been called a paradise planted by the divine hand, adds: "The Blessed Virgin is called a paradise planted by the hand of the Lord, because in the planting of her creation, only the hand of God and His grace had a place, and not the footprint of the devil and his servitude."
For what would it be to affirm that the Mother of God was immune from every stain, if not to drive away from her every stain of sin at all, whether actual or original? Saint Sabbas agrees in the Greek Menæa, day [3] of January, Ode 3, when, addressing the Mother of God, he says: "No one, as you, O Lady, is equally blameless, nor is there any beside you undefiled, O subject to no stain." And in the same place, day [1] of January, Ode 9: "You, who are intact from every stain." See Velasquez, De Maria immaculata concepta, book IV, dissert. 5, annot. 1.
The Virgin brought forth a new infant, older than Adam, and sitting upon a throne with the Begetter.
The race of mortals has been saved by your childbearing, which surpasses understanding; and those who were in the darkness of corruption, O all-holy Lady, have seen the light that shone from your womb, the cause of our restoration, O Maiden.
He who did not empty the bosom of the Father in becoming incarnate, O all-undefiled one, is seen in your bosom, held as an infant; Him, O Virgin Bride of God, render propitious to those who honor you piously.
The mind is at a loss to contemplate the great mystery of your childbirth; for you gave birth to God become man, O Ever-Virgin, Him who is incomprehensible.
In a manner befitting a mother, you gave birth to the Creator of all, and held Him in your arms, as a cherubic throne, Him who holds the universe, O you who have not known man.
Your wondrous childbirth strikes our minds with astonishment, O alone blessed one. For God took flesh from you, remaining what He was, O Theotokos, immutable in nature, whom we extol unto all ages.
O Maiden who gave birth to the timeless Light, which shone forth from the Father, enlighten my soul and my mind, O Virgin, driving far from me the darkness of the passions, that I may call you blessed, the ever-blessed hope of the faithful.
From the Canon for Saint Clement of Rome, day 24.
Sanctify, O Lady, my humble mind, you who gave birth to the supersubstantial Word, and are holier than all the supernal powers, O you who are graced by God.
Mother of the Lord, who ineffably gave birth to God, the Savior of all, entreat Him to save me, who am ever overwhelmed by passions.
You have restored the human nature which had been crushed and was subject to corruption, O undefiled one, by giving bodily form to God, and giving birth beyond nature, O you who have not known man; to whom we cry: Glory, Christ, to your power.
Let us honor the chaste one with a chaste mind; let us, decorating the beauty of Jacob with divine actions, piously sing her praises as the Mother of our God.
Isaiah was initiated into the depths of your childbirth, and proclaimed that you, a virgin, would have in your womb Him who, for the sake of mercy, became incarnate from you, O you who have not known man.
He who provides existence to all by His will, O all-chaste one, receives a temporal beginning from you and is born, dissolving the temporal failings of the human nature that had fallen and was subject to flux, O undefiled one.
O fearful and ineffable spectacle! In the womb dwells He whom nothing can contain, and He becomes flesh without change, and deifies me through mercy; and He preserves His Mother undefiled after childbirth.
You bear in your arms God, O most holy one, as a fiery throne, inviolate, who assumed human nature and was united to it in an ineffable union through boundless compassion; therefore we all magnify you.
From the Canon for the feast of St. Mercurius, the martyr, on the 25th
He was seen incarnate from a virgin maiden, He who for our sake became man similar to us, and He shows Mercurius, who became his athlete, as a faithful witness of His own passions, singing to Him with zeal: Let us sing to the Lord, for He has been gloriously glorified.
That the bush might prefigure your conception, which surpasses every mind, O chaste one, it appeared burning in the fire, and yet it was not consumed.
Upon you the life-bearing Word has descended, O Ever-Virgin, like rain, and dried up the downpours of polytheism.
Mortify, O Virgin, my living sin, you who brought forth Life, who delivered death to death.
You conceived, O maiden, through the voice of the angel, the Angel of the great counsel, and you brought forth, O purest one, incarnate from your most holy blood, Him who showed the entrances of life to all because of His ineffable mercy.
The orders of angels are struck with awe at the depth of your mystery, O Theotokos; for God was seen incarnate from you, to whom we sing in concert: Blessed are You, O Lord God. We all, the faithful, praise you, O inviolate one, as the cause of our restoration; for you brought forth God, the Cause of all things, above cause, who restored His own image, which had been crushed by malice, by His own mercy, O you alone super-blessed and full of grace.
Illumine, O gate of light, my soul, blinded by the darkness of the passions and obscured by evil thoughts, and placed in danger; and deliver me from temptations, perils, and tribulations, that I may glorify you, the hope and strength of the faithful.
From the Canon for the feast of our holy Father Alypius the Stylite, on the 26th
The words of the venerable prophet have reached their end; for behold, the Virgin has brought forth God in the flesh, who restores men previously crushed by transgressions and sins. O Virgin, pure palace of the Word, make my soul a house of the Holy Spirit; give me to drink from the fountain of the living water, which is the beginning of life, I who am inflamed by the heat of sin, that I may worthily glorify you.
Heal, O Lady, the passions of my soul, and illumine my mind and my heart, you who brought forth the Giver of light, Christ, the Lord, superior in all goodness.
O holy maiden, you brought forth the holy God, made man through His mercy, who sanctifies all who with faith and fear sanctify Him.
We, who are caught in tribulation, have a strong consolation, O chaste one,
and a firm defense, I say; deliver, O Mother of God, thy servants from dangers.
He who is uncircumscribed took upon Himself flesh, endowed with mind and soul, from thee, O Ever-Virgin, to save those who cry out: Blessed art Thou, O God, etc.
Thy birth-giving has now rendered sterile the harm that was born from the malice of the serpent, O Virgin, the unique extermination of the curse; wherefore we honor thee unto all ages.
Bestow illumination upon me, who dwell in the darkness of the passions, and deliver me from wicked works and from the flame that is reserved for me, wretched and sinful as I am, O inviolate Lady, the protection of those who praise thee.
From the Canon for the feast of St. Stephen the Younger, the 28th day.
The impassable gate, the pure temple of chastity, the most beautiful among women, the holy Lady, let the holy people glorify with sacred voices.
From thee alone, the pure one, the super-divine Word was incarnate, in the way which He alone knows, and He saved us, who adore His divine descent made for the sake of His mercy.
In thee, O most immaculate one, I have placed the hopes of my salvation; I have taken refuge under thy protection; be my helper, O damsel, and snatch me away from grievous things.
O supersanct one, who alone on earth didst truly give birth to the supersanct God, sanctify and save by thy mediation those who ever proclaim thee to be the Theotokos.
Her alone, worthy of all praise, the most beautiful among women, the Mother of God, the inexpugnable wall of Christians, the inviolate Lady, let us bless with an unmoved and undoubting heart.
Most sacred prophets most clearly declared beforehand the mystery of thy venerable parturition, O chaste one; and now we, clearly recognizing the fulfillment of the prophecy, devoutly call thee blessed.
By the sprinkling of the divine laver, which was poured forth from the side of thy Son and God, wash away, I beseech thee, O Virgin, the filth of wicked sin that clings to me.
O beloved of God, receptacle of light, the true strength of the holy martyrs and the pride of all the confessors, save us from dangers and surrounding calamities and from the incursions of enemies, while we celebrate thee with praises.
From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyrs Paramon and Philumenus, the 29th day.
In time thou didst bring forth Him who is outside of time, having become man; Him do thou earnestly entreat, O chaste and wholly immaculate one, as thy Son and Lord, that He may heal the temporal passions of my soul.
Establish and make stable my mind, which is turned about by many
passions, O Mother of God, most chaste, that I may glorify thee as is due.
Thou didst resuscitate all men, who were dead through transgression, by thy life-giving birth, O Virgin Mary: wherefore we glorify thee, and with divine praises call thee blessed.
The Lord, who hath honor equal to the Father and the Spirit, was incarnate of thy chaste blood, O Virgin, becoming man.
Deliver me from the scandals of life, O most immaculate one, for I am always occupied by the malice of the enemy, and held fast by the darkness of shameful thoughts in the night of blindness.
Rejoice, thou who alone didst bring forth joy to men; rejoice, O heaven, and Cherubic throne, and most glorious palace of the King of the ages, O Lady free from every stain.
The shadows of the Law and the venerable proclamations of the prophets prefigured thee, who wouldst ineffably be the Genitrix of our God, O chaste one, most filled with divine grace, to whom we all sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord.
Illuminate the pupils of my eye, darkened by the blindness of soul-destroying sin, O Genitrix of God, most chaste Lady; for thou art the help and illumination of the faithful, O inviolate one.
MENSIS DECEMBER
Thou didst bring forth Life, and dost direct the paths of my most unhappy soul into the way of peace, leading me to perform the divine will of God.
From the canon for the holy prophet Zephaniah, on the 3rd.
Through thee did the human race receive a share in redemption; for thou alone didst bring forth the Redeemer of all; therefore we call thee blessed, O Virgin, Mother of God, help of sinners, and raising up of those who have fallen.
The paths of the Desired One of all are seen in thee. For He who sits in the bosom of the Father, resides in thy bosom, O chaste one, in the manner of an infant, and voluntarily sucks milk, He who nourishes all things.
Thou didst bring forth to us, like a young child, the One older than all ages, O unique and most beautiful maiden, bringer forth ineffably of the Creator, O most holy Virgin, miracle of the angels and salvation of faithful men.
Heal the long-standing passions of my soul, O inviolate one, I beseech thee: and rend asunder the handwriting of all my sins with the spear of thy Son, and do not suffer me to perish, who hope in thee, O most pure one.
Mortify the appetites of my flesh, O Mother of God, who art the friend of good things, O Virgin, who didst bring forth the good Word and Lord; make my soul, which continually inclines to evil because of the serpent's assaults and stings, good, hastening to do what is good, O good one, as the unique refuge of the weary, and salvation of those who praise thee.
Behold now the prophecy of the divine herald is fulfilled: for the Virgin hath brought forth Him who produced the ages; to whom we sing unceasingly, saying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.
Thee, the Mother of the Lord of all, all generations of generations always call blessed, O most pure one, and glorify in sacred ways: for thou art become the asylum of all the faithful, who with faith sing: Priests, bless; O ye people, exalt Him above all forever.
From the canon for the feast of St. Ambrose, bishop of Milan, on the 7th.
Without seed, by the decree of the Father, of the divine Spirit thou didst conceive, and in the flesh didst bring forth the Son of God, who is from the Father without a mother, and for our sake is from thee without a father.
Thou didst renew the race of men, having alone brought forth the Creator and Lord of our nature; wherefore we glorify thee, O most gracious to God.
He who fashioned all things by His will, acts...
with wisdom; wishing to refashion mankind, O Virgin, He inhabited thy womb. Heal thou the wounds of my soul, O Virgin, by thy divine visitation, and illumine my mind, darkened by the negligence and malice of the warring enemy. Behold, O Virgin, in thy womb thou didst conceive the Word, co-eternal with the Father, and didst bring Him forth in the flesh, bestowing restoration upon all who have fallen in Adam, O all-immaculate one. Thou wast seen to be higher than the heavens, having brought forth the heavenly God, O all-pure one, who united earthly things with heavenly things, and granted the knowledge of Himself to all who cry out: All ye works, praise the Lord. With the voice of the archangel we cry to thee with joy, O Virgin: Hail, the undoing of the curse; hail, the redemption of all evils, thou who didst deify mortals by thy ineffable birth-giving.
From the canon for the holy martyrs Mennas, Hermogenes, and Eugraphus, day 10.
That thy servants may be liberated from the tyranny of the passions, O most pure Maiden, earnestly entreat thy Lord and Master, whom thou didst clothe in a body from thy chaste blood, O all-chaste one, and who conversed with us. Finding thee alone among women fair in beauty, O Maiden, Christ proceeded from thy womb, having become incarnate, adorning our race with divine beauties; wherefore we reverence thee. A rod from the root of Jesse, thou didst blossom forth the Sower of all creation, who withered the plants of fruitless knowledge, but planted in us the most true faith with devotion, O inviolate Virgin, all-laudable. Thou didst appear more exalted than the holy angels, O chaste Virgin, having brought forth the Angel of Great Counsel, God Emmanuel, who, by His descent and humiliation, made men heavenly, O Maiden, because of His ineffable mercy. Death continued even up to thee, O Virgin; for thou didst bring forth Christ, the Life, who bestowed immortal and divine redemption upon those who purely believe in Him; entreat Him, O all-holy one, that thy servants might be delivered from their transgressions. Without burning thy womb, without shaking the seals of virginity, the Word incarnate proceeded from thee, granting us incorruption and life, as we sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers. We have known thee, O Maiden, as the urn containing the manna of Divinity, the ark, and the table, and the lampstand, and the throne of God, and the palace, and the bridge leading those who sing to divine life: Let the whole creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all forever.
Our nature, which had been cast down, O most pure one, beheld the flash of the lightning of your birth, and has been redeemed from the night of ignorance and the dark confusion of the passions; therefore, we revere you as the cause of our salvation.
From the canon for the feast of Saint Daniel the Stylite, confessor, on the 11th day
He appeared as complete man, remaining what He was even after the incarnation, the immutable Lord who was born of you, O Theotokos. Deliver me, O Lady, from the violence of the passions, and now rout the enemies that assail me; establish me firmly on the rock of God’s will; enlighten my soul, O gate of divine light. The laws of nature were made new in you; for you gave birth, O most chaste one, to the Lawgiver—the Word—truly beyond cause and reason, who has liberated the race of men from irrationality, those who faithfully sing in unison: Glory to your power, O lover of mankind.
Having given birth to the Lord, you were shown to be higher than the powers above, and you have deified the nature of mortals, you alone most worthy of all praise. Whence we, the faithful, with heart and tongue glorify you truly as the Theotokos, O Virgin. We, the faithful, all possess you as our protection and rampart, we who are always in peril in the depth of evils and the swell of tribulations, O Theotokos, the only refuge of mortals. Be gracious to me, O Virgin, and heal me, wounded by the sword of sin, with the poultice of your intercession, while I cry: Blessed is the fruit of your womb.
Those who believe you to be the Theotokos, O most holy Lady worthy of all praise, adhering to your words, now call you blessed, since you gave birth to the blessed God for us, whom we praise in two natures and one person, crying out: O children, bless; priests, praise; people, exalt Him above all forever. Spare me, O Savior, who were born and preserved your Mother incorrupt after the birth, when You sit to judge my works; overlook my iniquities and my sins, as the sinless one, as the compassionate God and lover of mankind.
From the canon for the Sunday of the Commemoration of the Holy Forefathers, Adam and Eve
Let us lend an ear to the divine oracles, which proclaim the manifestation of Christ; for behold, He is born in a cave, from an unwed maiden, whose birth, full of dread, the star appearing to the astrologers foretells. Now the expectation of the nations comes forth from the Virgin, and Bethlehem opportunely opens up Eden, which was closed, receiving the Word made flesh and laid in a manger according to the flesh. Now our redemption is laid in a manger, and He is swaddled as an infant; and Magi, kings from the East, have arrived to see Him as God and King born upon the earth, and to worship Him with gifts faithfully.
He who is full is emptied in the flesh for our sake, and He who is without beginning receives a beginning; the Rich One becomes a beggar, and the Word of God, existing as God, is reclined in a manger for irrational beasts, as an infant, working the restoration of all things from the ages. A new child is recognized upon the earth, He who is always with the Father and the Spirit; and He who swaddled the earth with mist is clearly swaddled in bands, and is reclined in a manger of irrational beasts. Let us now, rejoicing, celebrate the pre-feast of His seedless birth. Behold, as the prophet foretold, the unwedded one has conceived God in her womb, and she hastens to bring Him forth clearly in the cave of Bethlehem, to whom we all sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.
Thou hast appeared from virginal blood, O Christ, becoming incarnate by an ineffable word; and as a perfect infant, through an excess of compassion, Jesus, Thou art born in a cave. A star from afar manifested Thee to the astrologers; praise, they cry out with faith, and superexalt Christ unto the ages. Wearing me [as a garment], He proceeds from the Virgin, and the Word of the Father is born in a cave without commingling; dance, O creation, with grateful voices magnifying His all-holy condescension for the sake of mercy.
From the canon for the holy martyr Eleutherius, day 15.
As a fire-formed throne, thou bearest the Creator; as a living bridal chamber and delightful palace, thou containest the King who became like unto us, O God-graced one. The rod of power hath sprouted Christ, in whom we are established; for the rod of Aaron, having once blossomed, foreshadowed thee, O uncultivated and pure one, O ever-virgin dove.
existence, was in reality the bearer of the demon, and will you think that it would not be a horror to Christ to be borne by her? Would the species of the dove be hateful to you from the first age, and would the truth, corrupted a little while before, come to Christ? And yet the dove contracted nothing in reality from the demon, it handed nothing over to God; but what Mary contracted from that, and what she gave to God, all know. Why, therefore, would the Holy Spirit not prepare in her inmost parts a guest-chamber and a singular throne for the divine Word in the most pure dove, the Spirit who thoroughly avoided for himself even the corrupted shadow of a dove?
OF JOSEPH THE HYMNOGRAPHER
The hosts of the angels were amazed, seeing in what manner the Invisible, in the form of our nature assumed from you, O Virgin Mother of God, became visible: whom do you suppliantly entreat, that he may render all who faithfully glorify you worthy of salvation.
Your miracle, O Pure One, seizes every mind with wonder; for you give birth to God with a body, and you nourish with milk the One who provides nourishment, without the experience of a husband, as He alone knows who has seen it Himself.
Mary, you who have been manifested as the tabernacle of sanctification, sanctify my wretched soul, defiled by the filth of pleasures, and make it a partaker of divine glory.
Finding you alone to be most pure, O All-Immaculate One, the most pure Word of God, brought forth from your womb, cleanses us, the faithful, from the filth of the passions arising in us from intemperance, O Bride of God.
As rain, Christ descended into your womb, O Virgin, and truly irrigated all creation, drying up, O Virgin, the muddy rivers of idolatry, He who alone is the benefactor.
Spare us who hymn you, O Lord, the ineffable birth from the Virgin, delivering your servants from temptations, passions, and afflictions by her intercessions: for you are indeed beneficent and the only lover of mankind.
From the canon for Saint Marinus [(97*)], on the 16th.
Hail, multi-named maiden: holy Mary, Mother of Christ, and Virgin: boast of the faithful, redemption of the curse, recall of Eve, unintelligible miracle, unburnt bush, unplowed earth.
The voices of the God-speaking prophets predicted you, O Virgin, as the future Mother of God, who for His ineffable mercy assumed human form.
The barrier of the ancient curse is broken by your birth-giving: for you bring forth God, Emmanuel, O most chaste One, who enlightened and gladdened all the ends of the earth with blessings: whom, praising, we faithfully glorify you.
You brought forth a new infant for us, O chaste One, who was born from the Father without time before the ages: therefore, O Maiden, we rightly call you blessed.
Ezekiel saw you as a gate, O Mother of God, through which the Sun of glory passed, who snatched man from corruption: whom entreat for the redemption of your servants.
Mother of God Mary, with constant prayers, supplicate your Lord and Son, that those may be delivered from fire who, with affection, sing and modulate: Blessed are You, O God of our fathers.
Jacob saw you as a ladder, O most pure One, on which God was leaning, raising those from earth to heaven who with orthodox faith cry out constantly: Bless the Lord, O works of the Lord.
Having been made the Mother of God far from every corruption and filth, now a seat more eminent than all the heavenly orders; and all generations praise you and call you blessed with affection, just as you predicted, O chaste One: therefore free the world from every necessity by your prayers.
From the canon for the feast of Saint Sebastian and his companions, on the 18th.
You gave birth to a new son, He who with the Father before...
and having renewed the laws of nature, O chaste Virgin Mother, inviolate in your divine and venerable childbirth, which was above all nature.
You have become the spiritual sanctification of Him who sanctifies all things, and a pure tabernacle for the world, O most immaculate Bride of God; for from you appeared God incarnate, who is made known to the world in dual nature and yet in a single hypostasis.
God, who is above all substance, chose you alone out of all generations, and He, the Molder of human existence, became substantial man for our sake, O Mother of God, most immaculate Lady.
O most immaculate, most radiant cloud of the sun, dispel the clouds of my soul through your intercessions, and enlighten my mind, obscured by the darkness of negligence, that I may praise you, O worthy of all praise.
You have renewed our substance, corrupted by transgression, by bringing forth Him who alone renews all things by His divine will, O blessed among women, most full of divine grace.
We name you, O chaste one, a golden urn, a most holy table of the bread of life from God, a place of sanctification, a most high throne in which rested the God of our fathers, who is worthy of all praise.
You were made beautiful by giving birth to the beautiful God and Lord, who illuminates mortals with His divine rays, to whom we cry out: "Bless the Lord, all you works."
The spiritual hosts tremble, seeing the divine splendor of the Father held in your arms in an inexplicable manner, and possessing your likeness, so that He might deify mortals, O Virgin Mother, not united to a man.
*From the canon for the holy martyr Boniface, on the 19th day.*
Let us praise with songs the holy Virgin, the mountain of God which Daniel foresaw, the spiritual tabernacle, the venerable tablet, the sanctification of glory, the table that contained the divine bread.
The God who is above all substance emptied Himself into your womb, without emptying the Father’s bosom, and became your Son, O most immaculate one, to save the human race.
Understanding, O Maiden, that your virginity remained sealed after childbirth, you faithfully magnified the Word who was ineffably born from your womb.
*We call you the ark of the new law,*
*And the tablet of the new law,*
*Sculpted by the Deity Himself,*
*On which God inscribed His own Word.*
Beautifully, [she is called] the tablet of the new law, alien to the old law of sin and the common fellowship of the ancient transgression; more beautifully: sculpted by the Deity Himself, so that God alone might be the artificer of Mary’s conception.
I cry to you, O Virgin! Cleanse my soul from every defilement, and save me, O chaste one, you who gave body on earth to the true God, the Savior. The bush prefigured you, O most praiseworthy and most chaste one, while it burned yet was not consumed; for you, in similar fashion, were not consumed although God was incarnate from you. In order that I may praise you with joyous voices, O Maiden, deliver me by your intercessions from dangers, tribulations, and the wicked thoughts that strive to vex me. Upon you, the chaste one, the One above divinity descended; He was incarnate in the way He Himself knows, and deified men, who sing together: “Bless all works and praise the Lord.” Illumine me with your light, O most pure Theotokos, for I am occupied by the darkness of sin, and grant me, O Bride of God, to walk in the daylight of the divine commandments, so that I may praise you, the all-praiseworthy one.
From the canon for the vigil or preparation for the feast of the Nativity of the Lord, day 20.
Eden is opened, as long as you are born, O Lord, from the God-child maiden in the city of Bethlehem in the flesh; we glorify your fearful economy. A star has already risen from the tribe of Judah, which, when the kings recognized it, they made their way from the East and hastened so that they might see Christ born in the flesh in Bethlehem. How, O Word, will the most narrow and most humble cave receive you, born in the flesh? How will you be wrapped in swaddling clothes, you who clothe the heavens with clouds? How will you be reclined as an infant in the stable of brute beasts? O Eden, once closed to me, open henceforward, seeing Christ the infant incarnate, and born in the city of Bethlehem, as it pleased Him, from the Maiden Virgin. In the cave of Bethlehem, the Maiden clearly brings forth God, the Maker of the universe, and having wrapped Him as a human in swaddling clothes, she now reclines Him in the manger. Let us attend to the holy words; the Lord is born a child for us, whose government is upon his shoulder, and he is called the Angel of the great counsel of the Father, Christ, the Prince of peace. As the Lord swore, behold, He has fulfilled the oath, giving us from the seed of David his own Mother, the Virgin, from whom the infant was born in the flesh in the city of Bethlehem, beyond all conception of words. The Virgin, a spiritual alabaster jar, carries Christ, the inexhaustible ointment, which goes forth in the cave of Bethlehem to be clearly poured out in spirit, so that He may fill our souls with his sweet fragrance.
From the canon for the feast of St. Juliana the martyr of Nicomedia, day 21.
The Virgin hastens to bring forth the Creator of nature in
the cave; he who from her, according to an ineffable hypostasis, took on flesh like a garment in a manner above nature, so as to deify the human race.
The compassionate One, in order to set mortals free, is born from the holy Virgin in Bethlehem, receiving swaddling clothes like an infant.
Beholding her virginity sealed after childbirth, the Theotokos was struck with wonder and cried out: "O Son, how shall I now swaddle Thee, who surround the sea with sand as with swaddling clothes?"
wondrous miracle! The immaculate Virgin hastens in the cave of Bethlehem to bring forth God made man.
He who by the nod of his will surrounds the sea with mist as with a swaddling band, being the Creator, is born of the Virgin maiden, and receives swaddling clothes as an infant, in order to redeem the world.
Hail, container of the Uncontainable, Mother-Virgin; for you are about to bring forth in the cave, O immaculate one, Him who is clothed in flesh for our sake, who restores the workmanship of his own hands.
The Lord, who makes the cloud his chariot, comes to us through the cloud of the Virgin to be born, so that he may disperse the dark clouds of the sins of our souls, while we cry out to him: "Bless the Lord, all you works of the Lord, the Lord."
Bearing Him who bears all things, you come to Bethlehem, O Virgin, there to bring him forth and to lay him, as an infant, in a manger, accomplishing in a wondrous way the restoration of mortals.
From the double canon for the feast of the holy great martyr Anastasia, day 22.
He who is rich becomes poor, born of the Virgin because of his compassion. The Magi, kings from the East, prepare their departure to behold Him incarnate and to worship him in the flesh.
God, who was invisible, appeared, born in a manner above human nature from you, O Mother-Virgin, because of his great compassion, having become poor, though he was rich, so that he might enrich the human race with immortality.
This is our only God, who, truly clothed ineffably in flesh from you, O Virgin, hastens to be born in a cave, so that he may make me, who have become a den of thieves, a temple of the divine Spirit.
O maiden who has not known man, you carry in your womb Him who is incarnate, who holds the entire creation; whom, even when born from you, you lay in a manger as an infant, though He is seen as the One before the ages.
The words of those who prophesied in the holy Spirit are now fulfilled: for the Virgin hastens to bring forth in the cave the most perfect God.
The heavenly King, O immaculate one, comes forth from your light-bearing womb, and is laid in a manger as on a throne.
Now the Word of the Father has come to his own, born in a new birth from the Virgin, and is seen as an infant in the cave because of his supreme compassion.
Christ hastens to be born from the Virgin in an underground cave. Let all creation exult.
O living city of God, you bring forth Christ in the city of Bethlehem, O Theotokos, for he has become perfect man beyond understanding, through his compassion.
Healing the human nature that was corrupted by the ancient transgression, without corruption he is born a new infant, and he sits in your bosom as on a throne, O unwedded one, not departing from the fellowship of the Father’s divinity.
The incarnate Word proceeds from your womb in an ineffable manner, O inviolate one, and he who is before the ages begins to be, and lies in a manger wrapped in swaddling clothes, dissolving the chains of our offenses.
O miracle that strikes the mind with awe! You are about to give birth, O Virgin Mother, to perfect God; and you are to lay in a manger him who is inaccessible to the very Cherubim and who is immortal by nature.
Now the Lord, who is present everywhere, has come, born of the Virgin in the city of Bethlehem. Exult, O creation, meeting him and chanting hymns of glory unto all ages.
O maiden most pleasing to God, you will bring forth the infant Creator of the ages, who is altogether immutable, in the city of Bethlehem, because of his ineffable mercy.
Bringing forth human nature, O holy Virgin Mother, you give birth in the city of Bethlehem to the transcendent Word, and you nourish with milk, as is the duty of a mother, him who nourishes all creation; and as a fiery throne you carry him, O most holy one, higher than the Cherubim.
Let all creation now joyfully exult, for the Theotokos now hastens to give birth to the Word of God, who is God, having become man.
From the canon for the vigil or preparations for the Nativity of the Lord, on the 23rd day.
When the kings of the Persians knew you, O Word of God, to be the King born on earth of the Virgin, they came with gifts, hastening to worship you.
Christ, delivering us from the darkness of malice, comes forth in the flesh to be born as a man.
The Lord, coming to redeem the human race from the ancient curse, is born of you in the flesh, O most inviolate and blessed one; therefore we glorify you with praises, for you are our glory and pride.
Now Christ comes into his own in a foreign body: let us all be pilgrims from dishonest passions, and let us receive him born in the flesh.
How, O King, shall a most narrow cave receive you, who became poor in spirit yet enrich all things? How shall the nature of mortals behold you clothed in a body? We worship your humiliation.
We praise you, O uniquely chaste one, the cause of all good things; for you gave birth to the incarnate Word because of the excess of his own goodness; a star in the city of Bethlehem heralded his birth.
The Lord, beautiful and the giver of good things, proceeds from your womb to be born, O Virgin, in an ineffable manner, wishing to adorn the human race with incorruption. To him we now sing: Let all creation praise the Lord and exalt him above all for all ages.
"You carry, my Son, the whole idea of the Spirit, and how do I carry you, who have become like me in all respects?" the Virgin asked, struck with wonder; let us, the faithful, all honor her as the Mother of God, and in praise let us glorify her with one voice.
From the canon for the Sunday after the Nativity of Christ, on which we celebrate the memory of Saint Joseph, the betrothed of the most holy Theotokos.
You gave birth in the flesh to Christ in Bethlehem, O unwed Virgin, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes; struck with fear at his coming, Joseph magnifies him and adores his power.
When Joseph the Just saw that God had taken flesh from your chaste womb, O pure Virgin, and had been born in a cave and placed in a manger, he magnified him with hymns, he who appeared as one of us.
To remove every doubt from your mind, the invisible one appeared to you clearly, saying, "Do not fear, Joseph, to take Mary now, the immaculate one; for she bears in her womb him who holds all things by his divine power."
She was found, as the prophet David said, to be a Virgin in the womb, containing God, the Emmanuel, who is by nature boundless. When the divine Joseph did not understand this, he was taught by an angel in the night while he slept.
You saw a new child on earth, O most noble Joseph, born of a chaste Virgin, he who was born of the Father before all ages; and you heard the angels praising him inside the cave, lying in a manger, O all-laudable Joseph.
The righteous Joseph, O Virgin most dear to God, having acknowledged you prefigured by sacred symbols, received your venerable betrothal by the lot of the rod, calling to mind the holy rod of Aaron that once had blossomed.
You saw the shadows of the Law bathed in the abundance of the light of grace; and from the Virgin, the luminous cloud, you gazed upon the intelligible Sun rising in the flesh; and like a star, O wise Joseph, you illuminated all who cry out ceaselessly: Let all creation bless the Lord.
You guarded, O God-bearing Joseph, the Virgin who preserved her virginity incorrupt; from whom God the Word was incarnate, preserving her a virgin after the ineffable birth. You, O Joseph, together with her, be mindful of us.
From the canon for the holy twenty thousand martyrs who were consumed by fire in the city of Nicomedia, on the 28th day.
I sing your praises, O most laudable and blessed one, over God...
S. JOSEPH THE HYMNOGRAPHER]
and blessed, who in the flesh gave birth to God, who is superior to all praises, and who has glorified the triumphant victors over the enemy.
That He might deify human nature, God became man from you, O chaste Virgin, in an ineffable and unthinkable manner; therefore we, the faithful, with harmonious voices call you blessed.
Having been redeemed by your delivery, O blessed one, from the ancient curse, we have received a blessing, life, and redemption, we who glorify you as the Theotokos.
That God might unite with the celestial spirits those who had slipped into the great abyss of transgression, He inhabited your womb, O most inviolate one, and became flesh.
By the power of Jesus, who was incarnate of you, O Blessed Mary, you remained truly a virgin after birth, just as you had been before birth. O miracle that transcends human faith!
You appeared higher than the heavens, having given birth to the Lord and God of all, whom cease not to implore fervently and with great intensity for the salvation of those who glorify you with fervent faith.
Ezekiel sees you, O Virgin, as the closed gate, through which passed Jesus who dwelt in your womb, and took flesh from your blood without any mixture or confusion.
O most immaculate and chaste one, who gave birth to that divine light which shone forth from the Father, have mercy on my soul, darkened by the errors of life and made a mockery by the enemy, and count it worthy of the light of saving repentance, O pure one.
THEOTOKIA FROM THE PARACLETICUS
THEOTOCIA.
From the Greek Paracletica (99).
From the canon for Tuesday, at Matins. Tone I.
The orders of the incorporeal ones sing hymns to you together with us, O Virgin worthy of all praise; for you bore within your womb the One who cannot be contained.


[1043] {#pg.105.1043}
A ruined, he took away the wall of enmity standing between us, established peace, and bestowed life and divine redemption.
Virgin chaste, you remained so after birth, O most holy; for you gave birth to God the Word, who became like us, without sin. Heal the wounds of my heart, O Maiden, and direct the movements of my soul on a straight and happy path to perform the will of God, O Virgin.
Hail, lone Mother of Him who begged for our flesh; hail, raising up of the fallen world, O most immaculate; hail, dissolution of sorrow; hail, salvation of the faithful; hail, most high throne of God.
Revolving in their minds, the divine-speaking prophets proclaimed the depth of your mystery, O Virgin, prophetically, illuminated by the divine Spirit; and we, now seeing the forecasts fulfilled in deed, gaze with great joy and believe.   O more-than-admirable Maiden, you bore Him for us who is before all ages and who was made like us through His extreme compassion, that He might save those who sing: Blessed are You, the God of our fathers.
Following your divine words, the generations of men call you blessed, O ever-blessed one, sweetly singing together: Bless the Lord, all you works.   O Virgin, lover of good things, make good my soul, which has been corrupted by the malice of sin; for you gave birth to the good God and Lord.
*From the Canon on the Vigil of the Lights, or Epiphany, day 3.*
O miracle of miracles! How is it that our God, who is above all creation, is created and formed from the Mother of God; and by His own will, He renews and fashions us again out of water and spirit, a most wonderful creation, He the only Benefactor?   The Cherubim and every heavenly nature shudder, O most immaculate one, out of reverence for your incomprehensible and venerable Offspring, who became like us through His ineffable mercy and was baptized in the flesh; whose divine appearance we now all celebrate with rejoicing.
*From the Canon on the holy seventy apostles, day 4.*
Let us honor the divine palace of the King, in which He dwelt as He willed; let us praise the unwedded and only Theotokos, through whom we have been deified.   Truly, you appeared as Virgin-Mother, chaste before birth, in birth, and after birth; for you gave birth to God, whom the assembly of the apostles manifestally proclaimed.   The most blessed choir of prophets of old...
Note: To the Bishop of Cythera, Antonius Pinellus of Venice published in 1529, in quarto. But since in the Menæa, of which we have spoken, there are very many canons of our Joseph scattered throughout each month concerning the praises of the saints, all those things from among them which pertained to the Theotokos have been culled, and now present themselves to the eyes of the pious to be read.


[1045] {#pg.105.1045}
in the Spirit, invokes thee divinely, O most pure one, as the gate and the shaded mountain.
Illumine, O Virgin, the eyes of my heart; shine upon me with the ray of repentance; deliver me from the everlasting darkness, O gate of light, refuge of all Christians who faithfully sing thy praises.
I praise thee, the only one worthy of all praise; I glorify thee, O ever-glorified by God; and I call thee blessed, whom generations of generations call blessed, O Virgin most blessed by God.
Thou hast become an expiation, O most pure one, for those who are always sinning, having given birth in an order above nature to Christ who takes away the sin of the world, to whom we cry out: Blessed art Thou, O Lord and God of our fathers.
O miracle surpassing all miracles! How dost thou give birth and remain a Virgin, O most pure bride of God? For thou hast brought forth the Word, co-eternal with the Father, to whom we all sing: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and superexalt Him unto all ages.
The splendor of the lightning of thy delivery shone forth and brightened the whole world, and destroyed the prince of darkness, O most pure Mother of God, the boast of angels and the salvation of all men who celebrate thee with unceasing voices.
From the Canon for our holy Mother Domnica, day 8.
Before birth thou wert incorrupt, O pure one, and after birth thou remained Mother of God, in a manner above nature; wherefore Domnica, desiring thee in the Holy Spirit, was led after thee, incorrupt, to thy son, the King of all, O immaculate one.
Strengthen, O most immaculate Lady, my weakness, [thou] who gavest birth to the power of the Most High, who grantest being to all, and who magnified the memory of Domnica.
Adam cast off the tunics of mortality by thy divine birth, and clothed himself in the robe which the Word alone, becoming incarnate, wove in thy womb.
Thou hast brought forth the Holy Lord of all, O Giver of the Lord, whom Domnica, desiring from her soul, dominates the death-dealing passions, O Virgin, praising thee.
For my sake, like unto me, that infant became, He who is most perfect, that He might renew me, grown old from passions, through thee, most holy bride of God.
My strength, and my praise, and my salvation is the Lord, who chose thee beforehand as a most pure Mother and an unwedded bride; before whom do not cease to intercede for thy servants, O immaculate one.
The supersubstantial God becomes substance for our sake from thy bowels, desiring to renew the corrupted substance through pity, O Virgin, and through mercy, He who is glorified unto all ages.
Spare me, O Lord, spare me, when Thou shalt come to judge,


[1047] {#pg.105.1047}
and do not condemn me to the fire, do not reprove me in Thy wrath. The Virgin who gave Thee birth, O Christ, entreats Thee together with the hosts of angels and the orders of the saints.
From the Canon to the holy martyrs Hermylus and Stratonicus, day 13.
The Lord, who cannot be grasped or contained by any creature, is contained within Thee, O Lady, having become mortal through His mercy, so that He might save mortals through His ineffable love for mankind.
O most holy one, who didst give birth to the most holy Word, sanctify our souls and bodies, while we bless Thee who art worthy of all praise.
The new infant, the Lord who is before the ages, appearing from the Virgin and becoming mortal, renews human nature. Let us sing to Him: Glory to Thy power, O Lord.
Thou didst give birth to God beyond speech and thought, and Thou didst remain a virgin after birth as Thou wast before birth, O chaste one, most dear to God.
Cause the waves of my fleshly passions to rest, I pray Thee, O Maiden, and as it were to fall asleep, through Thy ever-vigilant intercession; and do not allow me to fall into the deepest sleep of sin.
Thee, who didst bear in Thy womb the Manna of life, that ancient jar which contained the manna most truly and clearly prefigured. Blessed art Thou among women, O most pure Lady.   Through Thee the ancient Paradise is opened once again, and man, formerly condemned, is brought into it, and is truly deified, O chaste one, full of God’s grace, the lump of mortals who cry out: All ye works, praise the Lord.
The Cherubim shudder, seeing that Word who is inexpressibly present among them and who rests there, held as an infant in the arms of Thy mother, O most holy Lady, who surpassest in the height of Thy dignity all created things.
From the other Canon for the same saints.
Check the floods of my sins, Thou who didst dry up the corruption of death by Thy birth; and grant me compunction, O most pure Mother of God.   That turning sword, which used to bar the entrance to Paradise, blushes and is filled with shame, seeing the lance which pierced Thy Son, O Virgin Mother—He who was born of Thee.
Awaken me from sloth, for I am asleep and covered in sins; call me to repentance, O most chaste one, as Mother of the Word.
As fair, as beautiful, as radiant with the brightness of purity, Thou didst embody the Word who is beautiful in form and didst give Him birth, O Virgin Mother: He who by divine operation gives existence to all from the riches of His goodness.
Heal, O Virgin Mother of God, as one who is compassionate, the passions of my infirm soul, and the pain of my heart, O Virgin, and the wanderings of my


[1049] {#pg.105.1049}
and calm the grievous storm of my passions, I beseech thee.
Loosing the curse of Eve, thou didst dwell in a womb free from all stain, pouring forth a fountain of blessing to those who cry aloud: Blessed, O most pure one, is the fruit of thy womb.
He who is in all things perfect and by nature inaccessible, was made accessible to me, being clothed in flesh from thee, O unwedded one; whom do thou fervently beseech to scatter the burden of my iniquities, and to save me as I sing: Priests, bless; O ye people, superexalt Christ unto all ages.
Spare me, O Savior, who wast born and didst keep her who bore thee undefiled after the birth, when thou shalt sit to judge my works, overlooking my iniquities and my sins, as one sinless, as a merciful God and lover of mankind.
From the Canon to Saint John the Hut-Dweller, day 18.
By the grievous assaults of my passions, O Virgin, being tossed by a tempest, and shaken by the onslaughts of sin, I flee with longing to thy sleepless protection, O all-praised one. Have mercy on me, and save me, O Ever-Virgin.
As a myrrh-breathing rose, O undefiled one, did the Pure One find thee in the valleys, and He dwelt in the midst of thee, filling the human race with most sweet fragrance.
Direct the impulses of my soul, O all-immaculate one, toward the divine commandments of Him who shone forth from thy womb, delivering me by thy intercessions from the tempest of the scandals of this life.
Thou didst bear Emmanuel, the Lord of all, without the seed of a man, remaining a virgin even after the birth, O Virgin-Mother; whom do thou unceasingly entreat to deliver from the invasions of enemies those who flee under thy protection.
The Word, who is co-equal in operation and upon the throne with His Begetter, thou didst embody from thy womb, O chaste one, because of His ineffable compassion, having assumed our whole nature.
We praise thy birth-giving, O blessed one, through which we were redeemed from ancient condemnation; and we call thee blessed, O divinely-blessed one, whom alone He loved who is blessed and super-glorious.
A perennial river thou pourest forth for us who flee to thee, O chaste one; of whose abundant grace tasting, we praise thy birth-giving, O most inviolate one, and superexalt it unto all eternity.
Thy womb became the dwelling-place of Light, through whom those who sat in darkness have seen the light; whence we continually praise thee with unceasing voices, O Mother of God, and with longing we venerate the hope of our souls.
From the Canon to the Adoration of the Precious Chains of the Holy and All-Praised Apostle Peter, day 16.
All the swords of the deceitful enemy have failed, O undefiled Virgin.


[1051] {#pg.105.1051}
Since that time when that Word, who dwelt within your undefiled womb, was wounded by the lance, I beseech you now to wound my heart with his most sweet love.
Death halted when it reached you, its unbridled impetus checked; for you alone gave birth to the fountain of immortality, O Mother of God, Virgin Mother.
As the King of all, inhabiting your holy womb as a spacious palace, he appeared incarnate, O most pure Lady. Burdened as I am, O undefiled one, by the weight of many sins, lift me up now, strengthening me to bear the most light yoke of Christ. Our first father was clothed in the leather tunics of mortality; but the Creator is clothed in him, having become incarnate from your blood beyond all understanding, O all-blameless one.
He who descended upon the earth as rain, O Virgin, watered the whole earth with divine knowledge, and showed you to be more honorable than all the angels, O pure one. The prophet of old prefigured you as an intellectual candelabra, O Mother of God, bearing the divine lamp which enlightened those who were formerly overshadowed by the many darknesses of evil. You became a dwelling-place of light: therefore enlighten me, O maiden, darkened by all the unbelief of the enemy, so that in faith I may magnify you, O most holy Mother-Virgin.
From the Canon to the Holy Martyrs Speusippus, Eleusippus, and Meleusippus, on the 16th day
You appeared as an unplowed earth, O most august Mother of God, most chaste; you brought forth for us the provider of all, the Lord Jesus, of whom we partake and are recalled to life. Seeing God incarnate from you, O chaste Virgin Mother of God, we properly confess you, who were clearly the cause of the reformation of all things. That superessential One, who was without flesh, became incarnate from your venerable blood, O most chaste one; and having become flesh without any change, he conversed with men. The laws of nature are truly made new in you, O most pure Virgin: for you remain a Virgin after the birth, just as you were before the birth, having given birth to Christ the Lawgiver. Heal the passions of my miserable soul, O   most chaste Mother of God; render my mind, which is tossed like a storm by the invasions of the enemy, tranquil and peaceful, O maiden.   Jesus, the planter of all, truly found you to be a rose in the midst of thorns in the valleys of this world, O chaste Virgin, and born from your womb, he poured over us the most sweet fragrance of divine knowledge. We have acknowledged you as the spiritual candelabra, O Virgin Mary, for you received the inaccessible light, and you illuminated the souls of all the faithful and eliminated the darkness of sin. With voices full of thanksgiving we cry out to you: Hail, most pure dwelling-place of immaterial light; hail, cause of the deification of all; hail, dissolution of the curse; hail, recall of the exiled children of earth.
From the Canon to the Holy Martyr Neophytus, on the 21st day
Having given birth to the Creator by nature, you have deified the whole substance of those born of the earth; therefore we rightly confess you to be the Theotokos, O Virgin, Bride of God. The race of mortals ever offers a hymn of thanksgiving to you, Mother of God, having obtained immortality through you.

(51) It is a distinguished praise of the Theotokos that she was always kept untainted by any sin with regard to the state of grace, and was positioned far from the curse and subjection to the devil, outside the common defilement of nature. Therefore, by this praise, of which she is most worthy, she ought to be celebrated by all who desire to praise her. Furthermore, that this praise of the Theotokos is everywhere excellent, it ought to be beyond all doubt. It is most a matter of wonder that the Abulensis, although he thinks excellently of the conception of Mary, affirms that she was immune from sin, and pronounces that to be safer and clearly more eligible, at length arrived at saying: "The praise and glory of the Theotokos is not changed or diminished in this, if it is said that she incurred original sin, as those think who do not penetrate the nature of original sin":   since it is no small glory to be always like to God, and to have been exempt by the benefit of God from the state of unlikeness to God, which is original sin, and likewise from the stain of sin, which by its nature corrupts and infects, nay even kills the soul: just as, on the contrary, his praise is not diminished, who is supposed to be sullied by that stain. See Velasquez, *De Maria immaculate concepta*, lib. 11, dissertat. 5, annot. 1, where he shows that the most holy Virgin cannot be praised according to her dignity, unless to the common praises of the Theotokos that is added, which is surely that she was immaculately conceived. Moreover, Ambrosius Catharinus in his disputation *Pro immaculata conceptione*, lib. 1, acting against some who said that it did not pertain to the praise of Mary that she was preserved from the stain of original sin, says among other things: "What they add, furthermore, that it pertains little to the praise of the Lady that we ascribe to her the privilege of preservation from original sin, is absolutely unthinkable. Do they, I ask, think the foulness of sin, the wrath and enmity of God, and   slavery to the devil to be a small evil, even if one were held by these great evils for a short moment? But those who see the matter with spiritual eyes do not think so. Wherefore they judge it to be a great thing that she was saved from this so miserable condition by a singular gift, just as that woman herself, exulting in spirit, professed (Luke 1): *For He who is mighty has done great things for me.* But if we were to profess this gift, even in itself, to be small, yet surely it would become great, both by the excellence of the Giver, and also by the singularity of it, to whom alone it was given; for, as someone said excellently, even small gifts, when bestowed by great princes, are reckoned great and favorable. Finally, if that man, the diligent examiner and prudent appraiser of spiritual things, Augustine, could not without horror think about the flesh of Mary, once dead, being subject to corruption for any point of time (as he himself testifies), how much less should this certainly be thought concerning that most sacred soul, that it could truly be said to have been corrupted by sin, subject to the power of the devil, and finally, for any moment, even an enemy to God? But why do I delay further? When even in this place they fight diametrically against the opinion of the Blessed Thomas? For what they make of such little account, Thomas himself on the contrary makes so much of, that he therefore denies it is fitting for Mary, because it seemed too exalted, in that by it she seemed to be made equal to Christ. We, however, as we will declare in our own places, confess that it is indeed great, yet not so great that it ascends to the Majesty of Christ. Wherefore it is completely frivolous what they added, that it suffices that she be celebrated as the Mother of God, and that alone in place of all praise; for by this very reasoning they would conclude that she not be praised as Virgin, that she not be honored as sanctified, and that her glorious Assumption, and other titles of prerogatives in which she abounds, should be passed over in silence. Thus Catharinus in the cited place.

D ...that the Deipara is called [such], it must be asserted that every stain of sin, whether actual or original, had been entirely removed from her.
(54) To effect the body of Christ in the Eucharist, an immaculate host is required, and it is offered to God thus: "We offer to Thee, O Lord, an immaculate host": which is understood to persist everywhere clean and as unleavened bread without any leaven. Therefore, in the mystery of the Incarnation, the Son of God had to take flesh from an immaculate and most pure Mother subject to no old leaven, as learned authors observe that in ancient times, on the hosts in which the body of Christ was to be consecrated, images of the Mother of God were carved, so that the immunity of the Deipara from the stain of sin might be explained by the immaculate host of the Eucharist. See Velasquez, *De Maria Concepta*, book II, dissert. 2, annotat. 1, n. 5.
