Thou didst bring forth the subsistent Wisdom of God, O inviolate Virgin Mother of God, who made the saints most wise, by whom the pride of the architect of malice fell, and his worst stratagems.
O miracle of all miracles! The greatest, that a Virgin conceiving without male operation did not straiten in her womb Him who embraces all things.
O Virgin Bride of God, who without the experience of a bridal chamber, and without the corruption of seed, didst conceive the Only-begotten of the Father and bring Him forth in the flesh from thy immaculate bloods, cease not to pour forth prayers for the salvation of the world.
Me, surrounded by many perils and most dangerously tossed by the tempest of sins, guide now, O Lady Mother of God, by the breath of the Holy Spirit to the most peaceful harbor; for thou art the haven of Christians; wherefore we praise thee unto all ages.
Most lucid Mother of the Creator, consolation of those who mourn, protection of those in danger, and aid of those who labor, and swift visitation of the sick, guard me so long as I shall live.
MONTH OF JULY
From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyrs Cosmas and Damian, on the 1st
Thee, the seat and possession of God, the spiritual table, the beauty of Jacob, the bridge most happy and easy for crossing, and the stable and immovable ladder, O immaculate one, all the generations of men call blessed with affection.
He who is formidable to the celestial armies dwelt in thee in an ineffable manner, O chaste Virgin, having found thee purer than every nature, visible and intelligible; therefore we call thee blessed.
The lamp of divine light, superior to all creatures, which deified man, inasmuch as it brought forth God, is glorified as Mother of God.
Make to arise upon me, O Lady, a ray of divine knowledge, since I am severely oppressed by the darkness of ignorance; and lead me to the light of repentance, O immaculate one, as thou art the gate of light.
Save me, thou who brought forth the Savior; for the depth of sins disturbs me, and the tempest of desires tosses me, and the storm of the spirits of wickedness afflicts me.
Christ shall descend, as rain upon the fleece, into thy womb, O most dear to God; and He shall cause the torrents of iniquity to cease, as God; and He shall pour forth immortality and life as a fountain to those who sing: Blessed is the God of our Fathers.


[1139] {#pg.105.1139}
From your sacred blood the Creator of all has been incarnate, and has come forth from your womb, guarding you as a virgin. O miracle of miracles! O manifestation of new mysteries, accomplished in you for all ages!
Having appeared, O Virgin, higher than the Cherubim, make my mind higher than carnal pleasures and the temptations of life, and grant me to walk steadily in the paths of salvation, which lead, O Immaculate One, to the city on high.
From the Canon to the holy Thomas in the Palaion, and to the holy martyr Kyriake, day 7.
You stayed the violence of death, O chaste one, having given birth to Christ, the Bestower of immortality, at whom Hades trembled when it saw Him dead by voluntary decree.
Having given birth to the substantial Wisdom of God, O Virgin, deliver me from the sophist of malice by your intercession, O only all-blameless one.
Deliver from every evil of the enemy, O Virgin, those who truly know you to be the Mother of God, O all-pure one.
From another Canon to the Holy Unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian.
The Creator of all, as God, became incarnate from your pure blood, and came forth from your womb, guarding you, Virgin. O miracle of miracles! O manifestation of new mysteries, which have been wrought in you for all ages!
Having appeared, O Virgin, higher than the Cherubim, make my mind higher than carnal pleasures and the temptations of life, and grant me to walk steadily in the paths of salvation, which lead, O Immaculate One, to the city on high.
You fashioned the Savior and God from your chaste blood, O pure and inviolate one, who gave us as doctors of our passions, and fervent defenders, the wise Unmercenaries in spirit.
God chose you, most beautiful among women, and it pleased Him, who rests in His saints, to be born of you corporally, O chaste one.
Make me worthy through your compassion, O inviolate Virgin, who gave birth to the uniquely compassionate Word, who granted to all the ends of the earth holy, compassionate doctors and miracle-workers.
You gave birth to the substantial Wisdom of God, O inviolate Mother of God, who granted us the holy, all-wise ones, through whom the pride of the architect of malice and his most grievous stratagems have fallen.
The most pure Word made you a clean temple, O Lady, and He ever magnifies the divine Church of the Unmercenaries with signs and wonders.
O Maria, rod that sprouted from the root of Jesse, you brought forth, O inviolate one, the flower, Christ, who adorns His servants, the Unmercenaries, as with flowers, with miracles.
Death is destroyed in you; for you gave birth to the substantial Life, Christ the Lord, O inviolate one, protector of our life, who gave the Unmercenaries as doctors to those who cry: Bless all things.
You have become, O Virgin, the dwelling-place of that Light which has illuminated all things, and has now granted the light-bearing saints, who eliminate the darkness of deadly passions in the spirit, O only ever-inviolate Virgin.
From another Canon to the Holy Unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian.
Pour out upon us now, O chaste one, the drops of your mercies, you who ineffably gave birth to the good, the pious, and the merciful one, and who now exist as the protection of all.
He who alone is good, alone intimately merciful, has entered your immaculate womb, O totally immaculate one, wishing to reform us who are defiled by passions.
In you, O Virgin Mother of God, I have placed my hopes, that I might be delivered from all the malice of the enemy.
O chaste Lady, who gave birth to the incarnate God in an incomprehensible manner, ever entreat Him to deliver me from carnal passions and from eternal torments.
He who joined the lower things to the upper in your birth, O most chaste one, let Him keep in a tranquil state us who exalt you with praises.
He who is the Mountain of God, from whom the Truth is manifested, you are, O chaste Virgin, in whom He who is incomprehensible dwelt, and wished to become similar to men because of the excess of His mercy: to whom we chant: Blessed are you, etc.
Behold, O my soul, the gate of light, which now opens the entrances of repentance: behold the ladder of Jacob; the sole protection and defense of men: hasten through her intercessions to obtain mercy.
Acknowledging you, O Lady, to be the truly lucid cloud of the Sun of justice, may we be delivered through your intercession from the darkest shadows and from eternal punishment, O you who are free from every stain.
From the Canon in the feast of St. Thomas of the Palaion and St. Cyriaca the martyr, day 7.
You stayed the violence of death, O chaste one, having given birth to Christ, the Bestower of immortality, at whom Hades trembled when it saw Him dead by voluntary decree.
Having given birth to the substantial Wisdom of God, O Virgin, deliver me from the sophist of malice by your intercession, O only all-blameless one.
Deliver from every evil of the enemy, O Virgin, those who truly know you to be the Mother of God, O all-pure one.
(64****) This canon, with the following one, is missing in the printed Menaia.


[1141] {#pg.105.1141}
You have dissolved, O undefiled one, the curse of the first parents, having brought forth without the will of the flesh, O venerable one, Him who by His own divine will clearly produced all things.
Having brought forth Christ the King, as a queen, O God-graced one, make those who run to you worthy of the kingdom of heaven.
The only God found your womb alone to be pure, and is embodied and is recognized as man, saving man; whence, acknowledging you as the cause of good things, we sing: Blessed are you, who brought forth God in the flesh.
The supersubstantial God was made substantial according to us from you, O Virgin, and was seen as an infant, He who is from before the ages with the Father and the divine Spirit; whence we glorify you as His mother.
By the most radiant lamps of Him who was incarnate from you, O all-holy Virgin, we who know you above human thought to be the Theotokos are illuminated by faith, and are set free from the darkness of passions, and from all dangers and every tribulation.
*From the Canon to the holy martyrs Patermuthius and Copres, day 9 (64****)*
Put to death the affections of my heart, you who ineffably brought forth for us Christ our life, O Virgin who knows not the nuptial chamber, hope of those who run to you.
O salutary gate, open to me the gates of repentance, as a benign protectress, and deliver me from the gates of sin, keeping me by your divine power.
The Word of God received a body from your womb, O maiden Mother of God, and was seen as an infant, exhibiting to all an admirable generation full of wonder.
He who was most perfect, having been made man from you, O unwedded Virgin, deified the corrupted essence of men.
With unceasing voice we cry to you: Rejoice, O   most undefiled one; for you brought forth Christ, the joy of all, and have driven away all the sorrow of the first mother, Eve.
Behold that legal Ark prefigured your womb, containing Christ, our Manna, our food, O Mother of God, alone chaste, blessed.
You appeared higher than the heavens, when you brought forth the Word of God, who raised us to the heights, whom every spirit greatly exalts as our God, unto the ages.
Illumine with the rays of your light, O Bride of God, my soul, lying in the deep of sloth; arise, and disturb and cast down the enemies, who always vex my heart and drive me to pursue my lusts.
*From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyrs Proclus and Hilarion, day 12*
The poison which the first mother Eve had drunk in by hearing, Gabriel, by hailing you "Rejoice" (Ave), truly cast out, O Lady: for you alone brought forth beyond all thought and speech the destroyer of the malice of the serpent.
Dissolve, O Virgin, the chain of my evils, binding me with the love of the Word who was born from you, O all-pure one; and save me, Lady, by your prayers.
Having compassion on the work of Your hands, broken by the transgression, O Word, You dwelt in a womb that knew no marriage, and You proceeded in two substances, renewing the paths of immortality for those who know You.
Who is able to explain your mystery, O Lady?


[1143] {#pg.105.1143}
A O Mother of God, for you ineffably clothed the Creator of all with flesh.
Behold, the Virgin shall conceive, Isaiah once cried out, the angel of the great counsel, Emmanuel, the God and Lord and Savior of our souls.
As holier than all creatures, O chaste Virgin, you gave birth to the Creator and Lord, O undefiled Virgin, blessed Mother, ever-glorified.
God, who made and fashioned me, having become incarnate from your undefiled blood, O Lady, Mother of God, has reclaimed the world, which cries out thus: Bless and praise the Lord.
You have become the dwelling-place of Light, O chaste and most holy Virgin-Mother, in the visible matter of a body, by whom all who draw life in shadows are illuminated: wherefore we faithfully call you blessed.
From the Canon for the Synaxis, or assembly, of the Archangel Gabriel, day 13
Where Gabriel, etc. (The same is as the Canon for the day of 26 March.)
From the Canon for the feast of St. Golinduch the martyr, day 13
The Creator, wishing to cleanse our nature from the filth of malice, became incarnate from your pure womb, O Mother of God; therefore we all glorify you.
We have clearly seen God incarnate from your chaste blood, O Virgin, and having assumed our form through mercy; wherefore we faithfully glorify you.
You have dissolved the bond of transgression, having given birth to the Giver of good things with an excess of kindness, O Virgin-Mother. Wherefore we the faithful glorify you.
Since my mind is stained and rendered useless by many transgressions, O Mother of God, only undefiled one, I beseech you to pity me and save me by your mediation.
The Most High, having woven for Himself a garment from your pure blood, O undefiled one, adorned those who had been stripped of divine raiment; wherefore we longingly call you blessed.
Having you always as a propitiation before God, O most immaculate one, deliver us from the terrible torments of the life to come, and free us from all threats and the attempts of enemies, both visible and invisible.
You who by your birth-giving rendered the whole malice of the seducer barren, O chaste one, make my heart, which is barren of all good works, fruitful, by rendering God propitious to me.
At the voice of the angel, O chaste one, you conceived the Word of the Father, whom He had prepared as a dwelling-place for Himself; God, the infuser of grace. Consider the birth of the Mother of God, and you will not marvel at a conception without stain. Great are the things that are spoken, but they are true, they are holy, and they are fitting for the Mother of God, whose conception grace preceded, and hence the world marvels. Thus he.


[1145] {#pg.105.1145}
A who willed to become like unto us, whom do thou entreat that we might find mercy and the remission of sins, O most immaculate one; whence we ever glorify thee with grateful voices.
From the Canon for the Holy Apostle Aquila, day 14.
By the Word, O venerable one, thou didst conceive in thy womb the Word who through the Word created all things; therefore do we hymn thee with divine words, O thou full of the grace of God.
The only pure one, the only Lord, as He knew thee alone to be purer than all creation, O most immaculate one, was incarnate from thy chaste blood.
We address thee, O Theotokos and Lady, as a spiritual palace and the most high throne of the King.
Thou art become both Mother and handmaid of Christ, who was incarnate for our sake, whom do thou ever earnestly entreat to save us who call thee the chaste Theotokos.
O immaculate maiden, whose name echoes lordship, who hast brought forth God the giver of good things, save those who hymn thee from manifold temptations at all times.
Adam died of old through the corruption-producing food, O most pure Virgin, but thou, who didst bring forth our Life, hast quickened him; whence, as the cause of good things, we hymn thee and cry out: Blessed art thou, who didst bring forth God in the flesh.
Since truly, O chaste one, thou didst conceive in thy womb God the cause of all causes, who is above every cause, and didst bring forth for our sake Him who appeared as we are, O most immaculate one, do thou entreat Him for those who hymn thee.
The prophet foresaw thee as an illuminating lamp, O Virgin-Mother, bearing the Light sprung from Light, which richly illuminated what was before darkened by the rays of His ineffable divinity, O most immaculate one.
From the Canon for the Holy Martyrs Cyricus and Julitta, day 15.  Death is brought to naught through thee, and the sting of Hades is wiped away, O chaste Mother; for thou didst bring forth the immortal Master who died in the flesh.
Without emptying the Father’s bosom, O undefiled one, the Word who gave essence to all things dwelt in thy most immaculate womb, and appeared as flesh without change, and deified mortals, He who is supersubstantial.   The laws of nature, O all-chaste one, are changed in thy birth-giving which was above nature; for thou didst bring forth the Creator in a way beyond mind and reason.   God, the Word of God, took from thee flesh endowed with mind and soul, O all-holy one, and through compassion became man, and deified me who had been cast away through transgression; Him do thou entreat to save all things.


[1147] {#pg.105.1147}
With the sharp scythe of your intercession, cut away, O Maiden, the wicked thoughts from the roots of my soul, and make me fruitful, I pray; for you have given birth to God the Sower of all, and Savior.
Clinging to your words, all generations call you blessed, O Maiden, having been shown to be the Mother of the blessed God, who makes those who believe in Him blessed.
The Word, incarnate from your most immaculate blood, O immaculate Maiden, deified those who had previously inclined toward the most irrational passions of the flesh, through divine knowledge; therefore we exalt Him above all forever.
Illumine, O gate of light, my soul blinded by affections and darkened and endangered by wicked thoughts; and deliver me from temptations, dangers, and tribulations, that I may glorify you, the hope and fortress of the faithful.
*From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyr Athenogenes, day 16.*
You gave birth to the eternal Word, O unwedded one, having become flesh from your blood, beyond the comprehension of mind or word.
You appeared higher than the heavens, O chaste one, and ever holier than the Seraphim, since you supernaturally gave birth to the King and Lord of all.
You rendered the super-substantial One, equal in power and throne to the Begetter, incarnate, O most immaculate one, He who for compassion dwelt among men.
Recognizing you as Mother and Virgin, we unanimously venerate you as all-holy, and devoutly call you blessed.
As an intelligible ark, you carried the Lawgiver; as a radiant lamp, you brought forth the Light; as an unwatered root, O Theotokos, you sprouted the cluster of life.
The Word, whom you brought forth beyond word, O Mother of God Mary, entreat for us who faithfully praise you and call you blessed, O immaculate one.
Having been delivered through you, O most undefiled one, from the ancient fall of our first parents, we cry to you, "Hail," and with faith glorify Him who through you delivered us from corruption.
You carry in your arms the God who carries all things; you nourish the Nourisher, O chaste one, who became like us; entreat Him to deliver your people from all hardships and adversities.
*From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyr Marina, day 17.*
You have become a capacious vessel of divine grace, O immaculate Mother of God; therefore, Marina, pursuing and desiring you with virginal affection, was led after you to your Son.
Truly and properly, we the faithful venerate you as Theotokos, O most immaculate one; for you have given birth to God, who has become flesh. The most immaculate and only holy...


[1149] {#pg.105.1149}
one, who appeared holier than the Cherubim, save our souls from every surrounding adversity,   as we praise you with faith, O immaculate Virgin, Bride of God.
The Creator, who surrounds the sea with cloud as if with a swaddling cloth, by His own will is born as an infant from the virgin maiden who has not known man, and is wrapped in swaddling clothes in an ineffable manner.
O unique Virgin, because the pure Word loved you as pure and incorrupt, He became incarnate from you and refashioned man, He who glorified Marina with miracles.   You appeared higher than the heavens, having given birth to the heavenly God, O most chaste one, who has made the whole mass of earth-born creatures heavenly, and has brightened the revered memory of Marina; to whom we cry out: "All you works, praise the Lord."
You have caused light to rise for us from your inviolate womb, O Virgin, who, being illuminated by divine splendors, became light, O Mother of God, Virgin Mother, whose name resonates with joy.
From the Canon for the feast of Saint Emilian the martyr, on the 18th.
My strength, and my praise, and the illumination of my heart is Christ the Lord,   whom you gave birth to, O most immaculate one, who is understood in two substances, but in one hypostasis.
Ignoring the laws of nature in your childbirth, which was above nature, O Virgin Mother, you remained a Virgin after birth; for you gave birth to the Creator of all creation, O inviolate one.
We glorify you, O all-holy maiden, as the only one found to be the place of the Sanctification that sanctifies us, through whom those inhabiting the earth were made heavenly, and were rendered worthy of true life.
Heal me, who am wounded by the sword of sin, with your most effective medicine, you who gave birth to the Savior Christ, who was wounded by a lance for my sake,   and himself wounded the heart of the serpent.
Eve indeed plucked the fruit of the death-bearing tree; but you, O most chaste one, brought forth the tree of life, the taste of which brought to life all who were dead.
O Bride of God, adorned with a name of lordship, to you we cry out "Rejoice" with faith; for you gave birth to Christ the Lord, the ineffable joy, to whom we cry out: "Blessed are You, the God of our fathers."
Rain down upon me a drop of mercy, you who gave birth to the fountain of mercy, and dry up the showers of my sin, and calm the wild waves of my soul, O Virgin Theotokos Mary, that I may glorify you unto all ages.
Illuminate me with your light, O most worthy of all praise, as I walk in darkness; reach out your hand of help to me; the


[1151] {#pg.105.1151}
clouds of my soul dispel; the tempest of my passions calm, O refuge of those in despair.   From the Canon for the feast of our holy Father Dius, on the 19th.
You have become a tabernacle of the spiritual Sun, O most pure one, who has illuminated us with the divine splendors of piety and dispersed the mist of ignorance, O ever-Virgin.   He who dwells in the heavens has dwelt within you, O immaculate one; whom earnestly entreat to save the souls of those who praise you.
We have known you to be a light-bearing lampstand, carrying the divine radiance in your womb, O Virgin: wherefore we suppliants pray you, that with your light you may illuminate the souls of all who praise you.
Mortify the passions of my soul, O most praiseworthy one, you who brought forth the Life of all by an ineffable Word; and calm my troubled mind, O Maiden.
God the holy one has manifestly made you holier than the Cherubim, O Maiden, sanctifying those who cry out: Blessed are you among women, O most immaculate Lady.
You have appeared more spacious than the heavens, having contained God, O Mary most chaste; whom entreat to deliver me from the passions that hold me fast, and to rescue me from the future fearful judgment, as I cry aloud: All you works, praise the Lord.
Spare me, O Christ, when you come to judge the world with glory, having to entreat you, O Word, the Theotokos ever-Virgin, the orders of angels, and the assembly of the saints.   From the Canon for the feast of the holy Prophet Elias, on the 20th.
The supersubstantial God, O most clean one, has become incarnate from you, and for our sake appeared as man like unto us: whom earnestly entreat, O most chaste one, that I, who have sinned above all men, may be saved and delivered from torment.   O impervious gate, through whom one passes to God, open to me the gates of repentance, I pray, washing away the filth of my sins with the showers of your mercy, O maiden most dear to God.
With all the heavenly hosts, with all the prophets and martyrs, with the apostles and confessors, pour forth your prayers, O most clean Lady, that I, who have sinned much, may attain salvation and be snatched from future punishments.
Upon you, as rain, the supersubstantial Word has descended; whom entreat, O most innocent maiden, that He may now rain down upon me pure drops of compunction, by which all the filth of my measureless evils may be washed away.
O gate of God, show divine entrances to my miserable soul, by which I may enter with confession, and receive the absolution of my evils, O Theotokos.
I praise you, O most praiseworthy one, and I magnify you, O maid beloved of God,


[1153] {#pg.105.1153}
your pure childbearing; assist me, who am tossed about by the waves of life, and grant compunction to my humble soul, as a cleanser of its defilements.
The Legislator of piety and Master of repentance, Emmanuel, appeared having been born of you, whom now entreat, O all-holy Lady, to open for me the gates of righteousness from above, and to save me as I cry out: "Priests, bless the Lord."
Do not disregard the voices of your servants, as you are good, O most blameless Lady, but earnestly ask the Creator of all for the king to grant him victories, and for strength of soul, O Virgin, and for the participation and splendor of the divine kingdom.
149 Ex Canone in S. Focam martyrem, die 23 (65).
The punishment of our first parents was dissolved: for you brought forth God, who is before the ages, O undefiled one; who, having become a new infant, hath completely renewed the whole of human substance.
God, having been incarnate of you, because of the bowels of His mercy, was united to men, and took away the curse, O Lady alone heaped with every blessing.
Virgin immune from nuptials, Virgin blessed, glory of bishops, crown of all martyrs, free those who sing your praises from perils and tribulations.
The Wisdom of God built for Himself a house, as it was pleasing to Him, from your pure and holy blood, O Lady.
As a saving rain, the Word was poured forth   in your incorrupt womb, O most holy girl, and by His divine power dried up the torrents of malice.
Restore the shattered and ruined house of my soul, you, as most benign, by acts of repentance, O most chaste girl, who didst reform the whole nature of men by your childbirth.
The Ark of the Law, and the urn that contained the manna, prefigured you, O most chaste one; the divine table, and the lamp shining with gold, which brought forth that Light for the revelation of the Gentiles, which illuminated the whole world with divine knowledge.
Illumine, O pure one, my soul, wrapped in the darkness of sin, and free me from the flames and eternal darkness by your mediation, that with exultation of soul I may celebrate your greatness.
150 Ex Canone in festo S. Christine martyris, die 24.
You conceived the Word of the Father united to flesh according to the hypostasis that was from you; which, as she ardently loved, Christina obtained the glory of martyrdom.
Calm, O chaste Lady, the tumult of my thoughts, take away all consternation of soul, you who gave birth to Christ.
The most glorious of the prophets, Isaiah, once named you a rod, bringing forth the flower, the Lord, O Theotokos, mother and ever-virgin.
Enliven me who have become dead through sin, O chaste Virgin, having given birth to the immortal life.
The divine-speaking prophets,   perceiving the depth of your mystery, O Virgin, prophetically foretold it when illuminated from afar by the divine Spirit, that you would truly be the mother of the Lord of all.
Having transcended   the laws of nature, O Virgin, by your divine conception, you gave birth to God above the order of nature, crying: "Blessed are You, Lord God, unto the ages."

[1155] {#pg.105.1155}
are the unerring guide of those who trust in you and cry out unceasingly: "People, exalt the Lord above all."
O Virgin who loves the good, make my soul, corrupted by sins, good, and deliver me from the eternal flame by your intercessions.
From the Canon to the holy martyr Hermolaus and his companions, on the 27th day.
O most pure one, who brought forth the divine and immaculate light into the world, dispel the darkness that is in me, dissipate the clouds of my heart; illuminate me, O gate of light, who with faith magnify you and glorify God; for He has been gloriously glorified.
He who is understood as possessing a twofold nature, God and man, while in no way abandoning the Paternal bosom, sat in your bosom, O inviolate Virgin, circumscribed, while being uncircumscribed by His own nature.

Deliver me, O most immaculate one, from the grievous tempest of sins and of thoughts which cruelly invade my heart.
Like a fire-bearing throne, you carry the Master, O one most filled with divine grace; whom you should entreat to keep us safe when we are in danger in the sea of sin.
Having you, O Virgin, as a protection, a refuge, and a firm defense, may we through you be delivered from every tribulation.
The tempest of my boundless transgressions disturbs me and continually casts me into the abyss of despair, O Maiden; but anticipating this, reach out your hand to me and grant that I may enter secure into the calm harbors of repentance.
O all-holy Virgin, who gave birth to God in the flesh, save your people who cry out to you from every sin and tribulation: "Blessed are You, O God of our fathers."
O most pure one, who brought forth the divine and immaculate light, dispel the darkness that is in me, and dissipate the clouds of my heart. Illuminate me, O gate of light, for I praise you with faith, and glorify God; for He has been gloriously glorified.
Those who are troubled by the most wicked demons, who disturb me with vexation, deliver me from the fire of Gehenna, O you whom I praise with faith.
Just as the fire of the furnace did not once burn the most prudent youths, so the fire of Divinity did not now burn your womb, O Virgin Mother of God, which renewed the bounds of nature within you.
The Lord Almighty, having inhabited your womb, saved those who were afflicted with disease, bowed down to the earth, and openly serving sin; whence they now cry out to Him with firm faith: "O children, etc."
You have restored the corrupted substance of earth-born men by your incorruptible birth-giving. Wherefore I cry aloud: Restore me, who am entirely corrupted by wicked desires, as you are the most benign, and show me the paths that lead to life; for you are the guide of all who have recourse to you, O most pure one.


[1157] {#pg.105.1157}
We praise you, O most holy Lady, as the delightful palace and bright dwelling-place of the King of all, beseeching you to show us to be temples of your Son, cleansed of all opposing wickedness, and crying out unceasingly: "O peoples, exalt Christ unto the ages."
Spare me, O Savior, who were born and kept your Mother uncorrupt after the birth, when you shall sit to judge the universe; do not look upon my iniquities and my sins, as you are sinless and merciful, as God and lover of mankind.
From the Canon for the feast of the holy apostles Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, and Parmenas, day 28.
The ways of God made manifest in you have become known, O most immaculate one, through your wondrous birth-giving and incomparable union; whence we glorify you as the Lady of all creation.
You have brought forth the good Lord, who distills sweetness and redemption from evils, O inviolate Virgin, lacking every stain.
Without the union of a man you gave birth to God the Word, made flesh, O most chaste one, beyond mind and word; whence we duly glorify you, O Virgin, and as is our duty, we call you blessed.
We praise you, through whom we were redeemed from corruption, O most immaculate one, from the abyss, and from the wickedness of the avenging foe that formerly tyrannized us.

It also retains the same proportion to its parts as a successive whole, such as life is, compared to all the successes and steps of its course, which a permanent whole has to its parts. Moreover, if a positive and limited name, once applied to a part, extends itself to denominate the whole; how much more will a negative name, such as "Immaculate," being more universal and as it were not knowing how to be restricted, when attributed to one whole, spread out to denominate the part? Therefore, the rationale of "immaculate," which is attributed to the Virgin and the entire course of her life, will be able to denominate the conception as immaculate, as being the principal part initiating such a successive whole of this kind. So Nierembergius.

[1175] {#pg.105.1175}
of an innocent man, Adam, and lost her innocence, finding for us original sin: but Mary, from the mass of perdition, being conceived without perdition, lost original sin, first found innocence, and brought forth immaculate Him who washes away the sins of all, [having been rendered] immaculate. He says this.
Sanctius also, of the Order of Preachers, in his 13th Marian sermon, speaking of this innocence of the Virgin, said: "Eve had two names: the first, in the state of innocence, 'virago' (woman); the second, in the state of fallen nature, 'Eva'. But from the word 'virago', remove 'A', namely Adam, who lost that state, and there remains 'virgo' (virgin), to signify that the state of innocence, lost through Adam, is recovered and brought back through a Virgin."
Hence, Father Hortensius Pallavicinus of the Society of Jesus, in his *Elogia*, part 1, elogium 4, speaking of the immaculate conception of Mary, says among other things: "It would be a monster if the progenitor of the Blessed Virgin were not innocent, she who alone is conceived under the horoscope of innocence. Eve, the guilty one, first conceived sin: Eve, the innocent one, is first conceived without sin."
But concerning this same innocence of the Virgin, Peter Pázmány, Cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, speaks most excellently in his sermon on the immaculate conception of the Blessed Virgin, when he says: "It can be said with all the greater assertion that the most blessed Mother of God was not only innocent of every original stain, by which original sin is worse and more destructive than all the venial sins of the whole world   (that itself is the fountain and root of actual sins), but—arguing from this point also, Augustine against Julian, ch. 9, near the end, proves that Christ never sinned, because He was not infected with the original stain, and adds: 'Assuredly, He would have committed a greater sin, had He possessed one as an infant.'—so he says. Who also adds below: 'It is a great axiom of the tribunal that if a question arises concerning anyone, whether he be guilty or innocent, he ought to be considered innocent, until it can be demonstrated by undoubted proofs and light clearer than the day that he is guilty.' See Aristotle, *Probl.* 29, p. 13: 'We would rather free a guilty man than condemn an innocent one.' Therefore, since it cannot be shown by certain and light-clear proofs that the most blessed Virgin is guilty   of the original blight, nay rather, it is lawful by the Church to defend her without any error, we are bound not to deny it to her. Moreover, on the day of judgment it would not seem less unbecoming to complete in this the divine omnipotence and mercy, nor glorious to Judge Christ, who will then take an account from men of the divine precepts, if He had not so honored His Mother that the least of the angels of heaven would appear more innocent than she on that day, whereas they will appear throughout their whole eternity most innocent without any fault, yet their Queen, and the Mother of the most holy and omnipotent, had at one time been with a stain. Clearly, it does not seem less becoming that Christ should have cared less about the honor of His Mother and the manifestation of His own all-encompassing purity and mercy, both by withholding from His Mother a lesser prerogative, which the angels could say, upon the proclamation of that day, that they were more innocent than their own Queen, as well as by exalting His mercy, which was not lacking in the most excellent mode of redemption even preserving her from original sin. For, as Antonius Navarrus of the Dominican family says in a sermon on the conception of the Blessed Virgin: 'If God made the angels most pure spirits, why would He not make their Queen purer? Because she is as alien to every contamination in body as in soul. Saint Anastasius Sinaita favors this when, in Book 1 of his *Hexaemeron*, he calls the Mother of God: "The full moon, which never waned nor failed, nor was deprived of essential light, namely her virginity." For the essential light explaining virginity does not speak of the virginity of the body alone, for this cannot be called the essential light of grace and sanctity, for its lack can be combined with exceeding sanctity from the light of grace, as happened to Saint Anne; but it speaks of integral virginity or the purity of the virgin, namely of body and soul, whose purity the Fathers also called integrity and virginity. Therefore, the most sacred Virgin did not suffer a waning or defect in her integrity, either of body or of soul, which, although created in sanctity, was never bereft of the essential light of grace in the soul, nor of the superadded splendor of incorruption in the body, namely, all-encompassing virginity and purity. Saint Augustine and other Fathers said that the Virgin conceived the Word in her mind before her flesh, denoting her faith and will required for the assumption of humanity into her womb. And so the virtue of the soul was required for the divine conception. Wherefore it was fitting that the soul of Mary should have been no less pure, and integral, and a virgin from every contamination of fault, than her flesh pure and incorrupt. And lest anyone should understand Saint Anastasius himself to speak only of the perpetual virginity of the body, Saint Anastasius himself explains this, adding: "Mary remains a virgin as regards the soul": but perpetual virginity as regards the soul is perpetual integrity as regards sin, whether actual or original. See Nieremberg in *Exceptionibus*, ch. 13.
Blessed Albert the Great, ch. 181, on the *Missus est*, defining the most proper essence of virginity, says thus: "Virginity is a withdrawal from every evil, comprising as much the evil of the soul as of the body." And indeed, a greater account was taken by God of spiritual purity than of corporal integrity, because, as Augustine taught, Book x, *De mendacio ad Consent.*, ch. 20: "Whatever can be violated in the body is less than whatever can be violated in the soul."

(72) By the title “immaculate,” original sin is excluded even more than venial sin, by the force and signification of the epithet: for a venial stain is not so notorious that it strives to demolish the spiritual beauty of the soul, and thus it does not have as great a repugnance with the word of praise, “immaculate.” Moreover, original sin, since it utterly expels every ornament of grace, can in no way consist with the beauty of “immaculate.” Therefore, the signification of this word “immaculate” is more verified by the expulsion of original sin than by the expulsion of venial sin, according to the opinion of the Angelic Doctor, 1. 2, q. 8, a. 1, saying: “Properly speaking, venial sin does not cause a stain in the soul.”
(73) When the Blessed Virgin was blessed, she was such also in her creation, and consequently she avoided the curse of original sin at that time. The Church favors this in the Responsorium of the feast of the Circumcision, when it says: “And blessed forever, she brought forth to us God and man.” As if the Church were to say: Because the Blessed Virgin brought forth to us God and man, she was blessed forever. But what is “blessed forever,” if not always blessed, that is, from the beginning of her creation and thereafter? For eternity looks to every difference of time, and excludes no moment of time, but comprehends every part entirely and totally. Therefore, Mary was always blessed, and in every difference of time; she could not, therefore, incur original sin, the grace of blessing, which went before her, standing in the way.

For in the Old Testament, Christ and the most blessed Virgin did not exist, who are truly, and properly, and entirely, and antonomastically immaculate. But indeed, since such persons did not exist in the Old Testament, it is no wonder if the name "immaculate" were attributed to the holier ones, especially since it is not attributed to them absolutely. Thus, when it is said: "Blessed are the immaculate," it is added, "in the way," that is, in the mode of operating, not absolutely and entirely. David also said, "I will be immaculate," [which] indicates that at some time he was not such. Job also, who had acknowledged and supposed himself to have been conceived in sin, afterwards called himself immaculate regarding the present, not the past, just as others are signified as immaculate regarding the future in Scripture. However, the mode by which Josephus and other Fathers call the Virgin immaculate, absolutely and antonomastically, is not found elsewhere among other saints; and it indicates something most special and greater than all the sons of Adam, as Nierembergius observes in his *Epistolary Dissertations*, epistle 8.

A       Dei Genitricem, or Mother of God, they add almost always the title "immaculate." Thus the sixth general synod held at Constantinople under Pope Agatho, in action 5: "We confess our Lord Jesus Christ to be incarnate of the Holy Spirit, from our immaculate Lady, the Mother of God." Thus the Council of Trent, sess. vi, Can. 4: "The holy synod declares that it is not its intention to include in this decree, where it treats of original sin, the immaculate Virgin Mary, Mother of God." St. James in his Liturgy, which is found in the *Bibliotheca Veterum Patrum*: "Commemorating our most holy immaculate Lady, the Mother of God." Thus Origen, homil. 1: "Mother of God, immaculate." And the Fathers, both Greek and Latin, everywhere call the Mother of God not only immaculate, but often plainly, fully, entirely, and altogether immaculate, or most immaculate. Whence I conclude the privilege of immunity from original sin in the Blessed Virgin from her divine maternity, as follows: "The word 'immaculate' (as an anonymous author says in a certain suppliant booklet offered to the sacred Congregation of the Inquisition) expresses holiness through a negative term, that is, through the negation of any stain whatsoever; therefore it seems to exclude a stain for any instant. Therefore this word 'immaculate,' without any other restrictive addition, attributed to the Mother of God, signifies entirely that she was, absolutely and simply, and thus throughout her whole life, and consequently in the first instant of her conception, devoid of every stain. For just as a woman would in no way be called a 'virgin' absolutely who, although she might be chaste for a time, had nevertheless at some point fallen from the flower of virginity; so the Mother of God, or theotokos, could not be called immaculate absolutely and by antonomasia, however much she might have shone thereafter, if at any time she had been subject to an original stain, since the word 'immaculate' denotes the negation of any contracted stain whatsoever, specifically. But if you object that the argument is weak which is drawn from this word 'immaculate' for the Mother of God's immunity from original sin, since in Scripture those are often called 'immaculate' who are subject to an original stain (see Psalm 36: 'The Lord knows the days of the immaculate'; and Psalm 18: 'Then I shall be immaculate, and I shall be cleansed from the greatest transgression'; and Psalm 17: 'And I shall be immaculate with him,' and elsewhere; answer with Velasquez, *De Maria concepta*, book iv, Dissert. 3, single annotation: 'Names and epithets are to be understood according to the persons to whom they are given, and Christ is called "immaculate" in one way, as in Heb. ix: "He offered himself immaculate to the living God"; and 1 Pet. i: 'With the precious blood as of an immaculate Lamb, Christ"; but the Blessed Virgin is called "immaculate" in another way, and other humans are called "immaculate"]. For as Christ the Lord, subsisting in a divine person, is immaculate by his nature, so it is fitting for the Blessed Virgin to be immaculate in that way which becomes the Mother of God, and consequently to be immaculate in every respect, according to the proper signification of the word, through the negation of any stain whatsoever for any instant. Which indeed, as it does not befit other men when we call them 'immaculate,' we do not mean to signify that, but that they possess such purity as is possible for human nature (subject to original sin). From which it seems to me I can infer that in the view of the councils and the Fathers, the Mother of God is called 'immaculate' in the sense that she is entirely beautiful and without any actual or original stain, and that nothing else rings in the ears of all the faithful than that it is the Mother of God who was immaculate, just as her very conception was immaculate. For from the fact that we can—as we ought—say with "full cheeks" that the Mother of God is immaculate, it is clearly deduced, according to the doctrine of the anonymous doctor, that the conception of the Mother of God herself is to be honored with the same title. For, with the anonymous author being the assertor in the cited suppliant booklet, the word 'immaculate' expresses holiness through a negative term, that is, through the negation of any stain whatsoever, and therefore excludes a stain for any instant. Therefore, if the Mother of God is immaculate, any stain whatever is to be denied to her, for any instant whatever. Therefore, original stain, even for the first instant of life. Otherwise, if at that instant she is not called 'immaculate'... this word (in the judgment of the anonymous author) excludes both any stain whatsoever and for any instant whatsoever. Whence by contradiction, as I think,

You were shown to be the Rising of the Sun of justice, O most immaculate one; Him, beseech for the salvation of those who sincerely glorify you.
Sanctify my mind and enlighten my heart, O holy Mother of God, and deliver me from the straits that overwhelm me, that I may glorify you, O Theotokos, ever-Virgin.
Him who was incarnate of you, beyond mind and speech, O full of divine grace, beseech for the salvation of those who honor you with affection, and who shout in unison: Blessed are You, O God of our fathers.
As you are higher than all creatures, O Maiden most pleasing to God, and immune from every stain, make my mind   higher than the scandals of the deceiver, O most immaculate one.
With the voice of Gabriel, we cry out to you with rejoicing mind: Hail, joy of the faithful; hail, golden lampstand and table; mountain and intellectual gate; hail, divine


[1203] {#pg.105.1203}
A vehicle of Christ the King; hail, dissolution of the curse, O you who are blessed in all things.
From the Canon for Saint Epicaris, the 27th day
Behold, the laws of nature are renewed in you, O you who are immune from all stain; for you gave birth to God and man above the laws of nature and reason, whom the young girls have fervently loved with desire.
You remained supernaturally a virgin after birth, O most dear to God; and wounded by love for you, this virgin and martyr struggled eagerly, and after you, O chaste one, she was led to her Spouse, leading the dance together with the faithful virgins.
The substantial Word of the Father, without any change in Himself, was incarnate from you, O Virgin, with whose love the soul of Epicharis was kindled and made worthy of the celestial bridal chambers.
You embrace, O Mother of God, filled with divine grace alone, within your maternal arms, Him who embraces and contains all things.
Perceiving the most sweet fragrance of the Son incarnate from you, the most illustrious maiden, after you, O inviolate one, was led to Him with exultation of soul.
You have imparted new laws to nature, O Virgin, when you gave birth above the order of nature; for He who was incarnate from you in an ineffable manner was God and man.
O chaste Virgin, you remained after childbirth a matter of venerable wonder, O inviolate one: for you gave birth to the Word of God, whom the virgin Epicharis, confessing in the midst of wicked tyrants, proclaimed: Blessed is God, etc.
With the most sacred voices, the most sacred prophets manifestly foretold you as the Mother of God, O chaste and inviolate one: whom we superexalt above all, as the ruler of all, through all ages.
Light-bearing cloud, you who gave birth to the divine light, dispel the clouds of my miserable soul, O Mother of God, and illumine me with the light of salvation, you who alone are good; that I may unceasingly magnify you with faith and affection.
From the Canon for the feast of Saint Gregory of Great Armenia, and the Holy Martyrs Ripsimia, Gaiana, and their companions, the 30th day
Women, strengthened by the cross of Him who was incarnate from you, O chaste one, struggled steadfastly, and were led to Him after you, O Virgin: and they shine with the splendors of virginity and the blood of martyrs.
Ripsimia the martyr, knowing you alone to be the Virgin Mother, was charmed by your beauty, and was led after you to Christ, gleaming with her contests.
As one beautiful, as one chosen, as one fair, the young maidens loved you, who struggled with Ripsimia, O Virgin-Mother Mary, and after you they were led to your Son, rejoicing.
Sensing the fragrance of the ointment of the Word that shone forth from you, O chaste Virgin, they were pleasing to Him through athletic contests, rejoicing.
As soon as Ripsimia learned that He who was incarnate from you, O Mother of God, had been crucified, she was at the same time crucified with Him, as a lamb with the shepherd, as an immaculate victim of God.
Adorned with the crowns of martyrdom, the maidens were led to God, who blossomed from a Virgin, melodiously crying out: Blessed are You, O God, etc.   Not fearing the multitude of torments, and not yielding to the pleasures of the flesh, Ripsimia confessed the Lord born of a Virgin, crying out: Bless and praise the Lord.
Illumined by the light of the countenance that shone forth from you, O perpetual Virgin, Ripsimia with affection endured His sufferings, and expressed His death in her own flesh; whence she now exults with Him.
MONTH OF OCTOBER
From the Canon for the feast of Saint Charitina the Martyr, the 5th day
You have become a vessel capable of the divine nature, O Mother of God,


[1205] {#pg.105.1205}
A undefiled; wherefore Charitina, having longed with virginal love to follow you, has been brought to your Son.
Thee alone, blessed among women, O chaste one, the martyr Charitina, loving, has been glorified by your good graces.
You gave birth to the Word of God made flesh, O undefiled Mother of God, whom Charitina, loving most fervently, overcame by her struggle against fire and multiform tortures.
Human thought is unable to conceive your conception, which is beyond understanding, O Mother and Virgin; for you gave birth to God.
Finding you to be her strength and support, O Virgin, Charitina endured scourging with constancy, and joyfully she is led behind you to the Lord of all.   O unique Virgin, the pure Word loved you, pure and incorrupt, and in you He fashioned the whole man in becoming incarnate, having glorified Charitina through your miracles.
You appeared higher than the heavens, having given birth to the heavenly God, O most pure one, who made heavenly the whole lump of earth-born men, and who adorned the venerable memory of Charitina, to whom we cry: All you works of the Lord, bless the Lord.
A light has risen for us from your womb that knew no man, O Virgin, by whose rays the one named for joy was immediately illuminated, O Mother of God who knew not marriage.
From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyrs Eulampius and Eulampia, the 10th day   We, redeemed from the condemnation of our first parents by your birth, O undefiled Virgin, clearly and with voices of songs, we the faithful always call you blessed as the Mother of God.
Entreat, O most chaste Mother of God, that those who always honor you may be delivered from every evil invasion of enemies, from soul-destroying passions, and from grievous and troublesome dangers.
Habakkuk, having perceived you from afar most expressively, O chaste one, called you a mountain overshadowed by virtues, from which appeared to us He who illuminates our souls.
All the swords of the enemy have truly failed in the end, O   undefiled, all-pure, chaste one; for you gave birth to the God of all, who by His cross cast down the pride of that enemy.
As rain, God has been poured out into your womb, because of His ineffable compassion, and He has watered all with a torrent of delights, O Lady, and has renewed the corrupted creation.
The furnace did not burn the three youths, prefiguring your birth; for the divine fire, not burning you, dwelt within you, and illuminated all who cry out: Blessed are You, the God of our fathers.
O Maid who knew not marriage, hail, all-pure, the harbor of those in a storm; hail, Bride of God, the [refuge/aid] of sinners.


[1207] {#pg.105.1207}
A Hail, propitiatory for sinners; hail, you who bore God incarnate. O receptacle of light, which from you, O Pure One, worthily shone forth, enlighten the eyes of my soul, O most immaculate one, and banish the darkness of ignorance, and cast down and utterly destroy the mists of sin.
*From the Canon for the feast of the holy Apostle Philip, one of the seven Deacons, day 11.*
He who created all things from that which was not, had you, O inviolate Mother of God, as the cause of His incarnation; therefore the faithful, as is due, call you blessed. You became a mystical candlestick, O Maiden, truly carrying that lamp which, by its supreme goodness, illuminated those previously held in the night of ignorance. Your Son, O most immaculate one, made those who were sons of men to be sons of God, being incarnate from your pure blood and born of you; therefore we glorify you. We who truly confess you as Theotokos are delivered from temptations and most difficult affairs by your intercessions before the God and Lord of all, O Virgin, most full of divine grace.
Beyond the laws of nature, your holy Mother bore you, Christ, the Creator of nature, and beyond nature she truly remained a virgin inviolate, O One superior to all goodness. We name you a Virgin-Mother, O Mary, Bride of God, we who through you, day and night, are delivered from the harmful violence of enemies, from all kinds of temptations, and from the defilements of the soul. Make my soul, shaken by the wickedness of the enemy, firm and stable, O chaste Virgin, you who received without disturbance Him who by His divine gaze shakes the universe. Every living thing sends forth towards you a grateful voice, crying out with joy and saying: Hail, fire-formed throne of the Most High; hail, most spacious region of God; hail, O chaste and most beautiful crown of the apostles.
*From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyrs Probus, Tarachus, and Andronicus, day 12.*
The Word, co-eternal with the Father and the holy Spirit, willingly inhabited a virginal womb and became flesh without change; and having suffered voluntarily, He prepared the divine hosts of martyrs to contend with faith. As beautiful, as fair, as elect, having chosen you, O inviolate one, the Word who gave existence to all things, desiring your undefiled and God-containing womb, dwelt within it, He who is above all substance. You alone bear in the womb God incarnate, who gave being to all things, whom confessionally and unshakably the divine martyrs contended [to proclaim] in the stadium, O Virgin Theotokos, the wonder of angels and the wound of demons, most worthy of all praise. You have become superior to the powers above, O Virgin, [as] the Word


[1209] {#pg.105.1209}
A brought forth from the Father, O Virgin, co-eternal with the same Father and likewise without beginning; by whose splendors the athletes, being illuminated, fled beyond the night of godlessness.
You conceived in your womb Him who is before the ages, O immaculate one; and you brought forth in the flesh Him who is by nature inaccessible; and you fed with milk Him who nourishes all things, O Mother of God, who have known not a man.
The most complete Word is emptied in your womb, not departing from the Father’s bosom, and flesh is seen, and an infant is born, to whom we sing joyfully, O Virgin: Blessed be the God of our fathers.
With the ranks of the incorporeal ones, with the armies of martyrs, with the apostles and   prophets, let us all religiously and piously praise the Lady of all created things, as being holier than the Cherubim, and the only most chaste Mother of God, exalting Christ unto all ages.
Spare me, Savior, who were born and kept the one who bore you incorrupt after childbirth, when you sit to judge my works, overlooking my iniquities and my sins, as the sinless One, merciful God and lover of mankind.
From the Canon to the holy martyrs Carpus and Papylus, on the 13th day.
O gate of light, which from your incorruptible entrails shone forth, shed upon me the illuminating rays of repentance, and dissipate the darkness of my sins, O most divine and full of grace.
We have known, O Lord, that while you were God without beginning, you sustained having a beginning, and to proceed from the Virgin without mutation, whom you also preserved incorrupt and pure after childbirth.
The incontaminate bridal chamber of God, the mountain untouched by the hands of the stone-cutter, the holy ark and the table, and the censer   of the immaterial coal, we all the faithful proclaim you to be, O chaste Virgin, totally immaculate.
Having you as a saving harbor, O Virgin, we who are constantly tossed on the sea of the direst evils, flee to you, and hoping in you, we do not fear the evil counsels of our enemies.
You conceived without experience of marital union, and brought forth beyond the manner of nature the incomprehensible God, the Creator of nature. O great mystery! O unintelligible miracle, O Virgin alone without any stain.

The sacred chorus of the divine prophets proclaims you, O most pure one, to be the future Mother of God, to whom we all cry: Bless the Lord, all things, etc.
You carry in your arms,   O most chaste one, like a Cherubic throne, Him who carries all, who for our sake was clothed in our flesh, and though He was simple, he appeared dual; whom do you always entreat for us who praise you.
From the Canon for the feast of the holy martyrs Nazarius, Gervasius, Protasius, and Celsus, on the 14th day.
Let us praise the most immaculate maiden, who alone in her womb comprehended the Lord who is before the ages: for she was made wider than the heavens, clothing God with a body for the sake of His own goodness.
The legal tabernacle prefigured you as being the future holy tabernacle of God, O chaste one, in which our propitiation would come, which grants sanctification to us all.
Not leaving empty the Paternal bosom, He


[1211] {#pg.105.1211}
sat down in your most pure bosom, preparing a divine throne for all by His goodness, and glory that abides forever.
The sword which formerly guarded Eden is turned away from the faithful who are signed with the precious blood, which was once poured out from the side wounded by the lance, of Him who rose from you, O chaste one.
You innovated the laws of nature, O maiden Virgin, having brought forth God immortal, clothed in mortal flesh, that He might deify mortals by His goodness.
God, finding your womb a most luminous palace, dwelt within it, O most immaculate one, making those who cry out "Blessed are you, O God and Lord of our fathers," to be sons of light.
United to you in flesh according to substance, He who grants existence to all things reformed me entirely, and entirely renewed me who had grown old through transgressions; therefore we, the Virgin, praise you, O most chaste one, and superexalt you unto all ages.
The voice of the divine Gabriel we bring to you, O most chaste Maiden, rejoicing: Hail, full of grace, boast of martyrs and apostles, and salvation of all the faithful, Virgin Mother who knew not wedlock.

The Word of God was conceived in your womb by the Word,   wishing by His goodness to free mortals from irrationality, O Virgin Mother, immaculate, blessed, all-blameless.
Heal my soul, laboring with the malady of the passions that assail it, O Mother of God, most chaste, and guide it toward salvation.
You brought forth beyond speech the Word, united according to hypostasis in your womb, and having become man, O immaculate one, showing Him to be twofold in wills and in energies.
Let us praise the Theotokos, who alone conceived God without the work of a man, we who have been saved through her, and let us bless her with affection.
Dry up and root out, O most immaculate one, the thorny follies of my heart, and show it to be fruitful through your mediation, O most immaculate Maiden.
As in a pure vessel the pure Word dwelt within you, O Maiden, willing through you to cleanse the pollutions of men.


[1213] {#pg.105.1213}
For blessed is the fruit of your womb.
With mouth, and tongue, and soul I proclaim you, O God-bearer, and I entreat you, O immaculate one, enlighten my heart with your illumination, and deliver me from terrible darkness, while I cry out: All you works of the Lord, praise the Lord.   You have appeared as the dwelling-place of the unsetting light, O Theotokos, through whom those who dwelt in darkness and in the shadow of death have seen the light: therefore illuminate the senses of my heart.
From the Canon for the feast of Saint Andrew of Crete the martyr, on the 17th day.
Always burdened by the sleep of negligence, I run to your protection, O immaculate Virgin Mother; rouse me to the vigilance of repentance, delivering me from the everlasting punishment that follows.
In the likeness of flesh you gave birth to the God-Word who is consubstantial with the Father, O all-blameless one, in a way surpassing reason, remaining a virgin after childbirth; therefore we call you blessed in faith. You carry, O immaculate one, in your arms the one in an ineffable conception embracing those cast down by malice, and miserably enslaved to the deceiver, O all-praiseworthy Maiden; hence we glorify you as Theotokos.   (90) Immaculate does not mean lacking the stain of original sin if she had contracted it. So, that this eulogy of the Blessed Virgin might be true, we must, following the mind of Joseph, free the Blessed Virgin herself from the stain of original sin.


[1215] {#pg.105.1215}
The prophet of old foresaw thee as an intellectual lampstand, O chaste one, bearing the divine torch, Christ, by whom we all have been illuminated. Thou didst become a temple of the living God, in whom He who inhabits the heavens—having deigned in His great goodness to become man—ineffably made His dwelling, O Virgin worthy of all praise. Thou didst appear, O Virgin, to be wider than the heavens, containing in thy womb the God whom nothing can contain; entreat Him, O inviolate Lady, to deliver from lethal distress those who religiously praise and hymn thee. Thy womb became a dwelling-place of Light, which illuminated the world with the splendors of divinity and utterly banished the darkness of ignorance from the world; wherefore we glorify thee, O Maiden, who art free from all stain.
From the Canon for the feast of St. Varus the martyr, Day 19.
The supersubstantial Word dwelt in thy womb beyond the capacity of words, O immaculate one; and being born in a manner befitting God, He drew to Himself choirs of martyrs, with whom we sing hymns to thee. O Virgin Mother of God, I beseech thee, dispel the deepest darkness of my sloth and the clouds of my passions by the illumination of thy grace. Bring me up, O Lady, from the mud of passions and from the misery of thoughts that alienate me from God, who alone is pure, so that in faith I may call thee blessed. Having appeared truly holier than the Cherubim and Seraphim, O most immaculate one, sanctify all who now faithfully call thee blessed, and save those who celebrate thee with praises. Guide, O Lady, my miserable soul, which is always tossed about in the sea of most grievous evils, and bring it to a serene and tranquil harbor, while with a firm mind it calls thee blessed. Restore me, O Virgin, broken and contrite as I am from immeasurable transgressions, through thy mediation, applying a remedy to my soul and granting me speech to cry out: Blessed art thou, who gave birth in the flesh to God. I join sins to sins, and I do not tremble at the future formidable mystery; take away, O chaste one, the hardness of my soul, and by thy intercession convert me and save me. When the Lord had appeared from thee like a shining cloud, O Virgin, He utterly abolished the idols of Egypt; and He deemed worthy to bear the palm a multitude of those who strove, who imitated Him in enduring His venerable sufferings.
From the Canon for the feast of St. Artemius the martyr, Day 20.
The incorporeal Word, having been incarnate from thee in the manner that befitted God, O most chaste one, through an excess of love for mankind, joined Himself to sufferings


[1217] {#pg.105.1217}
and brought about impassibility for men; for the glorious Lord has been gloriously glorified.
He has been incarnate by His own will from thy blood, O Lady, O spotless one, the Lord, saving humanity; and He drew to Himself the throngs of martyrs.
God, O unpolluted and incorrupt one, preserved thee a virgin after childbirth, He who was well-pleased in thy womb to take upon Himself my whole humanity through extreme goodness.
He who was born of thee by His own will for our sake, O Lady, having for us endured the cross and burial, as a mighty one made Artemius a most steadfast witness of His sufferings.
O Theotokos and Virgin, save thy servants who are tossed by the surge of afflictions and beaten by the uprisings of the billows.
Thou didst give birth in a manner befitting God, O all-blameless Virgin, to Him who caused the spring of immortality to gush forth for the dead; therefore, entreat Him, O pure one, to put to death the passions of our body and to make us worthy of eternal life.
Thou didst recreate us, O all-holy one, who had flowed away by the bitter tasting of the tree and had fallen by sliding, having given birth to the Creator and the subsistent Word, O undefiled one, to whom we cry: "All the works of the Lord, bless the Lord."
Illumine me with the light of thy countenance, O Lord, as I am covered by the darkness of negligence, having to intercede for me, O Word, thy true, most chaste Mother,   together with the splendors of the angels and the glorious Artemius.
From the Canon for the feast of St. Abercius, Bishop of Hierapolis, and the seven holy youths in Ephesus, on the 22nd day.
Eloquent and expert tongues are not able to declare thy conception, which surpasses speech; for thou didst give birth in the flesh to God, O all-holy one, who became like us through goodness.
Having found thee purer, O all-holy one, than all creation, the Pure One dwelt within thee, wishing to dwell…


[1219] {#pg.105.1219}
in the one who had inhabited Adam, to eliminate the iniquity that had dwelt in Adam, as a lover of mankind.

Mortify the wisdom of my flesh, O Virgin, who brought forth Life, who took away death by death, and glorified the young children by a wondrous rising.

Heal my sick soul, O Virgin,   with a healing hand, and wipe away the filth of the passions clinging to me, and set me, made whole, before the tribunal of the Almighty God, that I may sing: All ye works, praise the Lord.
The prophet of old foresaw thee as an enlightening lampstand, O most chaste Virgin, truly bearing within thyself the divine lamp: that is, the only supersubstantial God, who for the sake of the depths of His mercy became man from thee.
Thou bearest in thine arms Him who holds all things by His divine palm; whom supplicate, O Virgin,   that I, who am alone


[1221] {#pg.105.1221}
A condemned, may be received into His arms on account of His ineffable piety, and be saved.
From the Canon for the Holy Martyrs Marcianus and Martyrius, on the 25th day.
Thou who didst conceive the timeless Son of God didst clothe Him with a body, O pure one, He having become man for the sake of His ineffable mercy; wherefore, worshipping Him, we piously glorify thee, the cause of the deification of all.
Thou art adorned with fringes of gold, as a Queen, and now standest at the right hand of the Master and God, O Lady, interceding for thy servants.

Suppliantly we cry to thee, Mother of God, showing your accustomed compassion toward this city and people; deliver us from a most severe earthquake and destruction.

Holy Bride of God,   have mercy now upon thy people who are in despair, and by thy motherly intercessions...


[1223] {#pg.105.1223}
A avert the indignation of God against us, we entreat thee.
Assent, O inviolate one, to the salvation of thy servants who are near to destruction because of the anger of God, and the heavy and horrible fury of the threats now hanging over us, on account of the multitude of our many sins.
Domina endowed with compassion, who gavest birth to the Savior who is supremely compassionate; look upon the affliction and the groaning of thy people, and hasten to intercede, that He may have mercy upon us.
Thou who didst not suffer corruption in childbearing, deliver us all, O Virgin, from all corruption and from the most heavy earthquake and tribulation, appeasing the indignation of the Lord with thy motherly reconciliations, O thou who art most dear to God.
From the Canon to Saint Demetrios, day 26
Pour forth constant prayers to God, O Maiden, that He may have mercy on me, who am ensnared by the many deceptions of this life and am wrapped in the blind night of sin.
Domina, most pleasing to God, thou who didst bring forth the Sun, dissipate and dispel from every side the dark clouds of2 my soul.
Mother and Virgin, who didst give the Word of God a body, deliver me from bodily passions, and heal all the contritions of my soul.
Thou hast been made beautiful, O Virgin,   inasmuch as thou didst give birth to the most beautiful Word; entreat Him with constant prayers, that He may have mercy on the sinful people, and that He may keep safe from every demonic deception the world which hopeth in thee, O Mother of God.
Do not despise the supplication of my miserable soul, O Virgin Mother of God: but by thy kindly intervention make me one who is domestic to God, and save me from the punishments of the future age prepared for me, O most immaculate one.
Having thee, O inviolate Virgin, as a bulwark and a wall, and a harbor, may we be snatched away from harmful temptations and various tribulations by thy prayers, while we praise thee as is thy due.

From the double Canon for the feast of the holy great martyr Anastasia the Roman, and of our holy father Abraham, day 29
We venerate thee as that ladder which reached unto heaven, and on which God rested, making men heavenly, O Maiden.

In thee, O most holy one, the Author of the universe, because of the excess of His compassion, willingly dwelt, and sanctified the substance of men, which had previously slipped into ruin because of the transgression.
After the birth thou didst remain inviolate, O Virgin, just as thou hadst been before the birth; for thou didst bring forth as a new infant Him who is known to have existed before the ages.
Me, who am oppressed by sloth and sunken in sin,


[1225] {#pg.105.1225}
A redeem by thy intercession, O Theotokos, Mother ever-virgin.
We praise thee, O all-praiseworthy Lady Theotokos, who in the flesh didst give birth without seed to God, who is to be praised above all.
Mother-virgin maiden, enlightened by the divine Spirit, O all-pure one, the holy prophets, illuminated by the light of the divine Spirit, proclaimed thee with holy voices—thou from whom God the Word was incarnate beyond cause and beyond speech, out of measureless compassion.
Thou who didst give birth to God who is a lover of mankind, O Lady who lovest the good, entreat Him to deliver me from the fire of Gehenna.
